history: Treasure's Sin and Punishment - Successor of the Earth is a Nintendo 64 rail shooter published in Japan in 2000. Western players got an official English release later, including a 2007 Virtual Console edition.

meta.name: Sin and Punishment - Successor of the Earth

title: Disney's Tigger's Honey Hunt
history: Disney's Tigger's Honey Hunt is a 2000 platformer based on Disney's Winnie the Pooh characters, on Nintendo 64 and PlayStation. Tigger collects honey across levels spun from that franchise.

title: Gauntlet Legends
history: Atari Games' Gauntlet Legends updates the four-hero dungeon crawl as a 3D arcade game in the late 1990s. The Nintendo 64 version ports that sequel, not the 1985 cabinet.

title: South Park Rally
history: Acclaim's South Park Rally is a 1999 kart racer using the Comedy Central cast. It is a separate Nintendo 64 license from the earlier South Park first-person game.

title: Monster Truck Madness 2
history: Microsoft's Monster Truck Madness 2 is a 1998 PC racing sequel with licensed monster trucks and muddy tracks. It belongs to the Windows series that began with the earlier Monster Truck Madness.

title: Mischief Makers
history: A robot girl grabs enemies and shakes them, in a side-scroller from Treasure.
lineup: It is a cult Nintendo 64 action game, not a Nintendo-made platformer.

title: Ogre Battle 64: Person of Lordly Caliber
history: Quest's Ogre Battle 64: Person of Lordly Caliber continues the series on the Nintendo 64, with a 1999 Japanese release. Real-time squad battles remain, wrapped in a larger class story.

meta.name: Ogre Battle 64: Person of Lordly Caliber

title: Killer Instinct Gold
history: Rare's Killer Instinct Gold is the 1996 Nintendo 64 version of Killer Instinct 2, training mode included. It covers the sequel, not the earlier Super Nintendo Killer Instinct cart.

title: Tonic Trouble
history: Ubisoft's Tonic Trouble is a 3D platformer about a clumsy alien who spills a magic drink on Earth, from the Rayman team. It drew much harsher reviews than Rayman 2.

title: Bomberman Hero (1998)
history: Hudson's Bomberman Hero (1998) turns the bomber into a Nintendo 64 platform-game hero instead of locking him to maze battles. It is a spinoff, not a numbered Super Bomberman port.

title: Quest 64
history: Imagineer's Quest 64 is a 1998 Nintendo 64 RPG published by THQ in the US and as Holy Magic Century in Europe. It is one of the few RPGs on that console, and a divisive one, with a lone hero and no traditional party.

title: Ready 2 Rumble Boxing
history: Midway's Ready 2 Rumble Boxing is a 1999 cartoon boxing game built around exaggerated fighters such as Afro Thunder. Nintendo 64 and Game Boy Color versions followed the arcade-style original.

title: Snowboard Kids
history: Atlus's Snowboard Kids is a 1998 Nintendo 64 downhill racer that mixes courses with item attacks. It plays more like a cartoon kart race than a simulation of the sport.

title: Hydro Thunder (1999)
history: Midway's Hydro Thunder (1999) is an arcade powerboat racer full of jumps and boost starts. The Nintendo 64 version is a home port of that cabinet, not an original Nintendo water game.

title: Army Men: Air Attack (1999)
history: 3DO's Army Men: Air Attack (1999) puts plastic-green helicopters over backyard battlefields. It is a spinoff of the Army Men toy-soldier series, and the Nintendo 64 edition is one home port.

title: Duke Nukem: Zero Hour
history: Eurocom's Duke Nukem: Zero Hour is a 1999 Nintendo 64 third-person shooter with a time-travel plot, published by GT Interactive. It is not Duke Nukem 64, the port of Duke Nukem 3D.

title: Ready 2 Rumble Boxing: Round 2
history: Midway's Ready 2 Rumble Boxing: Round 2 is the 2000 sequel, with a larger roster and the same exaggerated boxing. The Nintendo 64 version continues those cartoon bouts.

title: Excitebike 64 (2000)
history: Left Field Productions' Excitebike 64 (2000), published by Nintendo, is a 3D dirt-bike follow-up in spirit to the NES Excitebike. A track editor and stunt racing keep it from being a simple remake.

title: Turok 3: Shadow of Oblivion
history: Acclaim's Turok 3: Shadow of Oblivion closes the Nintendo 64 trilogy in 2000, with Danielle and Joseph as the hunters. It follows Seeds of Evil rather than restarting the comic license.

title: Extreme-G
history: Probe's Extreme-G, published by Acclaim in 1997, is a futuristic Nintendo 64 motorcycle racer with weapons mounted on the bikes. Sequels on the same console followed it.

title: Bomberman 64: The Second Attack
history: Hudson's Bomberman 64: The Second Attack is the 2000 Nintendo 64 sequel, known in Japan as a numbered follow-up to Bomberman 64. Adventure stages share space with the series' bombs.

title: Goemon's Great Adventure
history: Konami's Goemon's Great Adventure is the 1998 Nintendo 64 follow-up to Mystical Ninja, known in Japan as a Ganbare Goemon sequel. It shifts to a side-on view and keeps the series' jokes.

title: Battlezone (1998)
history: Activision's Battlezone (1998) reworks the Atari name into a PC game that mixes tank combat with base building. The Nintendo 64 release is a later, less famous port of that remake.

title: Rugrats in Paris: The Movie
history: Rugrats in Paris: The Movie is a 2000 licensed game based on the Nickelodeon film, with a Nintendo 64 version among the tie-ins. It uses the movie's Paris trip rather than an earlier Rugrats game-show setting.

title: Animaniacs
history: Konami's Animaniacs turns the Warner Bros. cartoon into a 1994 platformer on Super Nintendo and Game Boy. Yakko, Wakko, and Dot share the license, and the two cartridges are not the same game.

title: Breath of Fire II (1994)
history: Capcom's Breath of Fire II (1994) is the Super Famicom sequel remembered for building a township between quests. It continues the dragon-transformation line started by the first game.

title: Trials of Mana
history: Square's Trials of Mana began as Seiken Densetsu 3 on the Super Famicom in 1995, and you choose three heroes from six. It had no official English release until the much later remake that uses this title.

title: Goof Troop
history: Capcom's Goof Troop is a 1993 Super Nintendo cooperative game based on the Disney series, starring Goofy and Max. Two players solve rooms together; it is closer to a puzzle adventure than a cartoon brawler.

title: Live A Live
history: Square's Live A Live, directed by Takashi Tokita, is a 1994 Super Famicom RPG told as separate chapters across wildly different eras. An official English script waited until the HD-2D remake decades later.

title: Castlevania: Dracula X
history: Konami's Castlevania: Dracula X is the 1995 Super Nintendo game, a different and more limited project than the PC Engine's Rondo of Blood. Richter still faces Dracula, but the stages are not the CD game's.

title: Columns (1990)
history: Sega's Columns (1990) matches jewels dropped in sets of three, a puzzle associated with the Genesis as a rival to falling blocks. It began as a computer and arcade design, not as a Super Nintendo original.

title: Final Fight 2
history: Capcom's Final Fight 2 is a 1993 Super Nintendo sequel that never had an arcade cabinet. Haggar returns with new partners, Maki and Carlos, in Metro City.

title: Ultima VII: The Black Gate
history: Origin's Ultima VII: The Black Gate, from 1992, is Richard Garriott's sprawling mouse-driven chapter of Britannia on PC. A Super Nintendo game using the subtitle is a separate, much simpler adaptation.

title: Super Bomberman
history: Hudson's Super Bomberman brought four-player maze battles to the Super Nintendo in 1993 through the multitap. That cart is what made Bomberman a 16-bit party fixture.

title: FIFA 97
history: EA Sports' FIFA 97 is the soccer annual aimed at the 1996 season, still using an isometric pitch on the Super Nintendo. It continues the FIFA line rather than Konami's International Superstar Soccer.

title: Toy Story (1995)
history: Traveller's Tales' Toy Story (1995) is the Super Nintendo and Genesis platformer of the Pixar film, with Woody crossing rendered stages. The Game Boy cart is a separate, smaller tie-in.

title: Captain Commando
history: Capcom's Captain Commando is a 1991 arcade brawler about a future hero and three odd partners, one of them a baby in a mech. The Super Nintendo version is a port of that coin-op.

title: Final Fight 3
history: Capcom's Final Fight 3 is the 1995 Super Nintendo continuation, adding a super-move gauge and new allies in Metro City. Like Final Fight 2, it has no matching arcade cabinet.

title: Top Gear 2
history: Top Gear 2 is the 1993 Super Nintendo racing sequel, adding weapons and a longer season to the first game's split-screen driving. Kemco published the series, known in Japan under the Top Racer name.

title: NBA Jam (1994)
history: Midway's NBA Jam (1994), developed with Mark Turmell, is the two-on-two basketball game famous for dunks and the announcer yelling that he's on fire. Arcades led, and it became a major home hit in 1993.

title: Doom Troopers: Mutant Chronicles
history: Doom Troopers: Mutant Chronicles is a 1995 run-and-gun based on the Mutant Chronicles science-fiction setting. The similar first word does not make it id Software's DOOM.

title: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers
history: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers licenses the Saban television series. The 1994 Super Nintendo version is a one-on-one fighter, while the Game Boy release is another, smaller tie-in.

title: The Adventures of Batman and Robin
history: Konami's The Adventures of Batman and Robin is a 1994 Super Nintendo game based on the animated series, mixing platform stages with Batmobile runs. It is separate from Sunsoft's NES Batman carts.

meta.name: The Adventures of Batman and Robin

title: Battletoads in Battlemaniacs
history: Rare's Battletoads in Battlemaniacs is the 1994 Super Nintendo Battletoads game, still known for severe difficulty spikes. It is neither the NES original nor the Double Dragon crossover.

title: Final Fantasy Mystic Quest (1992)
history: Square's Final Fantasy Mystic Quest (1992) is a simplified RPG aimed at North America, released in Japan as Final Fantasy USA: Mystic Quest. It is not numbered among the main Final Fantasy games.

title: Maui Mallard in Cold Shadow
history: Disney's Maui Mallard in Cold Shadow casts Donald Duck as a hard-boiled detective in a 1996 platformer. Super Nintendo and Genesis versions exist, and some US packaging leads with Donald's name.

title: Demolition Man
history: Demolition Man is a 1994 Super Nintendo action game based on the Sylvester Stallone film. Corridor gunfights mix with brawling, and it is a movie license rather than a Midway arcade port.

title: Super Street Fighter II: The New Challengers
history: Capcom's Super Street Fighter II: The New Challengers adds Cammy, Dee Jay, T. Hawk, and Fei Long in 1993. The Super Nintendo version brought those four newcomers home.

meta.name: Super Street Fighter II: The New Challengers

title: Wing Commander
history: Chris Roberts's Wing Commander, from Origin in 1990, mixes cockpit missions with a branching story between flights. The Super Nintendo port is a later, simplified adaptation of the PC game.

title: The Simpsons: Bart's Nightmare
history: Acclaim's The Simpsons: Bart's Nightmare sends a sleeping Bart through sketch-like Super Nintendo stages in 1992. It does not continue the plot of the NES Space Mutants cartridge.

title: International Superstar Soccer Deluxe
history: Konami's International Superstar Soccer Deluxe is the 1995 Super Nintendo update, with more teams and refined matches. It builds on the first ISS game rather than on EA's FIFA.

title: BattleTech: A Game of Armored Combat
history: BattleTech: A Game of Armored Combat is the Super Nintendo name used for MechWarrior 3050, an isometric BattleMech game published by Activision. You pilot a Mad Cat in FASA's BattleTech setting.

meta.name: BattleTech: A Game of Armored Combat

title: Asterix & Obelix
history: Asterix & Obelix licenses the French comic about the Gaulish village that resists Rome. The 1995 Super Nintendo and Game Boy games are tie-ins to that bande dessinee, not an American cartoon.

title: Secret of Evermore
history: Square's Redmond studio developed Secret of Evermore in 1995, an action RPG that was not designed in Japan and was not released there. A boy travels with a dog that changes shape, in the manner of Secret of Mana.

title: X-Men: Mutant Apocalypse
history: Capcom's X-Men: Mutant Apocalypse is a 1995 Super Nintendo brawler starring the Marvel team. It is side-view action, not the later arcade fighter X-Men: Children of the Atom.

title: Sim City
history: Nintendo's Super Nintendo Sim City adds an advisor named Dr. Wright and lets Bowser strike as a disaster. It is a special edition of Will Wright's city builder, not the plainer NES port.

title: Top Gear
history: Kemco's Top Gear is a 1992 Super Nintendo split-screen racer, known in Japan as Top Racer. A password saves your place in a country-by-country season.

title: ActRaiser (1990)
history: Quintet's ActRaiser (1990), published by Enix, alternates side-view battles with a god's-eye mode where you grow a civilization. It is a Super Nintendo original from that Enix-associated studio.

title: Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals
history: Neverland's Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals, published by Taito, is the 1995 Super Famicom prequel known for intricate puzzle rooms. The US release kept those dungeon puzzles as a main draw.

meta.name: Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals

title: Prehistorik 2
history: Titus's Prehistorik 2 is a European caveman platformer brought to the Super Nintendo and Game Boy. The 1993 sequel stars a club-wielding hero of that series, not Data East's Joe & Mac.

title: Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame
history: Jordan Mechner's Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame is the 1993 DOS sequel, with new palace intrigue and the same careful swordplay. A Super Nintendo port exists, but the PC game is the original.

meta.name: Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame

title: Romancing SaGa 2
history: Square's Romancing SaGa 2, led by Akitoshi Kawazu, is a 1993 Super Famicom RPG about an empire passed down across generations. It did not receive a contemporary English release.

title: Spider-Man and Venom: Maximum Carnage
history: LJN's Spider-Man and Venom: Maximum Carnage adapts the comic crossover as a 1994 beat 'em up on Super Nintendo and Genesis. A red cartridge and the symbiote team-up are its public hooks.

title: Mega Man X3 (1995)
history: Capcom's Mega Man X3 (1995) continues the Super Nintendo X series under Dr. Doppler, and some versions let you play as Zero. It is the third X game, still a 16-bit run before later disc ports.

title: Umihara Kawase
history: Umihara Kawase is a 1994 Super Famicom platformer whose stretchy fishing line is used to swing, grab, and climb. The first edition stayed in Japan and later picked up a cult following.

title: Clock Tower (1995)
history: Human Entertainment's Clock Tower (1995), directed by Hifumi Kono, is a Super Famicom point-and-click horror game starring Jennifer and the Scissorman. It is a suspense adventure, not an action castle crawl.

title: Cool Spot
history: Virgin's Cool Spot stars the 7 Up mascot in a 1993 platformer on Genesis and Super Nintendo. The red dot hops through bright levels that began as a soda mascot.

title: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together
history: Quest's Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together, directed by Yasumi Matsuno, is the 1995 Super Famicom tactical RPG. Battles sit on a grid, which sets it apart from the real-time Ogre Battle.

meta.name: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together

title: Judge Dredd
history: Judge Dredd licenses the 2000 AD comic character for action games timed with the Stallone film in 1995. Super Nintendo and Game Boy carts share the name as movie-era tie-ins.

title: Final Fight
history: Capcom's Final Fight is the 1989 arcade brawler in which Haggar, Cody, and Guy try to clean up Metro City. The first Super Nintendo port dropped two-player play and, at first, Guy.

title: Terranigma
history: A callow hero leaves an underworld village and has to rebuild the surface world.
lineup: It is the last of Quintet's SNES action RPGs, released in Europe and Japan but not North America.

title: Killer Instinct (1994)
history: Rare's Killer Instinct (1994) is the arcade fighter Nintendo promoted with combo breakers and a rock soundtrack. The Super Nintendo port is a reduced home version; Killer Instinct Gold later covered the sequel.

title: Mega Man 7 (1995)
history: Capcom's Mega Man 7 (1995) moves the classic blue hero to the Super Nintendo and introduces Bass as a rival. It continues the NES story rather than the separate Mega Man X timeline.

title: Urban Strike
history: Electronic Arts' Urban Strike is the 1994 sequel that brings the Strike helicopter series into a city campaign. It followed Jungle Strike and still uses that series' mission map.

title: Civilization
history: The Super Nintendo Civilization is a console port of Sid Meier's turn-based history game from MicroProse. You still chase technologies toward space, one more turn at a time, on a smaller home map.

title: Frogger (1981)
history: Konami's Frogger (1981) hops a frog through traffic and across a river, one of the simple arcade ideas that became universal. Super Nintendo and Game Boy releases are much later ports.

title: Breath of Fire (1993)
history: Capcom's Breath of Fire (1993) is the first RPG in that line, a Super Famicom quest whose hero can take dragon form. A Game Boy Advance reissue is how many English-speaking players later met it.

title: Shin Megami Tensei
history: Atlus's Shin Megami Tensei is the 1992 Super Famicom RPG of a demon-haunted Tokyo, descended from the Megami Tensei books and Famicom games. Alignment choices shape a bleak modern apocalypse.

title: Pitfall: The Mayan Adventure
history: Activision's Pitfall: The Mayan Adventure is the 16-bit sequel to David Crane's Atari 2600 Pitfall, using pre-rendered jungle animation. It debuted on Genesis and Super Nintendo in the mid-1990s, not on the 2600.

title: DRAGON QUEST V
history: Enix's DRAGON QUEST V, a 1992 Super Famicom RPG, is famous for marriage, a playable generation, and recruiting monsters. It had no official English release until the Nintendo DS remake.

title: Romancing SaGa 3
history: Square's Romancing SaGa 3 is Akitoshi Kawazu's 1995 Super Famicom RPG, the last of the Romancing SaGa trilogy on that console. Like its predecessors, it waited many years for an official English edition.

title: Harvest Moon
history: A short farming life: crops, livestock, and town relationships on a clock.
lineup: It is the SNES original of the farming series later handhelds carried for years.

title: Super Punch-Out!!
history: A taller, faster boxing career than the NES game, still built on learning each boxer's tell.
lineup: It is the SNES Punch-Out!!, not the NES original and not the later Wii game.

title: Tales of Phantasia
history: Namco and Wolf Team's Tales of Phantasia is the 1995 Super Famicom game that started the Tales series. Real-time battles and a short voice track were notable on that hardware.

title: Syndicate (1993)
history: Bullfrog's Syndicate (1993) puts you in charge of a four-agent team moving through isometric cities, researching gear as you go. Corporate conquest of the world map is the computer original's signature.

title: Micro Machines 2: Turbo Tournament
history: Codemasters' Micro Machines 2: Turbo Tournament continues the toy-car races in 1994, and the Genesis J-Cart lets four people play without an extra adapter. The Super Nintendo version is a separate port of that sequel.

title: Kirby's Dream Land 3 (1997)
history: HAL's Kirby's Dream Land 3 (1997) is the Super Nintendo Kirby game with animal friends and a soft pastel look. It is the last Kirby released for that console generation.

title: Blackthorne
history: Blizzard's Blackthorne, from 1994, is a cinematic platformer also known as Blackhawk, shotgun and long cape included. It launched on the Super Nintendo before later machines, including a Game Boy Advance port.

title: Primal Rage
history: Atari Games' Primal Rage is a 1995 arcade fighter of stop-motion dinosaurs and giant apes. Home ports, the Super Nintendo one included, carry that prehistoric roster.

title: Illusion of Gaia
history: A boy crosses ancient sites in an action RPG that changes form for combat.
lineup: It is the middle game of Quintet's loose SNES trilogy with Soul Blazer and Terranigma.

title: Tom & Jerry
history: The Super Nintendo Tom & Jerry is a 1993 cartoon platformer, a different production from the NES game subtitled The Ultimate Game of Cat and Mouse. The chase itself is the whole license.

title: Kirby's Dream Course (1994)
history: HAL's Kirby's Dream Course (1994) plays like miniature golf, knocking Kirby into enemies to lower the stroke count. Japan first called the Super Nintendo game Kirby Bowl.

title: KING OF THE MONSTERS
history: SNK's KING OF THE MONSTERS is a 1991 Neo Geo grappling game between giant kaiju in cities you can smash. The Super Nintendo version ports that monster-versus-monster coin-op.

title: Demon's Crest (1994)
history: Capcom's Demon's Crest (1994) stars the gargoyle Firebrand in a Super Nintendo action game spun out of Gargoyle's Quest. Elemental crests change how he crosses the gothic stages.

title: Grand Theft Auto
history: DMA Design's Grand Theft Auto, from 1997, is the open-city crime game that started on PC. The Game Boy Color cartridge is a later, much smaller adaptation, not those original cities.

title: Pokemon Red
history: A trainer leaves a small town, fills a party, and aims at a league of gym leaders.
lineup: This page is Pokemon Red, the 1996 Game Boy game. Blue and Yellow are separate entries. A later remake pair, FireRed and LeafGreen, is on Game Boy Advance.

title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
history: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone is the US title for several different 2001 licenses of the first book and film. Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance, and home-console editions were made separately and do not play the same.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone

title: Pokemon Gold
history: A western region, a day-night clock, and two new starter lines follow the first league.
lineup: Gold is one half of the 1999 pair. Crystal revisits the same journey and has its own page. HeartGold on DS is a later remake.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening (1993)
history: Link washes up on Koholint Island, which is not Hyrule, and tries to wake the Wind Fish.
lineup: This page is the 1993 Game Boy game, including the later color DX edition as the same adventure. The 2019 Switch remake has its own page.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening (1993)

title: Super Mario Land
history: A pocket platformer with its own enemies, vehicles, and ending, not a shrunken Super Mario Bros.
lineup: It is Mario's first Game Boy outing and the start of the Land line.

title: Super Mario Land 2: 6 Golden Coins
history: Mario reclaims his castle from Wario across six coins hidden in themed zones.
lineup: It introduces Wario and is the second Game Boy Mario Land, bigger than the first.

title: Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3
history: Wario hunts treasure with a shoulder charge, and the ending changes with how greedy you were.
lineup: It is the first Wario Land, still numbered as a Mario Land game, on Game Boy.

title: Bubble Ghost
history: Bubble Ghost is a late-1980s computer puzzle about puffing a bubble through a room of candles and fans. The Game Boy cartridge is a later port of that ghostly blower.

title: Kirby's Dream Land
history: There is no copy ability yet. Kirby inhales, spits, and floats across five short lands.
lineup: It is Kirby's first game, the Game Boy original before Adventure added copy powers.

title: Colin McRae Rally (1998)
history: Codemasters' Colin McRae Rally (1998) is a stage-based rally game built around the real Scottish driver. The PlayStation original is the known version; a Game Boy edition is a separate, smaller port.

title: Hugo (1991)
history: Hugo (1991) stars the troll from ITE's interactive television quizzes, a character Scandinavian kids played through their TV remotes. Later cartridges, including a Game Boy one, turned those show tasks into a handheld product.

title: Metroid II: Return of Samus
history: Samus hunts metroids down a vertical nest, with a save that was new for the series.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Metroid. Samus Returns on 3DS and later games revisit this mission.

title: Disney•Pixar A Bug's Life
history: Disney•Pixar A Bug's Life licenses the 1998 Pixar film. The Nintendo 64 platformer and the Game Boy versions are different games that share the movie's insects.

title: Kirby's Dream Land 2 (1995)
history: HAL's Kirby's Dream Land 2 (1995) is the Game Boy sequel that pairs Kirby with animal friends, including a hamster, an owl, and a fish. It sits between the first Game Boy Kirby and the Super Nintendo Dream Land 3.

title: Asteroids (1979)
history: Atari's Asteroids (1979), by Lyle Rains and Ed Logg, is the vector-arcade game of a ship turning and thrusting among rocks. Later handheld versions are ports; the cabinet is the original.

title: Pokémon Yellow Version: Special Pikachu Edition
history: Game Freak's Pokémon Yellow Version: Special Pikachu Edition, released in Japan in 1998, keeps Pikachu at your side and follows the anime more closely than Red and Green. It is a special edition of the first generation, not a new region.

meta.name: Pokémon Yellow Version: Special Pikachu Edition

title: Missile Command
history: Dave Theurer's Missile Command is Atari's 1980 arcade game of defending cities from falling warheads. The trackball cabinet is the famous version; a Game Boy release years later does not make it a handheld original.

title: Wario Land II
history: Treasure and multiple endings matter more than a life counter.
lineup: It straddles Game Boy and Game Boy Color. This catalog files the color-era release with the handheld's second generation of Wario.

title: Disney's Pocahontas
history: Disney's Pocahontas is a Game Boy tie-in to Disney's animated film, one of several licensed Pocahontas games from the mid-1990s. It is not a major 16-bit platformer on the scale of Aladdin or The Lion King.

title: Road Rash (1991)
history: Electronic Arts' Road Rash (1991) is the Genesis motorcycle racer where you punch other riders and dodge the police. That 16-bit game is the series identity; Game Boy versions are later, smaller offshoots.

title: The King of Fighters '96
history: SNK's The King of Fighters '96 is the Neo Geo team tournament that changes bosses and lineups after the previous year's entry. A Game Boy port exists, but the arcade version is the real annual release.

title: Breakout (1976)
history: Atari's Breakout (1976) clears a brick wall with a ball and paddle, and Steve Wozniak's prototype for the company is part of its origin story. Any Game Boy edition is a distant port of that arcade idea.

title: The King of Fighters '95
history: SNK's The King of Fighters '95 is the team-based sequel to the first King of Fighters on Neo Geo. The Game Boy version is a reduced portable conversion of that 1995 arcade game.

title: Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge
history: Konami's Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge is the 1991 Game Boy sequel to Castlevania: The Adventure. Christopher Belmont climbs four castles; it is not a portable copy of Simon's Quest.

title: Castlevania: The Adventure (1989)
history: Konami's first handheld Castlevania, Castlevania: The Adventure (1989), is a stiff whip-platform trek that longtime fans still rank as the series' roughest start.

title: Final Fantasy Adventure
history: Before the Mana series carried that name, Final Fantasy Adventure was Square's 1991 Game Boy action RPG, released in Japan as Seiken Densetsu.

title: Missile Command (1980)
history: Dave Theurer's arcade classic Missile Command (1980) makes you shield cities from falling warheads with a limited stock of interceptors. Atari's trackball cabinet is the game that name means.

title: R-Type (1987)
history: Irem's side-scroller R-Type (1987) is remembered for the Force, a detachable pod that both shields the ship and powers its shot. The arcade cabinet came first; home versions followed.

title: Centipede (1981)
history: Ed Logg and Dona Bailey designed Atari's Centipede (1981), a trackball shooter set in a mushroom patch where the insect splits as you hit it.

title: Battlezone (1980)
history: Ed Rotberg's first-person tank duel Battlezone (1980) drew wireframe enemies on a vector screen. Atari's cabinet was notable enough that the U.S. Army asked about a training variant.

title: F-1 Race
history: HAL Laboratory built F-1 Race for Nintendo's Famicom in 1984, and it was among the first games to use the console's expansion port for a steering wheel.

title: New Ghostbusters II
history: HAL Laboratory's New Ghostbusters II is a 1990 license of the film sequel, issued on the NES in Europe and on Game Boy. North America did not receive this cartridge under that title.

title: Donkey Kong Land
history: Rare's Donkey Kong Land is a 1995 Game Boy companion to Donkey Kong Country, with its own stages squeezed out of pre-rendered artwork. It is a separate trek from the Super Nintendo game.

title: BurgerTime (1982)
history: Data East's BurgerTime (1982) stars chef Peter Pepper, who walks across ingredients to stack burgers while kitchen pests chase him across the ladders.

title: Snow Bros. Jr
history: Toaplan's snowball arcade game reached the Game Boy as Snow Bros. Jr. You roll foes into giant snowballs and kick them, a 1990 cabinet idea cut down for a cartridge.

title: Boulder Dash (1984)
history: Peter Liepa's cave puzzle Boulder Dash (1984) has you dig for diamonds while loose boulders tumble. First Star's original spawned a long line of home ports.

title: Real Bout Fatal Fury Special
history: SNK's Real Bout Fatal Fury Special is a 1997 Neo Geo revision in the Fatal Fury line, tuned as an arcade fighter with the series' plane-switching scraps.

title: Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi
history: Sculptured Software and LucasArts closed the 16-bit trilogy with Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi, a 1994 Super Nintendo run that includes speeder and Falcon stages.

meta.name: Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Fall of the Foot Clan
history: Konami's Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Fall of the Foot Clan is the turtles' 1990 Game Boy debut, a short side-scroller about reaching April. The handheld follow-up is Back from the Sewers.

meta.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Fall of the Foot Clan

title: True Lies
history: True Lies is an action license of James Cameron's 1994 spy film. Home editions, Game Boy among them, each adapt the movie on their own terms.

title: Lemmings 2: The Tribes
history: DMA Design's sequel Lemmings 2: The Tribes splits the marchers into tribes with different skills. The 1993 puzzle still asks you to save a set quota of them.

title: The Lost World: Jurassic Park
history: Several unrelated 1997 products share the name The Lost World: Jurassic Park, from a Sega light-gun arcade cabinet to separate home adaptations of Spielberg's sequel.

title: Tetris Attack
history: Nintendo sold Panel de Pon in the West as Tetris Attack, a rising-stack match puzzle restyled around Yoshi. Despite the name, tetrominoes never fall.

title: Casper
history: The friendly-ghost film spawned Casper, with separate Game Boy and Game Boy Color cartridges in the years after the movie. They are licensed adaptations, not one shared quest.

title: Bonk's Adventure (1989)
history: Hudson Soft's PC Engine mascot, also called PC Genjin, debuts in Bonk's Adventure (1989). A Game Boy port came after the TurboGrafx-16 original.

title: Double Dribble (1987)
history: Konami's basketball game Double Dribble (1987) cuts to a close-up dunk when a shot drops. That spectacle, on the arcade cabinet and the NES, became the signature.

title: Battle Arena Toshinden
history: Tamsoft's weapons fighter Battle Arena Toshinden arrived with the early PlayStation in 1995, published by Takara. Blade duels in 3D, not a handheld scuffle, are what the name refers to.

title: Zen: Intergalactic Ninja
history: Konami published Zen: Intergalactic Ninja on Game Boy in 1993, a side-scroller drawn from the small-press comic about an alien warrior.

title: Gargoyle's Quest (1990)
history: Capcom's Gargoyle's Quest (1990) stars Firebrand, the red demon from Ghosts 'n Goblins, on a Game Boy map of side-view fights. It is a spinoff, not a Belmont story.

title: Pinocchio (1996)
history: Disney's animated film about the puppet became the license for Pinocchio (1996). Home versions, Game Boy included, each retell that story in their own way.

title: Zool
history: Gremlin Graphics pitched Zool as a 1992 Amiga mascot, a ninja from the Nth dimension racing through themed worlds. Console and Game Boy ports followed.

title: Bionic Commando (1987)
history: Capcom's arcade original Bionic Commando (1987) introduced the grappling-arm commando that the NES game, where he cannot jump, made famous. A later handheld cartridge reused the name for a different release.

title: Star Wars (1983)
history: Atari's vector cabinet Star Wars (1983) seats you in an X-wing for the Death Star trench. It is a film-based arcade game, built years before the side-scrolling home licenses.

title: Chuck Rock
history: Core Design's caveman Chuck Rock belly-slams through a 1991 Amiga platformer. Console ports, and a Game Boy version, carried the same prehistoric joke.

title: FIFA (1993)
history: EA's first game in the long soccer line, known in full as FIFA International Soccer, is the release filed as FIFA (1993). Its isometric pitch defined early 16-bit FIFA.

title: Donald in Maui Mallard
history: Europe's name for Disney's 1995 platformer is Donald in Maui Mallard. North America called the console versions Maui Mallard in Cold Shadow, with Donald as a shirt-wearing detective.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: Back from the Sewers
history: Konami followed Fall of the Foot Clan with Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: Back from the Sewers, a 1991 Game Boy side-scroller that sends the turtles back through the sewers.

meta.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: Back from the Sewers

title: Xenon 2: Megablast
history: The Bitmap Brothers followed Xenon with Xenon 2: Megablast, a vertical shooter whose soundtrack came from Bomb the Bass. The Amiga original was ported widely, Game Boy included.

title: Mega Man: Dr. Wily's Revenge
history: Capcom's first Game Boy Mega Man, Mega Man: Dr. Wily's Revenge, remixes robot masters from the first two NES games. The 1991 cartridge is its own adventure.

title: Gauntlet II
history: Atari Games' 1986 arcade sequel Gauntlet II adds the cursed food called It, plus new classes, to the four-player dungeon crawl.

title: Krusty's Fun House
history: Audiogenic designed Krusty's Fun House for Acclaim in 1992: herd rats into a machine inside the clown's fun house. The Simpsons puzzle shipped on NES, Super Nintendo, Genesis, and Game Boy.

title: Castlevania Legends
history: Konami's 1997 Game Boy game Castlevania Legends stars Sonia Belmont. Koji Igarashi later placed this story outside the series timeline he treated as official.

title: Klax
history: Dave Akers designed Klax for Atari Games in 1989: catch colored tiles from a conveyor and stack them into scoring lines. Ports reached almost every home format of the period.

title: James Pond 2: Codename Robocod
history: Millennium's fish agent stretches through a toy factory in James Pond 2: Codename Robocod, wearing a robotic suit. It is the sequel to James Pond and a staple of Amiga and console play.

title: Gremlins 2: The New Batch
history: Sunsoft's license of Joe Dante's film sequel is Gremlins 2: The New Batch, with separate NES and Game Boy cartridges from 1990. The two versions do not play alike.

title: Super Dodge Ball (1988)
history: Technos turned its Kunio arcade dodgeball into Super Dodge Ball (1988), a cult NES sports game full of super throws. The Famicom original sits in the same late-1980s window as the year on this name.

title: Dragon Warrior Monsters
history: Enix's 1998 Game Boy spinoff Dragon Quest Monsters reached the West as Dragon Warrior Monsters. Breeding and battling creatures is the loop, a pocket cousin of the main series.

title: Donkey Kong
history: The familiar girders are only the first four stages. After that it becomes a puzzle platformer with flips and handstands.
lineup: It is the 1994 Game Boy Donkey Kong, not the 1981 arcade game and not Country.

title: The Blues Brothers
history: Titus built The Blues Brothers in 1991 as a platformer about the Belushi and Aykroyd revue. Computer, console, and Game Boy editions share the license.

title: Mario's Picross
history: Jupiter and Nintendo's Mario's Picross is a 1995 Game Boy logic book: fill grids from number clues while Mario hosts. Japan and Europe got it; North America waited on later reissues.

title: Bubsy 2
history: Accolade's sequel Bubsy 2 put the bobcat back on Super Nintendo and Genesis in 1994. Larger stages and the same talkative mascot define that follow-up.

title: Yoshi's Cookie
history: Bullet-Proof Software, Nintendo's Tetris partner, co-made Yoshi's Cookie in 1992. Matching cookies in rows on Game Boy and NES clears the board.

title: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie (BG)
history: Bandai's Game Boy tie-in to the Rangers feature is titled Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie (BG). The 1995 movie license is a side-scroller of its own, apart from the TV-season cartridges.

meta.name: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie (BG)

title: Super Off Road
history: Leland's 1989 arcade racer Super Off Road puts three trucks on an overhead dirt oval under Ivan Stewart's name. A Game Boy port was among the many home versions.

title: Toxic Crusaders
history: The Troma cartoon spun from The Toxic Avenger licensed Toxic Crusaders in 1992. Bandai's Game Boy cartridge stars those mop-wielding heroes.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man (1990)
history: Rare built LJN's Game Boy release The Amazing Spider-Man (1990) as a side-scroller of wall climbs and street fights. It is the first handheld Spider-Man, separate from the later Super Nintendo and PlayStation games.

title: Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters
history: Nintendo and Tose made Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters for Game Boy in 1991, a sequel to the NES angel-archer. It came out in North America and Europe, and skipped Japan at the time.

meta.name: Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters

title: Final Fantasy Legend II
history: Square's second SaGa game, released in Japan in 1990, is Final Fantasy Legend II in the West. The Game Boy cartridge keeps the mutant, human, and monster party of that line.

title: Turrican
history: Manfred Trenz's run-and-gun Turrican debuted in 1990 on the Commodore 64 and Amiga, famous for a transforming wheel. A Game Boy port followed the computer original.

title: The Battle of Olympus
history: Infinity's NES action game The Battle of Olympus, published by Broderbund in 1988, sends a Greek hero through side-view fights often compared with Zelda II. A Game Boy port later appeared in Europe.

title: Gargoyle's Quest II
history: Capcom moved Firebrand to the NES for Gargoyle's Quest II in 1992, a larger follow-up to the Game Boy original. Japan knew it as Red Arremer II.

title: Speedball 2: Brutal Deluxe
history: The Bitmap Brothers' future sport Speedball 2: Brutal Deluxe is the 1990 Amiga sequel to Speedball, a violent handball match in armor. Ports spread it far beyond that computer.

title: Ultima (Old)
history: Richard Garriott's first Britannia role-playing game is what Ultima (Old) points at: the 1981 Apple II original that opened the series.

title: Mega Man II(3Ds/GB)
history: Capcom's second Game Boy Mega Man is labeled Mega Man II(3Ds/GB). The 1991 cartridge continues the handheld remix line rather than porting one NES number straight across.

title: Tintin in Tibet
history: Infogrames' Tintin in Tibet is a 1995 platformer based on the Herge album. Super Nintendo, Game Boy, and other versions retell that mountain rescue.

title: Street Racer
history: Vivid Image's Street Racer is a 1994 cartoon kart racer on Super Nintendo and Genesis, built to sit beside Mario Kart. Ubisoft published it.

title: MTV's Beavis and Butt-Head
history: The MTV cartoon licensed MTV's Beavis and Butt-Head in 1994, one of several console and handheld versions sold that year. Couch gags and the duo's faces are the hook.

title: Donkey Kong Land 2
history: Rare's Donkey Kong Land 2 is the 1996 Game Boy companion to Donkey Kong Country 2, with Diddy and Dixie on a new handheld map. It is not a compressed port of the Super Nintendo game.

title: Mr. Nutz
history: Ocean's squirrel platformer Mr. Nutz started on Amiga and Super Nintendo around 1994. A Game Boy version carried the same acorn-hoarding hero.

title: The Final Fantasy Legend
history: Square's first SaGa game reached the West as The Final Fantasy Legend, a 1989 Game Boy cartridge. Japan called it Makai Toushi SaGa, and the Final Fantasy label was a Western branding.

title: Who Framed Roger Rabbit
history: The 1988 Touchstone film that mixes cartoons with live action licensed Who Framed Roger Rabbit. Home versions, including a Game Boy game from Capcom in some regions, adapt that case.

title: Kid Dracula
history: Konami's comic parody of Castlevania reached Game Boy in the West as Kid Dracula in 1993. The Famicom original, Akumajo Special: Boku Dracula-kun, came first.

title: Asterix (1993)
history: The Goscinny and Uderzo comics licensed Asterix (1993), one of Infogrames' many Gaulish platformers. The year baked into the name marks that particular release.

title: Mega Man III
history: Capcom's third Game Boy Mega Man, Mega Man III, arrived in 1992 and folds in bosses associated with the NES Mega Man 3 and 4. It remains a handheld remix.

title: Pokémon Puzzle Challenge
history: Intelligent Systems recast Panel de Pon with pocket monsters for Pokémon Puzzle Challenge, a 2000 Game Boy Color stack-matcher. Japan sold it as Pokemon de Panepon.

title: FIFA: Road to World Cup 98
history: EA Sports' FIFA: Road to World Cup 98 is the 1997 soccer annual aimed at the upcoming World Cup. Nintendo 64 and Game Boy were among the many versions.

title: Bomb Jack
history: Tehkan's 1984 arcade platformer Bomb Jack scores you for collecting bombs in the right order before they go off. Home computers of the era picked it up quickly.

title: Kirby's Pinball Land (1993)
history: HAL Laboratory's Game Boy pinball table starring the pink hero is Kirby's Pinball Land (1993). Three themed boards and a boss fight up top define that handheld original.

title: Tecmo Bowl (1990)
history: Tecmo's football game Tecmo Bowl (1990) is famous on the NES for calling plays from a set playbook. That coaching choice, more than any one console, is the public memory.

title: Boxing (1980)
history: Bob Whitehead designed Activision's Atari 2600 cartridge Boxing (1980), a two-player bout from the company's early sports line.

title: Final Fantasy Legend III
history: Square's third SaGa, out in Japan in 1991, is Final Fantasy Legend III in the West. Time travel frames this Game Boy party, still sold under the Final Fantasy label abroad.

title: Stargate (1995)
history: The Roland Emmerich film about an ancient portal licensed Stargate (1995). Acclaim's home versions sit with that movie year already printed in the name.

title: Pocket Monsters (Pokemon Green Version)
history: Game Freak's Japanese retail pair was Red and Pocket Monsters (Pokemon Green Version), both in 1996. The later Japanese Blue, not this green cart, supplied more of what international Red and Blue became.

title: Kick Off
history: Dino Dini's Kick Off is the 1989 Anco soccer game whose speed on Amiga and Atari ST made it a rival to later Sensible Soccer. A Game Boy version exists.

title: Metal Gear Solid
history: Hideo Kojima's 1998 PlayStation game Metal Gear Solid is the first 3D Metal Gear. A later Game Boy Color cartridge used this same title in the West for a different story, Ghost Babel.

title: Grand Theft Auto 2
history: DMA Design's Grand Theft Auto 2 stays top-down in 1999 and adds gang respect meters. The Game Boy Color cartridge is a smaller, separate city.

title: Alone in the Dark: The New Nightmare
history: Infogrames revived Edward Carnby in Alone in the Dark: The New Nightmare, a 2001 survival-horror sequel. The Game Boy Color edition is its own 2D game, apart from the console release.

meta.name: Alone in the Dark: The New Nightmare

title: Driver (1999)
history: Reflections' undercover-driver game Driver (1999) made film-style car chases a PlayStation hit. A later Game Boy Color version is a much smaller take on the same premise.

title: Pokemon Crystal
history: Crystal revisits Johto with animated battles and a story beat the Gold and Silver pair did not offer.
lineup: It is the third version of the second generation, still a Game Boy Color game.

title: Heroes of Might and Magic: A Strategic Quest
history: New World Computing's first Heroes game, Heroes of Might and Magic: A Strategic Quest, is the 1995 turn-based strategy of heroes, towns, and creature stacks. A Game Boy Color version arrived years later.

meta.name: Heroes of Might and Magic: A Strategic Quest

title: Rayman
history: Michel Ancel's limbless hero debuted in Ubisoft's Rayman in 1995, first shown on the Atari Jaguar. Later Game Boy Color and DS cartridges reuse the name with their own stages.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages
history: Time travel changes the map of Labrynna, with puzzles that depend on which era you stand in.
lineup: It is one of two linked Game Boy Color Zeldas. Secrets connect it to Oracle of Seasons.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages

title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons
history: A rod of seasons reshapes Holodrum, and the emphasis is action more than Ages' puzzles.
lineup: It is the sibling Game Boy Color Zelda, meant to be played beside Oracle of Ages.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons

title: Catwoman
history: Electronic Arts' Catwoman is the 2004 tie-in to the Halle Berry film. GameCube carries a 3D version, and Game Boy Advance has a separate side-scroller.

title: Pokemon Trading Card Game
history: A campaign of card battles that teaches a deck, not a creature-collecting league.
lineup: It is the Game Boy adaptation of the card game, adjacent to Red and Blue rather than a mainline sequel.

title: FIFA 2000
history: EA Sports shipped FIFA 2000 in 1999, naming the soccer annual for the season ahead. A Game Boy Color edition sat beside the console and PC copies.

title: Gex: Enter the Gecko (1998)
history: Crystal Dynamics' TV-quoting gecko returns in Gex: Enter the Gecko (1998), a 3D platformer on PlayStation and Nintendo 64. The Game Boy Color cartridge is a separate 2D version.

title: Donald Duck: Goin' Quackers
history: Ubisoft's 2000 Disney platformer Donald Duck: Goin' Quackers is called Quack Attack in Europe. Nintendo 64, GameCube, and Game Boy Color each received a version.

title: Vigilante 8
history: Luxoflux's Vigilante 8 is a 1998 car-combat game set in an alternate 1970s, on PlayStation and Nintendo 64. A Game Boy Color adaptation followed.

title: LEGO Racers
history: High Voltage Software built LEGO Racers in 1999 for LEGO Media, a kart racer with brick-built cars. Nintendo 64 got that game, and Game Boy Color got a smaller circuit set.

title: Road Rash II
history: Electronic Arts' Genesis sequel Road Rash II adds split-screen to the motorcycle combat of Road Rash. Punching rivals while racing is still the point.

title: Jet Set Radio
history: Smilebit's Jet Set Radio is the 2000 Dreamcast game about inline crews tagging a city, drawn in cel shading to a pirate-radio beat.

title: DOOM II
history: id Software's DOOM II is the 1994 sequel subtitled Hell on Earth, moving the fights into city levels. A Game Boy Advance port years later cut the episode down to fit.

title: Need for Speed: Underground 2
history: EA Black Box's Need for Speed: Underground 2 is the 2004 street-racing sequel with an open city and deep car customization. GameCube has that structure; the Game Boy Advance cart is a separate racer.

title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell
history: Ubisoft introduced Sam Fisher in Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell, a 2002 stealth game that started on Xbox. GameCube received it, and the Game Boy Advance edition is a separate 2D mission set.

title: Need For Speed Carbon
history: EA's Need For Speed Carbon follows Most Wanted in 2006 with canyon duels and a racing crew. GameCube, Wii, and Nintendo DS versions were sold, the handheld ones built as their own games.

title: Sonic the Hedgehog (1991)
history: Sega's Genesis mascot debuts in Sonic the Hedgehog (1991), built by Sonic Team as a speedy answer to Mario. Later Wii and 3DS reissues are that 16-bit game, not a new adventure.

title: Worms Blast
history: Team17 left the usual turn-based battles for Worms Blast, a 2002 puzzle closer to block-clearing. GameCube and Game Boy Advance both got versions.

title: Marvel Ultimate Alliance
history: Raven Software's Marvel Ultimate Alliance is Activision's 2006 team brawler, switching among Marvel heroes. Wii has that console game, and Game Boy Advance has a smaller separate one.

title: Pokemon FireRed
history: A remake of the 1996 Kanto journey, with the advance generation's mechanics and a post-game island.
lineup: This page is the 2004 remake, not Pokemon Red. LeafGreen is the paired remake.

title: Pokemon Ruby
history: A new region of contests, secret bases, and a weather-themed legendary.
lineup: Ruby is one half of the 2002 pair. Emerald is the third version. Omega Ruby on 3DS is a later remake.

title: The Sims 2
history: Maxis's The Sims 2 is the 2004 PC sequel that adds life stages and aspirations. GameCube and Game Boy Advance releases are separate console games, not the computer simulation shrunk down.

title: The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap
history: Towns and dungeons change scale when Link shrinks to the size of the Minish.
lineup: It is a complete Game Boy Advance Zelda, not a port of an earlier console game.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap

title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney
history: Capcom's courtroom adventure Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney first shipped on the Game Boy Advance in Japan in 2001. The Nintendo DS version that traveled worldwide adds a bonus case and touch-screen evidence.

title: Comix Zone
history: Sega's 1995 Genesis brawler Comix Zone fights through the panels of a living comic. A Wii Virtual Console release later reissued that same cartridge.

title: Rayman Raving Rabbids
history: Ubisoft's Rayman Raving Rabbids became a 2006 Wii party disc of motion minigames after starting life as a platformer. Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS copies are separate products.

title: Oddworld: Munch's Oddysee (2001)
history: Oddworld Inhabitants followed Abe with Oddworld: Munch's Oddysee (2001), an Xbox game that pairs him with a new Gabbit ally. A later Game Boy Advance version retells that journey in 2D.

title: Spider-Man 2: The Game
history: Treyarch's open-city web-swinging tie-in to Sam Raimi's second film is sold here as Spider-Man 2: The Game. The 2004 GameCube version is that sandbox; Game Boy Advance is a side-scroller.

title: Peter Jackson's King Kong: The Official Game of the Movie
history: Ubisoft's Peter Jackson's King Kong: The Official Game of the Movie is the 2005 tie-in that alternates a first-person explorer with Kong himself. GameCube has the main design; Game Boy Advance and DS editions are separate.

meta.name: Peter Jackson's King Kong: The Official Game of the Movie

title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow
history: Ubisoft's 2004 sequel Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow is the first Splinter Cell with spies-versus-mercenaries multiplayer. GameCube has that game, and Game Boy Advance has a 2D side story.

meta.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow

title: Final Fantasy
history: A party of four jobs crosses a cursed world in menu-driven battles.
lineup: It is the NES role-playing game that opened Square's Final Fantasy line.

title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
history: Electronic Arts' Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix is the 2007 tie-in to the fifth book and film, built around casting spells in Hogwarts. Wii, DS, and Game Boy Advance each got a version fitted to that hardware.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix

title: Ultimate Spider-Man
history: Treyarch's Ultimate Spider-Man is a 2005 open-city game based on the Ultimate comics, and you can switch to Venom. GameCube has the 3D version; the handheld editions are separate.

title: Need for Speed: Porsche Unleashed
history: EA's Need for Speed: Porsche Unleashed traces a career through Porsche history and was sold in Europe as Porsche 2000. The Game Boy Advance cartridge keeps the badge and strips the structure down.

title: Metroid: Zero Mission
history: A retelling of the first Metroid with a map, shinespark tricks, and a stealth ending the NES game did not have.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance remake of the NES original, so it has its own page rather than replacing that entry.

title: Tron 2.0
history: Monolith's Tron 2.0 is a 2003 PC sequel set inside the Tron computer world, with disc combat and light cycles. The Game Boy Advance release is a separate action game on that license.

title: Metroid Fusion
history: A more guided Metroid that still hides upgrades off the path it marks for you.
lineup: It launched beside Metroid Prime and is the handheld half of that return.

title: Lego Star Wars: The Video Game
history: Traveller's Tales' first brick Star Wars, Lego Star Wars: The Video Game, retells the prequel trilogy in 2005. GameCube supports co-op play, and Game Boy Advance has a simpler tie-in.

meta.name: Lego Star Wars: The Video Game

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
history: EA's The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King is a 2003 hack-and-slash of the third Jackson film, with two-player co-op on GameCube. The Game Boy Advance version covers the same war from the side.

meta.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King

title: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow
history: A future protagonist absorbs enemy souls in a castle you can map at your own pace.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance Castlevania most often named with Symphony of the Night's explorative style.

title: Shrek 2: The Game
history: Activision's Shrek 2: The Game is the 2004 tie-in to the DreamWorks sequel. GameCube and Game Boy Advance received different versions of that license.

title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney − Trials and Tribulations
history: The third Ace Attorney casebook, Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney − Trials and Tribulations, debuted on the Game Boy Advance in Japan in 2004. DS, Wii, and 3DS releases later carried those trials onward.

meta.name: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney − Trials and Tribulations

title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney − Justice for All
history: Capcom's second Ace Attorney game, Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney − Justice for All, arrived on the Game Boy Advance in Japan in 2002. The Western DS release came later, with the same four cases.

meta.name: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney − Justice for All

title: Madagascar
history: Activision's Madagascar is a 2005 tie-in to the DreamWorks zoo-animal film. GameCube, Game Boy Advance, and Nintendo DS each shipped their own version.

title: Lego Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy
history: Traveller's Tales followed the prequel game with Lego Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy in 2006, a brick retelling of the first three films. GameCube has co-op, and Game Boy Advance has its own version.

meta.name: Lego Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy

title: FINAL FANTASY II
history: Square's 1988 Famicom sequel FINAL FANTASY II raises stats by using weapons and spells, with no experience points. Game Boy Advance and Wii releases later reissued that game.

title: Tony Hawk's Underground 2
history: Neversoft's Tony Hawk's Underground 2 is the 2004 skate sequel that leans into a stunt-tour story. GameCube has that campaign; the Game Boy Advance cart is a separate adaptation.

title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4
history: Neversoft's Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4 is the 2002 entry that drops the two-minute run timer for open goals. GameCube uses that structure, and Game Boy Advance has a different skate game under the name.

title: FIFA 07
history: EA Sports' FIFA 07 covers the 2006 season and was a launch game on PlayStation 3 as well as on the older consoles.

title: Crash of the Titans
history: Radical Entertainment's Crash of the Titans is a 2007 Crash game about grabbing oversized enemies and turning them. Wii, DS, and Game Boy Advance versions differ from one another.

title: Broken Sword 1 - The Shadow of the Templars
history: Revolution Software's Broken Sword 1 - The Shadow of the Templars is the 1996 point-and-click about an American tourist pulled into a Templar plot in Paris. A Game Boy Advance port arrived later.

meta.name: Broken Sword 1 - The Shadow of the Templars

title: Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga
history: Brothers share timed jumps and hammers in a comedy RPG set in a neighboring kingdom.
lineup: It opens the Mario & Luigi series on Game Boy Advance. A 3DS remake exists as its own later entry.

title: Ratatouille
history: THQ's Ratatouille is the 2007 tie-in to Pixar's film about a rat in a Paris kitchen. GameCube, Game Boy Advance, and DS were sold as separate games.

title: Mother 3
history: A rhythm-timed battle system and a story told in chapters, released in Japan and never officially localized at the time.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance sequel to EarthBound, and the last Mother game.

title: Avatar: The Last Airbender - The Burning Earth
history: THQ's second Avatar tie-in, Avatar: The Last Airbender - The Burning Earth, covers the show's Earth Kingdom war in 2007. Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS each have a version.

meta.name: Avatar: The Last Airbender - The Burning Earth

title: Golden Sun
history: Djinn collectibles reshape both puzzles and a class system in a bright role-playing game.
lineup: Camelot's first Golden Sun is the Game Boy Advance original. The Lost Age continues the same story.

title: Fire Emblem
history: Permadeath tactics on a grid, and the first Fire Emblem released in North America.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance game simply titled Fire Emblem, known in Japan as The Blazing Blade.

title: Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord
history: Sir-Tech's Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord is the 1981 Apple II dungeon crawl, by Andrew Greenberg and Robert Woodhead, that set the party-based first-person template. Japanese Game Boy Color releases later carried the early scenarios.

meta.name: Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord

title: NHL 2000
history: EA Sports' hockey annual NHL 2000 shipped in 1999 under the following year's name. A Game Boy Color edition was made for that season.

title: Moorhuhn 3
history: Germany's Crazy Chicken fad continued with Moorhuhn 3, a 2001 entry in the deliberately silly hunting series. A Game Boy Color version put that joke on a cartridge.

title: Perfect Dark (GBC)
history: Rare's Perfect Dark (GBC) is a 2000 Game Boy Color mission set starring Joanna Dark, built as a stealth-leaning companion to the Nintendo 64 shooter. It is not that console campaign cut down.

title: Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2
history: Taito's arcade follow-up to Bubble Bobble is Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2, swapping bubbles for rainbows you climb. The 1987 cabinet was ported to many home systems afterward.

meta.name: Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2

title: Frogger 2: Swampy's Revenge
history: Hasbro's Frogger 2: Swampy's Revenge is a 2000 sequel to the Frogger revival, with more obstacle courses and a named villain in the title. Game Boy Color was one of the versions.

title: Mega Man Xtreme
history: Capcom's Game Boy Color X entry Mega Man Xtreme remixes stages from the first two Mega Man X games. North America received that cartridge in 2001.

title: Test Drive: Off-Road 3
history: Accolade's dirt-racing line continued with Test Drive: Off-Road 3 in 1999. A Game Boy Color edition was issued under the same off-road name.

title: Resident Evil Gaiden
history: Capcom's Resident Evil Gaiden is a 2001 Game Boy Color side story set on a cruise ship, developed outside the main survival-horror team. It does not port any console Resident Evil.

title: WWF Attitude
history: Acclaim's WWF Attitude is the 1999 wrestling game covering the Attitude Era roster, on Nintendo 64 and PlayStation. Game Boy Color has a reduced take on that license.

title: Mega Man Xtreme 2
history: Capcom's Mega Man Xtreme 2 is the 2001 Game Boy Color follow-up, with a parts system and bosses drawn from Mega Man X3. It stayed a handheld-only X game.

title: Army Men: Sarge's Heroes 2
history: 3DO's Army Men: Sarge's Heroes 2 is the 2000 sequel about green plastic soldiers at war with the tan army. Nintendo 64 has the 3D game, and Game Boy Color has a separate version.

title: Wizardry II: The Knight of Diamonds
history: Sir-Tech's Wizardry II: The Knight of Diamonds is the 1982 sequel, a shorter scenario that imports a party from the first dungeon. It belongs to the original Apple II Wizardry line.

meta.name: Wizardry II: The Knight of Diamonds

title: Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble
history: HAL and Nintendo's Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble reads a tilt sensor inside the 2000 Game Boy Color cartridge, so you tip the whole handheld to roll Kirby. The gimmick is the game.

title: Looney Tunes Racing
history: Infogrames' Looney Tunes Racing is a 2000 kart racer starring the Warner cartoon cast. A Game Boy Color version sits beside the PlayStation release.

title: Toki Tori (2001)
history: Two Tribes' egg-collecting puzzle Toki Tori (2001) is a Game Boy Color original about a small chick. Later Wii and 3DS releases remake this handheld game.

title: Rampage 2: Universal Tour
history: Midway's Rampage 2: Universal Tour sends George, Lizzie, and Ralph off Earth in 1999 to smash cities on other worlds.

title: Disney's Dinosaur
history: Disney's prehistoric film licensed Disney's Dinosaur in 2000. The Game Boy Color cartridge is one of several home versions sold with that movie.

title: Test Drive Le Mans
history: Infogrames' Test Drive Le Mans, also sold as Le Mans 24 Hours, is a 2000 endurance racer built around the French day-long race. A Game Boy Color version carries the same event.

title: Hugo: Black Diamond Fever
history: The Danish TV troll returns in Hugo: Black Diamond Fever, a 2001 entry from Interactive Television Entertainment's long Hugo line. Game Boy Color is one of many Hugo cartridges.

title: Daikatana
history: John Romero's Ion Storm shooter Daikatana is the 2000 PC game whose long delay became infamous. The Game Boy Color release is a separate action game, not that first-person project.

title: Yars' Revenge
history: Howard Scott Warshaw's Yars' Revenge is the 1982 Atari 2600 cartridge that became one of the console's biggest original sellers. The insect-versus-shield battle is an Atari design.

title: The Lion King: Simba's Mighty Adventure
history: Activision's The Lion King: Simba's Mighty Adventure is a 2000 follow-up to the earlier Lion King platformer, covering scenes past the first film. PlayStation and Game Boy Color both had versions.

meta.name: The Lion King: Simba's Mighty Adventure

title: Wizardry III: Legacy of Llylgamyn
history: Sir-Tech's third scenario, Wizardry III: Legacy of Llylgamyn, arrived in 1983 and shifts the dungeon crawl toward a new generation of heroes. It closes the original Apple II trilogy.

title: Pokémon Puzzle Challenge (2000)
history: Intelligent Systems recast Panel de Pon with Pokémon faces for Pokémon Puzzle Challenge (2000). Clearing stacks is the whole contest, and it is the color-handheld cousin of Pokémon Puzzle League rather than a Red or Blue adventure.

title: Harvest Moon GB
history: The first handheld Harvest Moon is Harvest Moon GB, a 1997 farm sim from Victor Interactive, published in the West by Natsume. Crops, livestock, and town visits fill the cartridge.

title: F1 Racing Championship
history: Ubisoft's official Formula 1 license F1 Racing Championship reached Nintendo 64 in 2000. The Game Boy Color edition is a simpler racer under the same name.

title: Dragon Ball Z: Legendary Super Warriors
history: Banpresto's Dragon Ball Z: Legendary Super Warriors is a 2002 Game Boy Color strategy game that retells major Dragon Ball Z fights with a card-like battle system. Infogrames published it in the West.

meta.name: Dragon Ball Z: Legendary Super Warriors

title: Azure Dreams GB
history: Konami's tower-climbing monster game reached Game Boy Color as Azure Dreams GB in 1999, a handheld companion to the PlayStation release. Random floors and egg hatching remain the loop.

title: Donkey Kong Land 3
history: Rare's Donkey Kong Land 3 is the 1997 handheld companion to Donkey Kong Country 3, starring Dixie and Kiddy. Color hardware shows off what the Game Boy version started.

title: Kirikou
history: Michel Ocelot's French animated film licensed Kirikou, a 2001 Game Boy Color release aimed at European players. It is a cartoon adaptation, not a Nintendo adventure.

title: Mickey's Speedway USA
history: Rare's Mickey's Speedway USA is a 2000 kart racer starring Mickey and the Disney cast, made for Nintendo 64. The Game Boy Color version is a separate top-down circuit game.

title: NASCAR Heat
history: Hasbro's NASCAR Heat is a 2000 stock-car license for that NASCAR season. PlayStation, PC, and Game Boy Color all carried editions.

title: Harvest Moon 2 GBC (1999)
history: Harvest Moon 2 GBC (1999) is Natsume's sequel to Harvest Moon GB, with a bigger town and more villagers than that first cartridge. It sits between the original Game Boy farm and Harvest Moon 3 GBC.

title: Harry Potter: Quidditch World Cup
history: EA's Harry Potter: Quidditch World Cup is a 2003 sports game about the broomstick matches from the books. GameCube has the 3D version, and Game Boy Advance has a simpler adaptation.

title: Tony Hawk's Underground
history: Neversoft's Tony Hawk's Underground is the 2003 skate game that adds a story and lets you get off the board. GameCube has that campaign; Game Boy Advance is a separate skate title.

title: Fire Emblem: The Sacred Stones
history: A smaller cast and a world map of optional fights distinguish this campaign.
lineup: It is the other widely released Game Boy Advance Fire Emblem, separate from the first Western release.

title: Final Fantasy Tactics Advance
history: Clan laws and a snow-globe world of jobs, built for short handheld maps.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance tactics game, a spin on the earlier PlayStation Tactics rather than that game's port.

title: James Bond 007: NightFire
history: Eurocom's James Bond 007: NightFire is EA's 2002 Bond shooter, a follow-up to Agent Under Fire. GameCube has the main missions, and Game Boy Advance is a separate first-person take.

title: Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories
history: Square Enix and Jupiter's Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories is the 2004 Game Boy Advance entry set between the first two Kingdom Hearts games. Fights run on a deck of cards, and a later PlayStation 2 remix rebuilds it in 3D.

title: Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue
history: Traveller's Tales' Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue is Activision's 1999 3D platformer based on the Pixar sequel. Nintendo 64 received that console game.

meta.name: Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue

title: Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance
history: Snowblind Studios' Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance is a 2001 console hack-and-slash in the Forgotten Realms, separate from BioWare's PC Baldur's Gate. GameCube got a port, and a Game Boy Advance game later used the name.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2003)
history: Konami's beat-em-up based on the cartoon that premiered the same year is Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2003). GameCube has the 3D brawler, and Game Boy Advance has a side-scrolling counterpart.

title: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Blue Rescue Team
history: On Nintendo DS, Chunsoft's Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Blue Rescue Team is where a human wakes as a Pokemon and takes rescue jobs in 2005. The cartridge can link jobs with its Game Boy Advance partner.

meta.name: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Blue Rescue Team

title: Medal of Honor: Underground
history: DreamWorks Interactive's Medal of Honor: Underground is a 2000 PlayStation follow-up that follows French fighter Manon through World War II. The Game Boy Advance release is a later, separate shooter.

title: Colin McRae Rally 2.0
history: Codemasters' Colin McRae Rally 2.0 is the 2000 rally sequel named for the Scottish champion, built around stage times. A Game Boy Advance version followed as a handheld adaptation.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
history: EA's The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers is the 2002 action game of the second Jackson film, including Helm's Deep. GameCube has the 3D battles, and Game Boy Advance has its own side-view campaign.

meta.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers

title: Advance Wars
history: Turn-based army maps where each commanding officer bends the same units in a different way.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance strategy game that introduced many players to the Wars series. A much later Switch collection revisits the early games.

title: Worms World Party
history: Team17's Worms World Party is a 2001 party-minded entry in the artillery series. The Game Boy Advance version keeps those turn-based worm battles on a small screen.

title: Madden NFL 07
history: EA Sports' Madden NFL 07 is the football annual for the 2006 season, and it launched on PlayStation 3 alongside the older consoles.

title: Ford Racing 3
history: The licensed Ford lineup racer Ford Racing 3 arrived in 2005. Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS versions are the handheld editions of that license.

title: Pirates of the Caribbean
history: Disney's pirate license reached Game Boy Advance as Pirates of the Caribbean in 2003, the year the first film opened. The cartridge is a handheld adventure under that name.

title: Mario Party
history: A board game of dice and minigames that assumes four people around one console.
lineup: It opens the Mario Party series on Nintendo 64.

title: Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance
history: Konami's Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is the 2002 Game Boy Advance follow-up to Circle of the Moon, with Juste Belmont exploring a twin castle. It is a brighter, larger handheld original.

title: Mario Kart: Super Circuit
history: Flat, bright courses for a small screen, plus a cup list drawn from Super Mario Kart.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance Kart, between the Nintendo 64 game and later handheld sequels.

title: The Incredibles
history: THQ's The Incredibles is the 2004 tie-in to Pixar's superhero film. GameCube has the console adventure, and Game Boy Advance has a separate side-scroller.

title: 2006 FIFA World Cup
history: EA Sports' official tournament game 2006 FIFA World Cup covers the national teams in Germany. GameCube and Game Boy Advance each received an edition.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords
history: Nintendo and Capcom's The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords is the 2002 multiplayer quest first packed with the Game Boy Advance port of A Link to the Past. Later DS and 3DS releases revisited four Links at once.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords

title: Wario Land 4
history: A jewel hunt with a timer that starts only after you decide to escape the level.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance Wario Land, louder and more animated than the color games.

title: Open Season
history: Ubisoft's Open Season is the 2006 tie-in to the Sony hunting-season cartoon. Game Boy Advance, GameCube, and Nintendo DS were sold as separate games.

title: Castlevania: Circle of the Moon
history: Konami launched the Game Boy Advance with Castlevania: Circle of the Moon in 2001, using paired cards for magic. In Japan it was sold as Akumajo Dracula: Circle of the Moon, outside the usual numbering.

title: Bionicle Heroes
history: Eidos published Bionicle Heroes in 2006, an action game based on LEGO's Bionicle toys. GameCube, Game Boy Advance, and DS versions each use that license differently.

title: Madden NFL 06
history: EA Sports' Madden NFL 06, released in 2005, adds a quarterback vision cone that hides receivers outside the passer's view.

title: Kirby & the Amazing Mirror
history: A maze of connected rooms and multiple Kirbys, closer to exploration than a straight stage list.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance Kirby that plays least like a linear platformer.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
history: Vivendi's The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring is a 2002 tie-in to the first Jackson film, a different product from EA's later movie brawlers. The Game Boy Advance version follows that journey in handheld form.

meta.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring

title: Heart of Darkness
history: Amazing Studio's Heart of Darkness is a 1998 cinematic platformer published by Interplay on PC and PlayStation, after a long development. Set-piece scenes are what the game is remembered for.

title: Sonic Advance
history: Dimps and Sonic Team's Sonic Advance is the 2001 Game Boy Advance platformer, the first Sonic built for that handheld. You can switch among a small cast at high speed.

title: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom
history: Heavy Iron's SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom is THQ's 2003 platformer, later remade as Rehydrated. GameCube has the 3D adventure, and Game Boy Advance is a separate side-scroller.

meta.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom

title: Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance
history: Midway's Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance is the 2002 fighter that moved the series into 3D and gave each kombatant two fatality styles. GameCube has that game; Game Boy Advance has a smaller 2D reading.

title: Star Wars: Episode III: Revenge of the Sith
history: LucasArts' Star Wars: Episode III: Revenge of the Sith is the 2005 tie-in to the third prequel film. Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS retell the movie as handheld action games.

meta.name: Star Wars: Episode III: Revenge of the Sith

title: The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie
history: THQ's The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie is the 2004 tie-in to the first SpongeBob feature. GameCube has a 3D version, and Game Boy Advance has a side-scrolling one.

title: Street Fighter Alpha 3 (1998)
history: Capcom closed the Alpha line with Street Fighter Alpha 3 (1998), an arcade fighter known for a huge roster and the ISM style selects. The Game Boy Advance port is a celebrated conversion that adds still more fighters.

title: Golden Sun: The Lost Age
history: A second party crosses the sea and links back to the first game's save.
lineup: It is the direct sequel, still on Game Boy Advance, and the end of the story the first cartridge started.

title: WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!
history: Seconds-long microgames pile up until the speed is the joke.
lineup: It is the first WarioWare, the Game Boy Advance original of a series that spread to every later Nintendo handheld and home console.

title: Kirby: Nightmare in Dream Land
history: A remake of Kirby's Adventure with extra modes and cleaner sprites.
lineup: This page is the Game Boy Advance remake. The NES Adventure remains its own entry.

title: Crash Nitro Kart
history: Vicarious Visions' Crash Nitro Kart is the 2003 kart follow-up to Crash Team Racing. GameCube and Game Boy Advance both have versions, the handheld one built separately.

title: Over the Hedge
history: Activision's Over the Hedge is the 2006 tie-in to the DreamWorks film about suburban animals. GameCube, Game Boy Advance, and DS each got a version.

title: SSX Tricky
history: EA Sports BIG's SSX Tricky is the 2001 snowboard sequel that exaggerates the trick system of the first SSX. GameCube has the main game, and Game Boy Advance has a reduced adaptation.

title: FIFA 2005
history: EA Canada shipped FIFA 2005 in 2004 with a first-touch system that changes how a trap sets up the next pass.

title: Pong (1972)
history: Al Alcorn's paddle tennis for Atari is Pong (1972), the arcade rally that became a commercial phenomenon. Decades of reissues followed that cabinet.

title: FIFA 06
history: EA Sports' FIFA 06 covers the 2005 season and was ready for the Xbox 360 launch as well as for older consoles.

title: Cave Story: Doukutsu Monogatari
history: Daisuke Amaya, working as Pixel, gave away Cave Story: Doukutsu Monogatari for PC in 2004. Later paid ports, including a Nintendo 3DS eShop release, spread that one-person platformer.

title: Meet the Robinsons
history: Disney's Meet the Robinsons is the 2007 tie-in to the time-travel cartoon. Game Boy Advance and GameCube versions shipped with the film.

title: Sonic Advance 3
history: Dimps' Sonic Advance 3 is the 2004 Game Boy Advance platformer that pairs Sonic with a partner who changes his moves. It is the third Advance game and stayed on that handheld.

title: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red Rescue Team
history: Nintendo's Game Boy Advance rescue story Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red Rescue Team shares a 2005 plot with a DS partner cart, both made by Chunsoft. Friend rescue codes pass between those two editions.

meta.name: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red Rescue Team

title: FIFA 2004
history: EA Sports released FIFA 2004 in 2003 and switched offsides off after complaints about the previous annual.

title: Super Mario Advance
history: Nintendo's Super Mario Advance is the 2001 Game Boy Advance remake of Super Mario Bros. 2, the game that began as Doki Doki Panic. A two-player Mario Bros. mode is included.

title: X2: Wolverine's Revenge
history: Activision's X2: Wolverine's Revenge is a 2003 Wolverine action game sold around the X2 film. GameCube and Game Boy Advance received different versions.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles 2: Battle Nexus
history: Konami's Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles 2: Battle Nexus is the 2004 cartoon follow-up named for a multiverse tournament. You clear ladders of fighters between story stages.

meta.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles 2: Battle Nexus

title: Sonic Advance 2
history: Dimps' Sonic Advance 2 is the 2002 Game Boy Advance sequel built around a boost that sends Sonic uphill. Cream the Rabbit joins the playable cast here.

title: Dead to Rights
history: Namco's Dead to Rights is a 2002 third-person shooter about a cop whose dog fights beside him. GameCube ports the console game, and Game Boy Advance is a separate side-scroller.

title: Cars
history: THQ's Cars is the 2006 racing game based on the Pixar film. GameCube has the console racer, and Game Boy Advance has a smaller licensed version.

title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, The Witch, and The Wardrobe
history: Disney's The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, The Witch, and The Wardrobe is the 2005 action game based on the Walden film. GameCube and Game Boy Advance each retell that story for their hardware.

meta.name: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, The Witch, and The Wardrobe

title: Surf's Up
