history: Ubisoft's Surf's Up is the 2007 tie-in to the penguin-surfing film. Game Boy Advance and GameCube versions shipped with the movie.

title: Advance Wars 2: Black Hole Rising
history: A new enemy faction and more COs extend the map-by-map campaign.
lineup: It is the second Game Boy Advance Advance Wars, not the DS Dual Strike.

title: Super Mario World: Super Mario Advance 2
history: Nintendo's Super Mario World: Super Mario Advance 2 is the 2001 Game Boy Advance port of Super Mario World. Luigi is playable from the start, which the Super Nintendo original did not allow.

meta.name: Super Mario World: Super Mario Advance 2

title: Bionicle: The Game
history: LEGO's Bionicle storyline licensed Bionicle: The Game in 2003. GameCube and Game Boy Advance each received an action version of those toy heroes.

title: Turok: Evolution
history: Acclaim's Turok: Evolution is the 2002 prequel in the dinosaur-hunting series. GameCube has the first-person game, and Game Boy Advance has a separate side-scroller.

title: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Rogue Spear
history: Red Storm's Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Rogue Spear is the 1999 tactical shooter that followed Rainbow Six. The Game Boy Advance cartridge is a later handheld mission set, not the PC planner.

meta.name: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Rogue Spear

title: Top Spin 2
history: 2K Sports' tennis sequel Top Spin 2 arrived in 2006 with an emphasis on shot timing. The Game Boy Advance release is the handheld edition of that license.

title: X-Men: The Official Game
history: Activision's X-Men: The Official Game fills the gap between the X2 and X3 films in 2006, with Wolverine, Iceman, and Nightcrawler among the leads.

title: Shark Tale
history: Activision's Shark Tale is the 2004 tie-in to the DreamWorks underwater film. GameCube and Game Boy Advance each have a version.

title: The Urbz: Sims in the City
history: EA's The Urbz: Sims in the City is a 2004 console spinoff that follows street crews instead of suburban lots. GameCube and Game Boy Advance versions were built for those machines.

meta.name: The Urbz: Sims in the City

title: Fantastic Four
history: Activision's Fantastic Four is the 2005 tie-in to the Marvel film. GameCube and Game Boy Advance let you use the four heroes in separate adaptations.

title: Batman Begins
history: Eurocom's Batman Begins is EA's 2005 stealth action tie-in to Nolan's film. GameCube has that design, and Game Boy Advance has a separate version.

title: Batman: Vengeance
history: Ubisoft's Batman: Vengeance draws on The New Batman Adventures in 2001, pitting Batman against that cartoon's villains rather than a movie plot.

title: The Simpsons: Road Rage
history: Radical Entertainment's The Simpsons: Road Rage sends Springfield locals on fare-chasing drives in 2001, published by Electronic Arts. Homer, Bart, and other regulars each get a car.

title: Yoshi's Island: Super Mario Advance 3
history: Nintendo's Yoshi's Island: Super Mario Advance 3 is the 2002 Game Boy Advance port of Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island. Extra stages sit beyond the Super Nintendo set.

title: The Incredibles: Rise of the Underminer
history: THQ's The Incredibles: Rise of the Underminer picks up after the Pixar film in 2005 and makes the Underminer the threat. Mr. Incredible shares the dig with Frozone.

meta.name: The Incredibles: Rise of the Underminer

title: Kill Switch
history: Namco's Kill Switch is a 2003 third-person shooter often credited with popularizing a dedicated cover button. The Game Boy Advance version is a handheld take on that idea.

title: Asterix & Obelix XXL - Kick Buttix!
history: The Goscinny and Uderzo comics supply Asterix & Obelix XXL - Kick Buttix!, a 2004 handheld entry in the Asterix and Obelix XXL line. Game Boy Advance uses the Kick Buttix name on the box.

title: Shining Force: The Legacy of Great Intention
history: Sega's first strategy RPG in the line, Shining Force: The Legacy of Great Intention, arrived on the Genesis in 1992, developed with Climax. A later Game Boy Advance remake reworks that campaign.

meta.name: Shining Force: The Legacy of Great Intention

title: Shrek SuperSlam
history: Activision's Shrek SuperSlam is a 2005 arena fighter starring the DreamWorks cast. The Game Boy Advance version is a handheld brawler under that name.

title: Mario vs. Donkey Kong (2004)
history: Nintendo Software Technology's puzzle chase Mario vs. Donkey Kong (2004) succeeds the 1994 Game Boy Donkey Kong. Mario pursues toy Mini-Marios through construction-site stages.

title: Finding Nemo
history: THQ's Finding Nemo is the 2003 tie-in to the Pixar ocean film. The Game Boy Advance version is a side-scrolling adaptation of that movie.

title: Pac-Man World 2 (2002)
history: Namco's 3D platformer sequel Pac-Man World 2 (2002) sends Pac-Man after ghosts who stole the golden fruit. A Game Boy Advance version turns that quest into a handheld platformer.

title: Robots
history: The Blue Sky robot-city film licensed Robots in 2005. The Game Boy Advance version is the handheld edition of that movie tie-in.

title: Pink Panther: Pinkadelic Pursuit
history: The cartoon panther licensed Pink Panther: Pinkadelic Pursuit in 2003, a platformer sold in Europe and North America. Game Boy Advance is one of the versions.

title: Star Wars Episode I: Jedi Power Battles
history: LucasArts' Star Wars Episode I: Jedi Power Battles is a 2000 brawler through the first prequel, with two players as Jedi. It launched on PlayStation, and a Dreamcast version followed.

meta.name: Star Wars Episode I: Jedi Power Battles

title: Mega Man Zero
history: Inti Creates' Mega Man Zero starts a new Capcom series on the Game Boy Advance in 2002, set after the X games. High difficulty and cyber-elves define that handheld original.

title: Avatar: The Last Airbender
history: THQ's Avatar: The Last Airbender is the 2006 action game based on the Nickelodeon series. The Game Boy Advance version is a side-scrolling tie-in to the bending battles.

title: Grand Theft Auto Advance
history: Digital Eclipse developed Grand Theft Auto Advance for Rockstar in 2004, a top-down Game Boy Advance story of its own. It does not port Grand Theft Auto III.

title: Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town
history: Marvelous remade Back to Nature on the Game Boy Advance as Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town. Natsume published that 2003 Western farm sim.

meta.name: Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town

title: Alien Hominid
history: The Behemoth's run-and-gun Alien Hominid began as a Newgrounds Flash cartoon and reached consoles in 2004. The hand-drawn look stayed intact on the retail versions.

title: The Legend of Spyro: A New Beginning
history: Krome Studios' The Legend of Spyro: A New Beginning is Vivendi's 2006 reboot, a darker origin for Spyro. The Game Boy Advance version is a separate 2D adaptation of that restart.

meta.name: The Legend of Spyro: A New Beginning

title: Mega Man Battle Network
history: Capcom's Mega Man Battle Network starts a 2001 Game Boy Advance RPG about net battles fought with collectible chips. It stands apart from the classic platformers.

title: Resident Evil 4
history: An over-the-shoulder shooter that debuted on GameCube before it spread to other hardware.
lineup: This page is the 2005 GameCube original, not the later remake. It is here because the home debut was a Nintendo console.

title: Hitman 2: Silent Assassin
history: IO Interactive's Hitman 2: Silent Assassin is the 2002 stealth sequel that set Agent 47's contract structure. A GameCube port brought those missions to Nintendo's console.

title: Tomb Raider: Legend
history: Crystal Dynamics rebooted Lara Croft with Tomb Raider: Legend in 2006, that studio's first Tomb Raider. GameCube received a port of the console adventure.

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast
history: Raven Software's Star Wars Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast returns Kyle Katarn to a lightsaber in 2002. LucasArts published it, including a GameCube version.

meta.name: Star Wars Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast

title: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
history: Ubisoft Montreal revived Jordan Mechner's series with Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time in 2003, built around a dagger that rewinds a few seconds of mistakes.

meta.name: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time

title: Need For Speed: Most Wanted
history: EA Black Box's Need For Speed: Most Wanted is the 2005 street racer about climbing a blacklist of police and rivals in an open city. The GameCube version is that same pursuit.

title: Prince of Persia: Warrior Within
history: Ubisoft's Prince of Persia: Warrior Within is the 2004 sequel, a darker follow-up to The Sands of Time with a heavier combat focus. GameCube received that console version.

title: Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones
history: Ubisoft closed the Sands trilogy with Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones in 2005, mixing acrobatics with speed kills. GameCube has the original release, and a Wii version followed.

meta.name: Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones

title: Crazy Taxi (1999)
history: Sega's Hitmaker cabinet Crazy Taxi (1999) is a clock-racing fare game that became a Dreamcast hit. The GameCube release is a home port of that arcade design.

title: Sonic Adventure 2
history: Sonic Team's Sonic Adventure 2 splits into hero and dark stories on the Dreamcast in 2001, and it introduces Shadow. The GameCube Battle edition later added more multiplayer.

title: Sonic Adventure DX: Director's Cut
history: The 2003 GameCube edition of the Dreamcast original is Sonic Adventure DX: Director's Cut, adding Game Gear games and mission cards. It is an enhanced port, not a new numbered sequel.

title: KAO the Kangaroo: Round 2
history: Poland's Tate Interactive continued its boxing kangaroo with KAO the Kangaroo: Round 2, a cartoon platformer that reached GameCube. It is the sequel in that European series.

title: Beyond Good & Evil
history: Michel Ancel's Beyond Good & Evil is Ubisoft's 2003 adventure about the photographer Jade on Hillys. The GameCube version is one of the original releases.

title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Chaos Theory
history: Ubisoft's third Splinter Cell, Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Chaos Theory, is the 2005 entry many players treat as the peak of the early stealth games. The Nintendo DS release is a different top-down game.

meta.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Chaos Theory

title: XIII
history: Ubisoft's cel-shaded shooter XIII adapts the Belgian comic by Van Hamme and Vance in 2003, cutting between panels as you fight.

title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Double Agent
history: The 2006 undercover entry Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Double Agent shipped as two different campaigns. GameCube and Wii carry the last-generation version, separate from the Xbox 360 game.

meta.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Double Agent

title: Red Faction II
history: Volition's Red Faction II leaves the first game's destructible Mars tunnels for a more linear 2002 campaign with squad chatter.

title: Street Racing Syndicate
history: Eutechnyx's Street Racing Syndicate is a 2004 street racer that mixes races with a city nightlife scene. GameCube shipped alongside the PlayStation 2 and Xbox versions.

title: Need for Speed: Underground
history: EA Black Box turned the series toward illegal street racing with Need for Speed: Underground in 2003. The GameCube version is that pink-slip career.

title: Sonic the Hedgehog 2
history: Sega's Sonic the Hedgehog 2 is the 1992 Genesis sequel that introduces Tails and the spin dash. Later Wii and 3DS releases reissue that 16-bit game.

title: Resident Evil (2002)
history: Shinji Mikami directed Capcom's GameCube remake Resident Evil (2002), a full rebuild of the 1996 mansion. A Wii edition later reissued that same remake.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess
history: A wolf form, a darker Hyrule, and a launch-window Wii adventure that also shipped on GameCube.
lineup: This one page covers both 2006 releases. Twilight Princess HD on Wii U is a separate remaster page.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess

title: Broken Sword 3 - The Sleeping Dragon
history: Revolution Software's Broken Sword 3 - The Sleeping Dragon is the 2003 sequel, the first Broken Sword in 3D. George and Nico return, and GameCube was among the platforms.

title: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker
history: A cartoon sea of islands, a conducting baton, and a boat that is the overworld.
lineup: The cel-shaded voyage under the King of Red Lions starts on this page. Wind Waker HD on Wii U is a separate page.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker

title: BloodRayne
history: Terminal Reality's BloodRayne is Majesco's 2002 action game about a dhampir agent. GameCube is one of the console versions, and a film later used the name.

title: GUN
history: Neversoft's western GUN is a 2005 revenge story on horseback, published by Activision. The GameCube version is that open-country shooter.

title: The Sims
history: Will Wright and Maxis's The Sims is the 2000 PC phenomenon about household needs. The GameCube release is a separate console game inspired by it.

title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
history: EA's Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets is the 2002 tie-in to the second book and film. On GameCube you can roam Hogwarts between classes, a step past the first game.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets

title: Ikaruga
history: Treasure's Ikaruga is Hiroshi Iuchi's 2001 shooter, built on swapping black and white polarity to absorb shots. The GameCube disc is a home port of that arcade game.

title: Super Mario Sunshine
history: Mission-based tropical stages and a water pack that sprays, hovers, and cleans goop.
lineup: Isle Delfino, FLUDD, and Shadow Mario are the adventure on this page. A limited Switch compilation, Super Mario 3D All-Stars, included it for a time and is not treated here as a standing listing.

title: Conflict Desert Storm
history: Pivotal Games' squad shooter Conflict Desert Storm follows special forces in the Gulf War and was published by SCi. GameCube received a port of that tactical campaign.

title: Super Smash Bros. Melee
history: A faster Smash with wavedashing culture, trophies, and a much larger roster than the Nintendo 64 game.
lineup: It is the GameCube Smash, the competitive center of the series for years.

title: killer7
history: Suda51 and Grasshopper Manufacture's killer7 is Capcom's 2005 on-rails assassin game, drawn in cel shading. It debuted on GameCube and PlayStation 2.

title: Call of Duty: Black Ops
history: Treyarch's Call of Duty: Black Ops is the 2010 Cold War shooter that opened the Black Ops line. A Wii version shipped, and the Nintendo DS edition is a separate portable campaign.

title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3
history: Infinity Ward and Sledgehammer closed the original Modern Warfare story with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 in 2011. The Wii version adapts that campaign for motion controls.

title: LEGO The Lord of the Rings
history: Traveller's Tales' LEGO The Lord of the Rings retells the three Jackson films in 2012 and lets you wander an open Middle-earth between story beats.

meta.name: LEGO The Lord of the Rings

title: Tomb Raider: Underworld
history: Crystal Dynamics' Tomb Raider: Underworld continues the Legend-era Lara in 2008. The Wii version is a reduced adaptation, and the DS game is a separate side story.

title: Call of Duty: World at War
history: Treyarch's Call of Duty: World at War is the 2008 World War II shooter covering the Pacific and the Eastern Front. Wii has a version, and the DS edition is its own portable game.

meta.name: Call of Duty: World at War

title: World of Goo
history: 2D Boy's World of Goo is the 2008 physics puzzle about building structures from living goo balls, a PC and WiiWare hit. Nintendo Switch received a port much later.

title: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare
history: Infinity Ward rebooted Call of Duty in the present day with Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare in 2007. A Wii port came later, and the DS version is a separate campaign.

title: Bully: Scholarship Edition
history: Rockstar's Bully: Scholarship Edition is the 2008 expanded release of the 2006 school satire. The Wii version includes the extra classes from that edition.

title: Tomb Raider: Anniversary
history: Crystal Dynamics rebuilt the 1996 mansion raid as Tomb Raider: Anniversary in 2007, using the Legend engine. A Wii version followed the PlayStation 2 and PC releases.

title: Need For Speed: Hot Pursuit
history: Criterion rebooted the police-chase idea as Need For Speed: Hot Pursuit in 2010, with Autolog social features. A Wii version was built around that console's controllers.

title: Far Cry
history: Crytek's Far Cry is the 2004 PC shooter on a tropical island that launched the series and showed off the first CryEngine.

title: STAR WARS: The Force Unleashed II
history: LucasArts' STAR WARS: The Force Unleashed II is the 2010 sequel about Starkiller's clone. Wii and Nintendo DS versions are scaled adaptations, apart from the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 game.

meta.name: STAR WARS: The Force Unleashed II

title: Rayman Origins
history: Ubisoft Montpellier returned to side-scrolling with Rayman Origins in 2011, playable with up to four characters. Wii and Nintendo 3DS both received that painted platformer.

title: LEGO Star Wars - The Complete Saga
history: Traveller's Tales compiled the prequel game and the original-trilogy game as LEGO Star Wars - The Complete Saga in 2007. Wii and Nintendo DS versions include that combined episode list.

meta.name: LEGO Star Wars - The Complete Saga

title: LEGO Batman
history: Traveller's Tales' first brick Batman, LEGO Batman, arrived in 2008 and splits the campaign between hero chapters and villain chapters.

title: LEGO Batman 2 DC Super Heroes
history: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Batman 2 DC Super Heroes is the 2012 sequel with spoken dialogue and an open Gotham. It reached Wii, Wii U, DS, and 3DS.

title: Cave Story+
history: Nicalis published Cave Story+, the enhanced edition of Daisuke Amaya's freeware, with redrawn art and extra modes. Wii, DS, and 3DS releases carried that version.

title: Mini Ninjas
history: IO Interactive, the Hitman studio, made the family adventure Mini Ninjas in 2009. Wii and Nintendo DS both received versions about the young ninja.

title: LEGO Harry Potter: Years 1-4
history: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Harry Potter: Years 1-4 retells the first four stories in brick form in 2010. Wii and Nintendo DS versions cover those Hogwarts years.

title: METAL SLUG 3
history: SNK's METAL SLUG 3 is the 2000 run-and-gun widely called a high point of the arcade line. A Wii release later brought that Neo Geo game over.

title: BIT.TRIP RUNNER
history: Gaijin Games' BIT.TRIP RUNNER is a 2010 WiiWare rhythm game: CommanderVideo auto-runs, and every jump has to stay on the beat. It is the fourth BIT.TRIP release.

title: Back to the Future: The Game
history: Telltale's episodic sequel to the film trilogy is Back to the Future: The Game, from 2010, with Christopher Lloyd returning as Doc. A Wii version collected those episodes.

meta.name: Back to the Future: The Game

title: Broken Sword 1 - Shadow of the Templars (The Director's Cut)
history: Revolution's Broken Sword 1 - Shadow of the Templars (The Director's Cut) is the 2009 remake of the 1996 adventure, adding a chapter playable as Nico. Wii and Nintendo DS use that expanded script.

meta.name: Broken Sword 1 - Shadow of the Templars (The Director's Cut)

title: Sid Meier's Pirates!
history: Firaxis remade Meier's 1987 seafaring game in 2004 as Sid Meier's Pirates!, mixing sailing, sword fights, and dancing. The Wii version is a later port of that remake.

title: UNO
history: Mattel's shedding card game reaches consoles as UNO, matching colors and numbers the way the tabletop deck does. Wii and Nintendo DS editions let a room play without the physical pack.

title: FIFA 14
history: EA Sports' soccer annual FIFA 14 shipped in 2013. The Wii and Nintendo 3DS editions are separate from the Ignite-engine game on newer consoles.

title: Swords and Soldiers HD
history: Ronimo Games' side-scrolling strategy of Vikings, Aztecs, and Chinese armies was upgraded as Swords and Soldiers HD. The HD edition sharpens the WiiWare original.

title: LEGO Harry Potter: Years 5-7
history: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Harry Potter: Years 5-7 covers the last three stories in 2011, from the Order of the Phoenix through the Battle of Hogwarts.

title: Need For Speed Undercover
history: EA's Need For Speed Undercover is a 2008 street racer framed as an undercover-cop story in an open city. Wii and Nintendo DS versions are scaled-down games under that name.

title: Sniper Elite
history: Rebellion's Sniper Elite is the 2005 World War II shooter known for its bullet-camera kills. The Wii release is a later port of that first game.

title: LEGO Star Wars III - The Clone Wars
history: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Star Wars III - The Clone Wars is the 2011 game based on the animated Clone Wars, adding large ground battles. Wii, DS, and 3DS received versions.

meta.name: LEGO Star Wars III - The Clone Wars

title: And Yet It Moves
history: Broken Rules' And Yet It Moves is a 2009 puzzle where you rotate the whole scene so the character can walk on a new surface. The WiiWare version brought that paper-collage idea to a console.

title: Toribash
history: Nabi Studios' Toribash is a turn-based fighter: you set each joint, then watch the physics play out. The WiiWare release is a console edition of that PC original.

title: Rec Room
history: Against Gravity launched Rec Room in 2016 as a social virtual-reality hangout full of user-made rooms and mini-games. Players meet as avatars on PC headsets.

title: Toki Tori
history: Two Tribes reissued the chick's egg hunt as Toki Tori on WiiWare in 2008, after the Game Boy Color original. Later Wii U and 3DS releases keep that puzzle.

title: LEGO Indiana Jones: The Original Adventures
history: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Indiana Jones: The Original Adventures retells Raiders, Temple of Doom, and The Last Crusade in brick form. Wii and Nintendo DS versions cover those three films.

meta.name: LEGO Indiana Jones: The Original Adventures

title: Rayman 3: Hoodlum Havoc
history: Ubisoft's Rayman 3: Hoodlum Havoc sends Rayman against hoodlums in the Glade of Dreams in 2003, and he can lock onto several targets at once.

title: Resident Evil 3: Nemesis
history: Capcom's Resident Evil 3: Nemesis is the 1999 sequel in which Jill flees Raccoon City while Nemesis hunts her. The GameCube version is a later port of that PlayStation game.

title: Sonic the Hedgehog 3 (1994)
history: Sega's Genesis sequel Sonic the Hedgehog 3 (1994) adds save files and a story built to lock onto Sonic & Knuckles. Wii Virtual Console later reissued that 16-bit cartridge.

title: Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon
history: Red Storm's Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon is the 2001 squad shooter about commanding Ghosts in a near-future war. The GameCube version is a console port of that tactical game.

title: The Simpsons: Hit & Run
history: Radical Entertainment's The Simpsons: Hit & Run is a 2003 open-world driving tour of Springfield, published by Vivendi. GameCube is one of the original releases.

title: Metroid Prime
history: First-person exploration of a ruined planet, with a scan visor and suits that reopen old rooms.
lineup: Retro Studios' first-person debut for Samus, scan visor and all, is the game on this page. Metroid Prime Remastered on Switch is a separate page, not a replacement for this one.

title: Star Wars Bounty Hunter
history: LucasArts' Star Wars Bounty Hunter casts you as Jango Fett in 2002, taking contracts with a jetpack before Attack of the Clones.

title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
history: EA's Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban is the 2004 tie-in to the third book and film. The GameCube version adds that year's spells to another Hogwarts roam.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban

title: Sonic & Knuckles
history: Sega's Sonic & Knuckles is the 1994 Genesis cartridge famous for a lock-on port that clips Sonic 2 or Sonic 3 on top. Knuckles is playable, and later compilations keep that team-up.

title: Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2
history: EA's Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2 brought police chases back in 2002. The PlayStation 2 version was built by a different team than the GameCube, Xbox, and PC releases.

title: Mario Kart: Double Dash
history: Nintendo's Mario Kart: Double Dash is the 2003 GameCube entry that seats two riders in each kart so a partner can throw items. It is a home-console Mario Kart.

title: Luigi's Mansion
history: Luigi vacuums ghosts in a flashlight tour of a locked house, room by room.
lineup: It is the GameCube launch game that started the Luigi's Mansion series. Later numbered games are sequels, not this mansion.

title: Judge Dredd: Dredd vs. Death
history: Rebellion's Judge Dredd: Dredd vs. Death pits the 2000 AD lawman against the Dark Judges in 2003, and you can book perps between firefights.

title: Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door
history: Stage-play battles and a rogue's gallery of partners under a cursed town.
lineup: It is the GameCube Paper Mario. A 2024 Switch remake has its own page.

title: Freedom Fighters
history: IO Interactive's Freedom Fighters is a 2003 shooter set in an alternate New York occupied by the Soviet Union. GameCube received a port of that squad campaign.

title: TMNT
history: Ubisoft's TMNT adapts the 2007 CGI movie and lets the four brothers tag into combo strings during fights.

title: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Lockdown
history: Red Storm's Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Lockdown is the 2005 Rainbow Six that plays as a more linear shooter than the planning-heavy earlier games. GameCube is one of the console ports.

title: Medal of Honor: Frontline
history: EA's Medal of Honor: Frontline is the 2002 World War II shooter that opens on the D-Day beach. The GameCube version followed the PlayStation 2 original.

title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
history: EA's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire is the 2005 tie-in built around the Triwizard tasks. The GameCube version supports three players in those challenges.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire

title: Sonic Heroes
history: Sonic Team's Sonic Heroes groups characters into speed, flight, and power teams in 2003. GameCube was a lead Nintendo version of that multiplatform platformer.

title: Neighbours from Hell: Revenge Is a Sweet Game
history: The German prank series about tormenting a noisy neighbor reached consoles as Neighbours from Hell: Revenge Is a Sweet Game. A GameCube version brings those trap-setting levels off the PC.

meta.name: Neighbours from Hell: Revenge Is a Sweet Game

title: Legacy of Kain: Blood Omen 2
history: Crystal Dynamics' Legacy of Kain: Blood Omen 2 continues Kain's vampire timeline in 2002 as a hack-and-slash sequel, years after the first Blood Omen.

title: Spider-Man: The Movie
history: Treyarch developed Activision's Spider-Man: The Movie, the 2002 tie-in to Sam Raimi's first film. The GameCube version is that 3D action game.

title: Enter the Matrix
history: Shiny Entertainment's Enter the Matrix sits beside The Matrix Reloaded and uses footage shot for the films. The 2003 GameCube version stars Niobe and Ghost.

title: Resident Evil Zero
history: Capcom's Resident Evil Zero is a 2002 prequel made first for GameCube, pairing Rebecca Chambers with Billy Coen. A Wii edition later reissued that story.

title: FIFA Street
history: EA Sports BIG's FIFA Street is a 2005 trick-based street soccer spinoff, not the annual simulation. GameCube was part of that original multiplatform release.

title: Terraria
history: Re-Logic's Terraria is the 2011 sandbox of digging, crafting, and bosses, played on a flat plane. Ports reached Wii U, Nintendo 3DS, and Nintendo Switch.

title: Assassin’s Creed IV: Black Flag
history: Ubisoft's Assassin’s Creed IV: Black Flag is the 2013 pirate story of Edward Kenway in the Caribbean. The Wii U version is a full release of that naval game.

title: Super Meat Boy
history: Team Meat's Super Meat Boy is the 2010 platformer from Edmund McMillen and Tommy Refenes, a precise successor to the Flash game Meat Boy. Wii U and Switch ports followed the PC release.

title: Minecraft
history: Markus Persson started Mojang's block-building sandbox Minecraft, publicly playable from 2009. Wii U, 3DS, and Switch editions are later ports of that world.

title: Watch Dogs
history: Ubisoft's Watch Dogs is the 2014 open-world game about hacking Chicago's ctOS network. The Wii U port puts a map on the gamepad.

title: Deus Ex: Human Revolution - Director's Cut
history: Eidos Montreal's expanded cyberpunk RPG Deus Ex: Human Revolution - Director's Cut launched on Wii U in 2013, restoring boss fights and adding commentary. Other platforms received that cut afterward.

meta.name: Deus Ex: Human Revolution - Director's Cut

title: Assassin’s Creed III
history: Ubisoft's Assassin’s Creed III is the 2012 chapter set in the American Revolution, starring Connor. The Wii U port uses the gamepad for the map.

title: Darksiders Warmastered Edition
history: The 2016 remaster of Vigil Games' horseman adventure is Darksiders Warmastered Edition, updating the 2010 original. Wii U and Nintendo Switch both received that edition.

title: Don't Starve
history: Klei's Don't Starve is a 2013 wilderness survival game where hunger and darkness are the usual killers. The Wii U port is a console edition of that PC roguelike.

title: Rayman Legends
history: Ubisoft's Rayman Legends followed Origins in 2013 and was shaped around the Wii U gamepad for Murfy's stages. A Nintendo Switch port later carried the same painted levels.

title: Guacamelee! Super Turbo Championship Edition
history: Drinkbox expanded its 2013 luchador adventure with extra stages on Wii U and Switch in Guacamelee! Super Turbo Championship Edition.

title: Sniper Elite V2
history: Rebellion's Sniper Elite V2 is the 2012 World War II sequel known for an X-ray bullet camera. A Wii U port brought those Berlin missions over.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
history: Climbing, cooking, and a Hyrule you can cross without a set dungeon order.
lineup: It launched on Wii U and Nintendo Switch in 2017. This one page names both. Tears of the Kingdom is the sequel and has its own page.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

title: Bayonetta
history: Hideki Kamiya and PlatinumGames' Bayonetta is the 2009 character action game first published by Sega. Nintendo later funded Wii U and Switch ports, then a sequel.

title: Call of Duty: Black Ops II
history: Treyarch's Call of Duty: Black Ops II splits its 2012 campaign between the 1980s and a near-future war. The Wii U version was a launch title, with loadouts on the gamepad.

meta.name: Call of Duty: Black Ops II

title: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth
history: Nicalis and Edmund McMillen rebuilt the 2011 roguelike as The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth in 2014. Wii U, 3DS, and Switch ports followed the PC release.

title: LEGO The Hobbit
history: Traveller's Tales' LEGO The Hobbit is the 2014 brick telling of Peter Jackson's Hobbit films. Wii U and Nintendo 3DS were part of that release.

title: Darksiders II
history: Vigil Games switched horsemen for Darksiders II in 2012, playing as Death and adding loot. Wii U and, later, Switch ports carry that action RPG.

title: Child of Light
history: Ubisoft Montreal's Child of Light is a 2014 role-playing fable told in rhyme, with a watercolor look. Wii U was an original platform, and Switch came later.

title: Mass Effect 3
history: BioWare's Mass Effect 3 is the 2012 finale of Commander Shepard's trilogy. The Wii U version is a port that followed the Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, and PC releases.

title: The Swapper
history: Facepalm Games' The Swapper is a 2013 puzzle about making clones and moving your mind into them. The Wii U version ports that atmospheric PC game.

title: Resident Evil Revelations
history: Capcom built Resident Evil Revelations first for the Nintendo 3DS in 2012, a cruise-ship story set between Resident Evil 4 and 5. Wii U and later Switch ports expanded it, Raid mode included.

title: Never Alone
history: Upper One Games' Never Alone, also called Kisima Ingitchuna, is a 2014 puzzle platformer drawn from Inupiat folklore. Wii U and Switch versions include the cultural videos.

title: LEGO Marvel Super Heroes
history: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Marvel Super Heroes packs a large Marvel roster into an open New York in 2013, with Galactus among the threats.

title: SteamWorld Dig
history: Image & Form's mining adventure SteamWorld Dig first launched on the Nintendo 3DS eShop in 2013. Wii U and Switch ports followed that robot prospector.

title: Thomas Was Alone
history: Mike Bithell's Thomas Was Alone is a 2012 puzzle about colored rectangles, narrated by Danny Wallace. Wii U and Switch ports came after the PC original.

title: Scribblenauts Unlimited
history: 5th Cell's Scribblenauts Unlimited turns typed words into objects Maxwell can use, a 2012 puzzle. Wii U and Nintendo 3DS share that spawning trick.

title: Race The Sun
history: Flippfly's Race The Sun is a 2013 endless racer: a solar craft that fails when the sun sets. The Wii U version ports that minimalist PC game.

title: Oddworld: New 'n' Tasty
history: Just Add Water's Oddworld: New 'n' Tasty rebuilds Abe's Oddysee in 2014, a new pass at the 1997 factory escape. Wii U was among the console releases.

title: Call of Duty: Ghosts
history: Infinity Ward's Call of Duty: Ghosts is the 2013 shooter with a new cast after Modern Warfare. The Wii U version includes the campaign and uses the gamepad for extras.

title: Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed
history: Sumo Digital's Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed is a 2012 Sega crossover whose karts switch among car, boat, and plane in the middle of a lap.

title: How to Survive
history: Eko Software's How to Survive is a 2013 zombie game about crafting weapons on an island. The Wii U port is a console edition of that overhead camp.

title: Stealth Inc 2: A Game of Clones
history: Curve Studios' Stealth Inc 2: A Game of Clones is a 2014 stealth-puzzle sequel, tied closely to the Wii U. Clones and light puzzles extend the test-chamber traps of the first game.

meta.name: Stealth Inc 2: A Game of Clones

title: Little Inferno
history: Tomorrow Corporation, the studio behind World of Goo, made Little Inferno in 2012: order toys from a catalog and burn them. The Wii U version was an early home for that fireplace.

title: LEGO Batman 3: Beyond Gotham
history: Traveller's Tales sent the DC cast into space in LEGO Batman 3: Beyond Gotham, a 2014 sequel built around the Lantern Corps. Wii U and Nintendo 3DS were part of the release.

title: Tom Clancy’s Splinter Cell Blacklist
history: Ubisoft's Tom Clancy’s Splinter Cell Blacklist is the 2013 Splinter Cell with a faster pace and a new voice for Sam Fisher. The Wii U version ports that campaign.

title: Need for Speed: Most Wanted - A Criterion Game
history: Criterion's Need for Speed: Most Wanted - A Criterion Game is a 2012 open-city reboot, a different game from the 2005 Most Wanted. The Wii U version was part of that multiplatform release.

meta.name: Need for Speed: Most Wanted - A Criterion Game

title: Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams
history: Black Forest Games rebooted the 1987 platformer as Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams in 2012, switching between dream worlds. A Wii U version brought that revival to Nintendo's console.

title: The Bridge
history: Gravity rotates around impossible architecture in The Bridge, a 2013 puzzle inspired by M.C. Escher. The Wii U release ports that black-and-white PC game.

title: FIFA 2002
history: EA Sports released the soccer annual FIFA 2002 in 2001, with power-bar shooting. The GameCube version joined that year's multiplatform set.

title: Sonic Adventure 2 Battle
history: The GameCube edition of Sonic Adventure 2 is Sonic Adventure 2 Battle, adding more multiplayer to the hero and dark stories. It was a launch-window title for the console.

title: FIFA Street 2
history: EA Sports BIG's FIFA Street 2 continues trick-based street soccer in 2006. The GameCube version arrived near the end of that console's sports lineup.

title: Mario Party 7
history: Hudson and Nintendo's Mario Party 7 is the 2005 party game, the last Mario Party on GameCube. It supports eight players and the microphone accessory.

title: Super Monkey Ball
history: Amusement Vision's Super Monkey Ball launched with the GameCube in 2001: tilt the stage to roll a monkey inside a ball. It grew out of the arcade Monkey Ball.

title: Mario Party 6
history: Hudson's Mario Party 6 is the 2004 GameCube party game whose boards change on a day-and-night cycle. The microphone peripheral is used again.

title: NBA LIVE 06
history: EA Sports' basketball annual NBA LIVE 06 shipped in 2005. The GameCube version is that season's edition of the long NBA Live series.

title: Burnout
history: Criterion's Burnout started the series in 2001 around near-miss boosts and crashes. A GameCube port followed the PlayStation 2 original.

title: Capcom vs. SNK 2
history: Capcom's 2001 crossover Capcom vs. SNK 2 mixes both companies' fighters under the groove system. The GameCube edition is the EO revision of that arcade game.

title: Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles
history: Square Enix's Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles is a 2003 GameCube action RPG built for four players linked to Game Boy Advances. It opened a spinoff line rather than continuing the numbered games.

title: Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life
history: Marvelous's Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life follows one farmer across chapters of a life on GameCube. Natsume published the Western release that corresponds to the 2003 Japanese original.

title: James Bond 007: Everything or Nothing
history: EA's James Bond 007: Everything or Nothing is a 2004 third-person Bond game with Pierce Brosnan voicing 007. GameCube is one of the original releases.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Third Age
history: EA's The Lord of the Rings: The Third Age is a 2004 role-playing game with an original party and turn-based battles running beside the film trilogy.

meta.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Third Age

title: Burnout 2: Point of Impact
history: Criterion's Burnout 2: Point of Impact adds a 2002 mode where the score comes from causing the biggest traffic pileup, alongside the usual races.

title: James Bond 007: From Russia with Love
history: EA's James Bond 007: From Russia with Love adapts the 1963 film in 2005 and uses Sean Connery's likeness, jetpack sequence included.

meta.name: James Bond 007: From Russia with Love

title: James Bond 007: Agent Under Fire
history: EA's James Bond 007: Agent Under Fire is a 2001 original mission set, not adapted from one film. The GameCube version adds split-screen multiplayer the PlayStation 2 release lacked.

title: I-Ninja
history: Argonaut's I-Ninja is a 2003 cartoon platformer about a small ninja grading his own combat. GameCube shipped with the PlayStation 2 and Xbox versions.

title: Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 2
history: Dimps' fighting sequel Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 2 adds fusions and a board-game story in 2003. The GameCube version is part of that multiplatform release, published by Atari in the West.

title: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six 3: Raven Shield
history: Red Storm's Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six 3: Raven Shield is the 2003 tactical shooter. The GameCube release is the action-led console edition, not the full PC mission planner.

meta.name: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six 3: Raven Shield

title: Star Fox Assault (2005)
history: Nintendo and Namco's Star Fox Assault (2005) sends Fox back to Arwing flights and on-foot shooting after Star Fox Adventures left the series on dinosaur-back. It is the GameCube entry, not Star Fox 64.

title: Spyro: A Hero's Tail
history: Eurocom took over Spyro for Spyro: A Hero's Tail in 2004, after Insomniac's trilogy, and Vivendi published that home-console sequel.

title: FIFA 2003
history: EA Sports released FIFA 2003 in 2002, adding a Club Championship that pits licensed teams in a cup.

title: Rock Band 2
history: Harmonix's Rock Band 2 is the 2008 instrument sequel, with a larger setlist and a tour mode. The Wii version supports the guitar, drums, and microphone.

title: Battle vs Chess
history: Fantasy scenes play out the moves in Battle vs Chess, a 2011 chess game. Wii and Nintendo DS versions were released around that battle-chess idea.

title: METAL SLUG 2
history: SNK's METAL SLUG 2 is the 1998 run-and-gun sequel, adding transformations and new vehicles. A Wii release later reissued that Neo Geo game.

title: FINAL FANTASY IV: THE AFTER YEARS
history: Square Enix's sequel to Final Fantasy IV, FINAL FANTASY IV: THE AFTER YEARS, follows a new generation after the original cast. It began on mobile phones and later reached Wii, DS, and 3DS.

meta.name: FINAL FANTASY IV: THE AFTER YEARS

title: Sonic Unleashed
history: Sonic Team's Sonic Unleashed switches between daytime speed stages and a nighttime werehog in 2008. The Wii version was built separately from the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 game.

title: Spider-Man 3
history: Treyarch's Spider-Man 3 is the 2007 tie-in to Sam Raimi's third film, black suit included. The Wii version uses motion controls for that movie's action.

title: A Boy and His Blob
history: WayForward's A Boy and His Blob revives David Crane's 1989 puzzle in 2009: feed a blob to change its shape. Wii, DS, and 3DS all received that remake.

title: Rock Band
history: Harmonix's Rock Band sold guitar, drums, and a microphone as one band kit in 2007. A Wii version followed the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 launch.

title: Disney•Pixar Toy Story 3: The Video Game
history: Avalanche Software developed Disney's Disney•Pixar Toy Story 3: The Video Game in 2010, an open toy-box tie-in to the Pixar film. Wii and Nintendo DS versions both shipped.

meta.name: Disney•Pixar Toy Story 3: The Video Game

title: The Amazing Spider-Man
history: Beenox's The Amazing Spider-Man is the 2012 open-world game based on the Marc Webb film. Wii, Wii U, and the DS family received versions that differ from the main console release.

title: Puzzle Quest: Challenge of the Warlords
history: Infinite Interactive's Puzzle Quest: Challenge of the Warlords mixes match-three puzzles with a fantasy campaign in 2007, drawing on the Warlords line. Wii and Nintendo DS carried that board to consoles.

meta.name: Puzzle Quest: Challenge of the Warlords

title: Mario Kart Wii
history: Bikes, wheel-shaped shells, and online play in the Kart that sold with a plastic wheel.
lineup: It is the Wii Mario Kart, not Mario Kart 8.

title: Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30
history: Gearbox opened its World War II squad line with Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30 (2005), a Normandy campaign in which giving orders mattered as much as the shooting.

meta.name: Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30

title: Super Smash Bros. Brawl
history: A large roster, a story mode called the Subspace Emissary, and stage hazards turned up.
lineup: It is the Wii Smash, between Melee and the 3DS and Wii U games.

title: FIFA 11
history: EA Sports' club-season football sim FIFA 11 arrived in 2010, and the Wii edition kept motion swings while the other consoles stayed on a pad.

title: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 4 - Dangeresque 3: The Criminal Projective
history: Telltale put Strong Bad's homemade movie hero on a film set in Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 4 - Dangeresque 3: The Criminal Projective, a 2008 episode of the Homestar Runner series also sold on WiiWare.

meta.name: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 4 - Dangeresque 3: The Criminal Projective

title: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 2 - Strong Badia the Free
history: Strong Bad tries to found a country in his own house in Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 2 - Strong Badia the Free, one of Telltale's 2008 Homestar Runner episodes on WiiWare.

meta.name: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 2 - Strong Badia the Free

title: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 5 - 8-Bit Is Enough
history: Retro games take over the season finale Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 5 - 8-Bit Is Enough, closing Telltale's 2008 Homestar Runner run, with a WiiWare release alongside PC.

meta.name: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 5 - 8-Bit Is Enough

title: Spider-Man: Shattered Dimensions
history: Beenox split Spider-Man: Shattered Dimensions (2010) across four comic-book versions of the hero, while the Wii and DS releases are smaller cousins of that HD campaign.

title: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 3 - Baddest of the Bands
history: A battle of the bands drives Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 3 - Baddest of the Bands, another 2008 chapter in Telltale's Homestar Runner series, also released on WiiWare.

meta.name: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 3 - Baddest of the Bands

title: Quantum of Solace
history: Both Casino Royale and the later Bond film are covered by the shooter Quantum of Solace (2008), and a Wii build used pointer aiming.

title: The Beatles: Rock Band
history: Harmonix built The Beatles: Rock Band (2009) entirely from the Beatles catalog, the licensed band game Apple Corps allowed onto plastic instruments.

title: The Godfather: The Game
history: EA Redwood Shores adapted the film trilogy as the open-city crime game The Godfather: The Game (2006), and a Wii port followed the original consoles.

title: LostWinds
history: Frontier launched WiiWare with LostWinds (2008), drawing gusts on the screen so the wind can carry a hero across floating islands.

title: New Super Mario Bros. Wii
history: Four players share a side-scrolling map, with a midair spin carried over from the DS game's idea of 2D Mario.
lineup: It is the Wii entry in the New Super Mario Bros. line, between the DS original and the Wii U game.

title: Rock Band 3
history: A keytar and pro-difficulty parts for real instruments arrived in Harmonix's Rock Band 3 (2010), and the Wii release used that same band setup.

title: Pro Evolution Soccer 2010
history: Konami shipped Pro Evolution Soccer 2010 in 2009, and the Wii edition favored motion kicks over the simulation controls of the other versions.

title: Streets of Rage
history: Sega's side-scrolling brawler Streets of Rage (1991) began on the Genesis, and Virtual Console later reissued it on Wii and Nintendo 3DS.

title: Disney Universe
history: Players wear Disney character costumes through the four-player platform levels of Disney Universe (2011), which included a Wii release.

title: Guitar Hero 5
history: Activision let any player drop into a song already in progress in Guitar Hero 5 (2009), a party-minded entry that also reached Wii.

title: Donkey Kong Country Returns
history: Mine carts, rocket barrels, and levels that expect both Kongs, in a return Retro built for Wii.
lineup: This page is the Wii game, which also had a 3DS version. Donkey Kong Country Returns HD is a separate Switch page.

title: Dead Space: Extraction
history: Eurocom's on-rails prequel Dead Space: Extraction (2009) debuted on Wii with pointer aiming, covering an earlier outbreak before a PlayStation 3 port.

title: NBA 2K12
history: Visual Concepts put Michael Jordan on the cover of NBA 2K12 and built a Jordan Challenge from his career highlights, a 2011 release that also reached Wii.

title: Silent Hill: Shattered Memories
history: Climax reimagined the first Silent Hill as Silent Hill: Shattered Memories (2009), a Wii game with a psychological profile and no combat, later ported to PSP and PlayStation 2.

title: Safecracker: The Ultimate Puzzle Adventure
history: Kheops Studio's mansion of combination locks, Safecracker: The Ultimate Puzzle Adventure, is a puzzle adventure about opening safes, later brought to Wii from PC.

title: Rogue Trooper
history: Rebellion turned the 2000 AD comic into Rogue Trooper (2006), a third-person shooter about the blue Genetic Infantryman, with a Wii version years later.

title: Manhunt 2
history: The UK refused to classify Rockstar's stealth sequel Manhunt 2 (2007) until scenes were cut, and the Wii release was caught in that same censorship fight.

title: Just Dance 2019
history: Ubisoft still manufactured Just Dance 2019 for the original Wii and for Wii U in 2018, long after most publishers had left those consoles.

title: 2010 FIFA World Cup
history: EA Sports' 2010 FIFA World Cup is the licensed tie-in to the tournament held in South Africa, and a Wii edition shipped with it.

title: Luxor 3
history: Colored spheres have to be shot into rolling chains in MumboJumbo's Luxor 3 (2007), and a Wii version joined the casual PC original.

title: Xenoblade Chronicles
history: A huge world on the bodies of two titans, with combat that auto-attacks while you time arts.
lineup: Shulk's story on the Bionis and the Mechonis starts on this page. Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition on Switch is a separate page.

title: Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3
history: Spike's arena fighter Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 (2007) fielded one of the largest rosters in that Dragon Ball line, released on Wii and PlayStation 2.

title: G-Force: The Video Game
history: Disney's spy-guinea-pig film received the tie-in G-Force: The Video Game (2009), with separate Wii and DS builds beside the other consoles.

title: Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End
history: The third film's licensed action game Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End (2007) shipped on Wii and DS along with the home-console versions.

meta.name: Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End

title: Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles
history: Capcom retold the early Resident Evil outbreaks as the Wii light-gun game Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles (2007), later reissued on the Wii U eShop.

title: Mega Man 10(2010)
history: Capcom and Inti Creates followed Mega Man 9 with another 8-bit revival, Mega Man 10(2010), sold on WiiWare with the same limited lives and steep difficulty.

title: WWE '13
history: Yuke's built WWE '13 (2012) around an Attitude Era campaign, and the Wii edition shipped beside the HD wrestling games.

title: NBA 2K13
history: Jay-Z was executive producer of NBA 2K13 (2012), the basketball season known for that curated soundtrack, and a Wii edition was included.

title: Just Dance 2018
history: Ubisoft's pop-routine collection Just Dance 2018 reached stores in 2017 and was still sold for the original Wii.

title: Metroid Prime 2: Echoes
history: Light and dark worlds share a map, and ammunition is a resource the first Prime did not press as hard.
lineup: It is the GameCube sequel, still a Retro Studios Metroid.

title: Madden NFL 13
history: EA introduced the Infinity Engine on HD consoles in Madden NFL 13 (2012), while the Wii edition stayed on the older feature set.

title: BIT.TRIP CORE
history: Gaijin Games' second WiiWare rhythm game, BIT.TRIP CORE (2009), bats beats back with a paddle.

title: BIT.TRIP FATE
history: Commander Video rides a continuous line in BIT.TRIP FATE (2010), a WiiWare chapter of Gaijin Games' rhythm series where every hit answers the music.

title: SAMURAI SHODOWN II
history: SNK's weapons fighter SAMURAI SHODOWN II reached Neo Geo in 1994, and the Wii Virtual Console later sold that arcade game again.

title: Secret Neighbor Beta
history: Hologryph's online hide-and-seek test Secret Neighbor Beta (2019) uses the Hello Neighbor house and was a PC beta, not a Wii release.

title: Rooms: The Main Building
history: Doors only connect after the chambers slide into place in Rooms: The Main Building (2010), a puzzle released on WiiWare.

title: Tales of Graces f
history: Namco's PlayStation 3 edition Tales of Graces f (2012) adds the future arc missing from the earlier Wii release of Tales of Graces.

title: Brothers in Arms: Earned in Blood
history: Another sergeant's squad retells the Normandy fighting in Brothers in Arms: Earned in Blood (2005), the follow-up Gearbox shipped the same year as Road to Hill 30.

meta.name: Brothers in Arms: Earned in Blood

title: The Simpsons Game
history: The family comments on being inside a video game in EA's platformer The Simpsons Game (2007), which has distinct Wii and DS versions.

title: Secret Files: Tunguska
history: Animation Arts built the point-and-click mystery Secret Files: Tunguska (2006) around the Tunguska explosion, and later ports reached Wii and DS.

title: Just Dance 2017
history: Ubisoft's Just Dance 2017 is the 2016 tracklist, still sold as a disc for both Wii and Wii U.

title: Dream Pinball 3D
history: Themed video-pinball tables fill Dream Pinball 3D (2006), and published editions reached both Wii and DS.

title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
history: Motion-controlled spells carry the Wii build of EA's film tie-in Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (2009), with a separate DS game for the sixth movie.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince

title: James Cameron's AVATAR: The Game
history: Ubisoft's James Cameron's AVATAR: The Game (2009) reached stores before James Cameron's film, and the Wii and DS editions are smaller than the HD versions.

title: Doc Clock: The Toasted Sandwich of Time
history: Stickmen Studios' WiiWare puzzle Doc Clock: The Toasted Sandwich of Time (2010) rotates each stage so the clockwork hero can cross the gaps.

meta.name: Doc Clock: The Toasted Sandwich of Time

title: Spider-Man: Web of Shadows
history: The black suit drives Activision's open-Manhattan game Spider-Man: Web of Shadows (2008), and the Wii version is its own build rather than the PS3 and Xbox 360 game.

title: TrackMania
history: Nadeo's restart-friendly time trials came to a living room as the 2010 Wii release of TrackMania.

title: Disney Epic Mickey 2: The Power of Two
history: Junction Point, led by Warren Spector, added Oswald as a co-op partner in Disney Epic Mickey 2: The Power of Two (2012), released on both Wii and Wii U.

meta.name: Disney Epic Mickey 2: The Power of Two

title: Tom Clancy's H.A.W.X.
history: Ubisoft's arcade dogfighter Tom Clancy's H.A.W.X. (2009) sits in the Clancy universe, and the Wii version used motion-assisted flying.

title: Kung Fu Panda
history: The DreamWorks film became the brawler tie-in Kung Fu Panda (2008), with separate Wii and DS versions released alongside the movie.

title: Transformers: The Game
history: Traveller's Tales tied Transformers: The Game (2007) to the first Michael Bay film, switching between robot and vehicle, including on Wii and DS.

title: Wii Sports
history: Tennis, bowling, baseball, golf, and boxing played with motion, and the pack-in that taught the Wii remote.
lineup: It is the Wii launch sports game. Wii Sports Resort and Nintendo Switch Sports are separate entries.

title: Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock
history: Neversoft's Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock (2007) is remembered for its cartoon guitar boss battles, and it was the first Guitar Hero packaged for Wii.

meta.name: Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock

title: X-Men Origins: Wolverine
history: The bloodier Uncaged Edition of X-Men Origins: Wolverine (2009) on HD consoles outpaced the film's violence, while the Wii release was a separate, milder build.

title: No More Heroes
history: An assassin ranks up by earning cash at odd jobs between motion-sword duels.
lineup: It is the Wii original from Grasshopper Manufacture, a third-party game that became a series on Nintendo platforms.

title: Virtua Tennis 4
history: Sega aimed Virtua Tennis 4 (2011) at motion controls, and the Wii version swings the remote as the racket.

title: Golden Axe
history: Sega's fantasy brawler Golden Axe (1989) came from the arcades, and the Wii Virtual Console later reissued it rather than debuting it.

title: Sam & Max Season One: Save the World
history: Telltale's first six Sam and Max episodes are collected in Sam & Max Season One: Save the World (2007), and a Wii version packaged that season for the console.

meta.name: Sam & Max Season One: Save the World

title: Flight Control HD
history: Firemint's path-drawing air-traffic puzzle Flight Control HD (2010) is the console upgrade of the phone game, routing planes so they never collide.

title: Guitar Hero World Tour
history: Drums and vocals turned the series into a full band in Guitar Hero World Tour (2008), and the Wii edition supported that same four-instrument set.

title: Okami
history: Clover Studio's paintbrush adventure Okami (2006) began on PlayStation 2, and the Wii port mapped the celestial brush to pointer controls.

title: MDK 2
history: BioWare's sequel MDK 2 (2000) followed Shiny's MDK as a third-person shooter on PC, Dreamcast, and PlayStation 2, not as a Wii debut.

title: Driver: Parallel Lines
history: Reflections split a New York crime story between 1978 and a later era in Driver: Parallel Lines, and the 2006 original later received a Wii port.

title: Bejeweled 2
history: PopCap followed its breakthrough match-three with Bejeweled 2 (2004), adding puzzle and endless modes on top of swapping gems.

title: SENGOKU Anthology
history: SNK's SENGOKU Anthology collects the three Sengoku arcade brawlers, demon-fighting beat-em-ups released on PC and PlayStation 2 rather than Wii.

title: Disney Infinity
history: Avalanche Software's toys-to-life sandbox Disney Infinity (2013) unlocks Disney play sets with plastic figures, including Wii, Wii U, and a separate 3DS game.

title: 428: Shibuya Scramble
history: Chunsoft's live-action sound novel began on Wii in Japan, and the 2018 international release of 428: Shibuya Scramble brought that branching Shibuya story west.

title: de Blob 2
history: Blue Tongue's de Blob 2 (2011) continues the paint-the-city platforming of the original, and THQ included a Wii version at launch.

title: Syberia
history: Benoit Sokal's point-and-click Syberia (2002) follows a clockwork journey east, later ported to DS and, much later, to Switch.

title: GRID (2008)
history: Codemasters rebuilt its circuit-racing line as GRID (2008), and the DS release is a separate handheld rather than that console sim.

title: Plants vs. Zombies GOTY Edition
history: PopCap's expanded reissue Plants vs. Zombies GOTY Edition (2010) adds extras on top of the lawn-defense original, including a music video and further modes.

title: The Sims 3
history: EA's life sim The Sims 3 (2009) opened whole neighborhoods instead of a single lot, while the DS and 3DS editions are smaller separate games.

title: Plants vs. Zombies
history: George Fan's lawn-defense comedy Plants vs. Zombies (2009) made PopCap a household name, and a DS version later recreated those lanes on a handheld.

title: Bejeweled 3
history: Quest modes and new gem powers surround the classic grid in PopCap's Bejeweled 3 (2010), the match-three follow-up best known on PC.

title: Sonic & SEGA All-Stars Racing
history: Sumo Digital packed Sega characters into the kart racer Sonic & SEGA All-Stars Racing (2010), and both Wii and DS received their own versions.

title: MX vs. ATV Reflex
history: Rainbow Studios' off-road racer MX vs. ATV Reflex (2009) is known for leaning the rider to shift weight, with a separate DS release.

title: Colin McRae: DiRT 2
history: Codemasters' festival off-road racer Colin McRae: DiRT 2 (2009) has reduced Wii and DS editions that are not the HD game.

title: Star Wars: The Force Unleashed
history: LucasArts' Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (2008) follows a secret apprentice between the film trilogies, and the Wii and DS versions were built apart from the HD consoles.

title: Agatha Christie - The ABC Murders
history: Artefacts Studio's point-and-click Agatha Christie - The ABC Murders (2016) adapts the Poirot novel, a different game from the earlier DS title that used the same book.

title: Need for Speed: ProStreet
history: EA Black Box turned the series toward sanctioned race days in Need for Speed: ProStreet (2007), leaving open-road police chases behind, with Wii and DS versions.

title: Transformers: War for Cybertron
history: High Moon Studios set Transformers: War for Cybertron (2010) on the robots' home world, a licensed shooter praised well beyond the usual tie-in, while Wii and DS got separate games.

title: LEGO Indiana Jones 2: The Adventure Continues
history: TT Games' LEGO Indiana Jones 2: The Adventure Continues (2009) covers the fourth film and rebuilds scenes from the earlier movies, on Wii and DS as well.

meta.name: LEGO Indiana Jones 2: The Adventure Continues

title: Pokemon HeartGold
history: A remake of Gold in which a chosen Pokemon walks behind you and Johto leads into Kanto.
lineup: This page is the 2009 DS remake, not Pokemon Gold.

title: Might and Magic Clash of Heroes
history: Capybara Games debuted the puzzle RPG Might and Magic Clash of Heroes (2009) on DS, matching colored troops in rows before an HD remake spread elsewhere.

meta.name: Might and Magic Clash of Heroes

title: SteamWorld Heist
history: Image and Form's turn-based crew shooter SteamWorld Heist (2015) makes ricochet shots the main trick, first on 3DS and later on Wii U.

title: DuckTales: Remastered
history: WayForward rebuilt Capcom's NES pogo-jump classic as DuckTales: Remastered (2013), and Wii U was one of the platforms for that remake.

title: Octodad: Dadliest Catch
history: Young Horses' physics comedy Octodad: Dadliest Catch (2014) asks you to puppeteer an octopus through ordinary chores, and a Wii U port followed PC.

title: Q.U.B.E: Director's Cut
history: Toxic Games expanded its first-person cube puzzles in Q.U.B.E: Director's Cut (2014), and that longer edition reached Wii U.

title: Shantae and the Pirate's Curse
history: WayForward shipped Shantae and the Pirate's Curse (2014) on 3DS and Wii U, a pirate-gear platformer in the half-genie series.

title: Teslagrad
history: Rain Games' wordless platformer Teslagrad (2013) uses magnetism inside a tower, and a Wii U port followed the PC release.

title: Back to Bed
history: Bedtime Digital's Back to Bed (2014) guides a sleepwalker across Escher-like paths by placing objects in his way.

title: Ziggurat
history: Milkstone Studios' first-person dungeon crawl Ziggurat (2014) randomizes floors and arms a wizard with wands, later appearing on Wii U.

title: BIT.TRIP Presents... Runner2: Future Legend of Rhythm Alien
history: Gaijin Games added branching paths timed to the soundtrack in BIT.TRIP Presents... Runner2: Future Legend of Rhythm Alien (2013), the auto-runner sequel, including a Wii U version.

meta.name: BIT.TRIP Presents... Runner2: Future Legend of Rhythm Alien

title: Shovel Knight
history: Yacht Club Games' Kickstarter homage Shovel Knight (2014) revives NES-style action, and it launched on Wii U and 3DS as well as PC.

title: The Cave
history: Ron Gilbert made The Cave (2013) at Double Fine, an adventure about seven wanderers exploring one cavern, Wii U included.

title: Unepic
history: A pizza-delivery worker trapped in a castle is the joke inside Unepic (2011), a PC Metroidvania parody later ported to the Wii U eShop.

title: The LEGO Movie - Videogame
history: TT Games retold the film in brick form as The LEGO Movie - Videogame (2014), released on Wii U and 3DS with the movie.

title: LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens
history: TT Games' brick version of the seventh Star Wars film, LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens (2016), adds scenes between the movie's beats on Wii U and 3DS.

meta.name: LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens

title: Road Redemption
history: Motorcycle combat in the spirit of Road Rash is the pitch of Road Redemption (2014), which first appeared through PC early access rather than on Wii U.

title: Lone Survivor: The Director's Cut
history: Jasper Byrne expanded his 2D survival horror as Lone Survivor: The Director's Cut, the 2012 game's larger edition, and a Wii U port followed.

title: LEGO Marvel's Avengers
history: The first two Avengers films get the brick treatment in TT Games' LEGO Marvel's Avengers (2016), which shipped on Wii U and 3DS.

title: Edge
history: The cube-rolling puzzle Edge (2011) grew out of an earlier mobile game, and later Wii U and 3DS versions carried that same rolling challenge.

title: LEGO Jurassic World
history: TT Games retold the first four Jurassic films as LEGO Jurassic World (2015), with releases on Wii U and 3DS.

title: FORCED
history: BetaDwarf's co-op arena game FORCED (2013) sends fighters through trials while spirit orbs rewrite their abilities.

title: Human Resource Machine
history: Tomorrow Corporation set the visual programming puzzles of Human Resource Machine (2015) in a dreary office, launching on Wii U alongside PC.

title: Axiom Verge
history: Tom Happ built the Metroidvania Axiom Verge (2015) alone, using glitches as weapons, and a Wii U version followed PC and PlayStation 4.

title: Pinball Arcade
history: FarSight Studios licensed real Williams and Bally machines for Pinball Arcade (2012), a digital pinball collection that included a Wii U version.

title: Batman: Arkham Origins Blackgate - Deluxe Edition
history: Armature's handheld Metroidvania moved to home consoles as Batman: Arkham Origins Blackgate - Deluxe Edition (2014), a Wii U edition with extra maps from the Blackgate side story.

meta.name: Batman: Arkham Origins Blackgate - Deluxe Edition

title: Minecraft: Story Mode
history: Telltale's episodic, choice-driven take on Minecraft is Minecraft: Story Mode (2015), and a Wii U release carried that season.

title: The Fall
history: Over the Moon Games' The Fall (2014) follows a combat suit's artificial intelligence, and that adventure was ported to Wii U.

title: OlliOlli
history: Roll7's skateboard game OlliOlli (2014) is all timed tricks and landings, born on PlayStation Vita and later ported to Wii U and 3DS.

title: Tumblestone
history: Pulling runs of matching blocks out of columns is the versus puzzle Tumblestone (2016), which launched with a Wii U version.

title: Mighty No. 9
history: Keiji Inafune's Kickstarter action game Mighty No. 9 (2016), developed with Inti Creates, was widely received as a troubled Mega Man successor, and it did reach Wii U and 3DS.

title: Toki Tori 2+
history: Two Tribes refused text tutorials in Toki Tori 2+ (2013), so each creature's effect has to be learned by trying it, and Wii U was a lead platform.

title: Lovely Planet
history: Tiny stages and a single-shot rhythm define Lovely Planet (2014), a brightly colored first-person game from quicktequila.

title: RUSH
history: Two Tribes' cube-routing puzzle RUSH (2010) uses conveyors and warps to reach colored exits, and a later Wii U version plays on the GamePad.

title: Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove
history: Yacht Club bundled the later knight campaigns with the original in Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove, gathering the 2014 game and its expansions on Wii U and 3DS.

title: Slender: The Arrival
history: Blue Isle's commercial horror game Slender: The Arrival (2013) followed the free Slender demo and the internet myth that spawned it.

title: Lego City Undercover
history: TT Fusion's open-city police comedy Lego City Undercover (2013) began as a Wii U exclusive and used the GamePad as a map before ports years later.

title: Sky Force Anniversary
history: Infinite Dreams rebuilt its vertical shooter as Sky Force Anniversary (2015), a score-chasing shmup that also reached Wii U.

title: Stick it to The Man!
history: Zoink's comedy platformer Stick it to The Man! (2013) gives the hero a spaghetti arm that slaps stickers onto other people's thoughts.

title: Volgarr the Viking
history: Ghosts 'n Goblins is the model for the harsh arcade platformer Volgarr the Viking (2013), which later showed up on the Wii U eShop.
Jeppe Carlsen's one-button platformer 140 (2013) pulses its geometry in time with the music.

title: Nihilumbra
history: BeautiFun Games' Nihilumbra (2012) paints colors onto the ground to change how it behaves, a mobile puzzle-platformer later brought to Wii U.

title: Xeodrifter
history: Renegade Kid's pocket Metroidvania Xeodrifter (2014) hops a drifter between tiny planets on 3DS and Wii U.

title: EARTHLOCK: Festival of Magic
history: Snowcastle Games' Norwegian turn-based RPG EARTHLOCK: Festival of Magic (2016) is that studio's debut project.

title: Whispering Willows
history: A girl who can step out of her body is the hook of the ghost-story adventure Whispering Willows (2014), which was ported to Wii U.

title: Freedom Planet
history: GalaxyTrail's fast platformer Freedom Planet (2014) is often set beside classic Sonic, and a Wii U port followed the PC release.

title: Bayonetta 2
history: A spectacle fighter published by Nintendo, about a witch who uses her hair as a weapon.
lineup: This page covers the Wii U original and the Switch version of the same game. Bayonetta 3 is a sequel.

title: Costume Quest 2
history: Double Fine returned to Halloween costume battles in Costume Quest 2 (2014), a sequel that shipped on Wii U.

title: Shantae: Risky's Revenge - Director's Cut
history: WayForward upgraded its DSiWare sequel for home consoles as Shantae: Risky's Revenge - Director's Cut (2014), including a Wii U version.

title: Electronic Super Joy
history: Electronic music backs the tough platforming of Electronic Super Joy (2013), an indie originally on PC and later on Wii U.

title: Super Mario Galaxy 2
history: A sequel that returns to planetoids and adds Yoshi, with a world map instead of the first game's observatory story.
lineup: It is its own Wii game, not a level pack inside the first Galaxy. This page does not claim a current re-release.

title: Nova-111
history: Turn-based steps share a grid with real-time blasts in Nova-111 (2015), an indie hybrid released on Wii U.

title: Ultratron
history: Puppy Games' twin-stick homage to Robotron is Ultratron, first on PC and later brought to Wii U by Curve Digital.

title: The Swindle
history: Size Five Games' steampunk heist The Swindle (2015) lays out each burglary differently before a final score, and a Wii U version was sold.

title: Pumped BMX +
history: Timed flips on a side-view bike course define Pumped BMX + (2015), an indie trick racer on the Wii U eShop.

title: CastleStorm
history: Zen Studios mixed castle defense with physics projectiles in CastleStorm (2013), and a Wii U version followed.

title: Shutshimi
history: Power-ups are absurd and temporary in the short horizontal shooter Shutshimi (2015), an indie arcade game on Wii U.

title: Chariot
history: Hauling a royal coffin through treasure caves is the co-op platforming of Chariot (2014), released on Wii U.

title: Sonic Lost World
history: Sonic Team built parkour on floating continents for the Wii U game Sonic Lost World (2013), and the 3DS version uses its own stages.

title: Year Walk
history: Simogo's folklore horror Year Walk (2013) began on phones, where a companion app held extra clues, and a Wii U port came later.

title: Frederic: Resurrection of Music
history: A revived Chopin stars in Forever Entertainment's rhythm game Frederic: Resurrection of Music (2012), a Polish indie later sold on Wii U.

title: Citizens of Earth
history: Recruiting ordinary townspeople as party members is the joke of the turn-based RPG Citizens of Earth (2015), on Wii U and 3DS.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword
history: A sky of islands above a surface you unlock in regions, played with motion sword swings.
lineup: The motion-sword adventure that opens on Skyloft starts on this page. Skyward Sword HD on Switch is a separate page.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword

title: STARWHAL
history: Local multiplayer narwhals poke each other in space in STARWHAL (2014), a couch game that included a Wii U version.

title: FIFA 13
history: EA Sports brought FIFA 13 (2012) to Wii U in that console's launch window, with an edition that was not the HD consoles' feature set.

title: Guitar Hero Live
history: FreeStyleGames restarted the series as Guitar Hero Live (2015), using first-person live-action crowds and a new guitar instead of the old five-color notes, Wii U included.

title: Ittle Dew
history: Ludosity's short dungeon-puzzle adventure Ittle Dew (2013) is a Swedish homage to classic top-down quests, released on Wii U.

title: Knytt Underground
history: Nifflas' long subterranean wander Knytt Underground (2012) favors exploration over combat, and it reached the Wii U eShop.

title: Spy Chameleon - RGB Agent
history: Changing color to stay hidden is the entire puzzle of Spy Chameleon - RGB Agent (2014), a Wii U eShop release about a chameleon agent.

title: Shantae: Half-Genie Hero
history: WayForward's Kickstarter return Shantae: Half-Genie Hero (2016) brought the half-genie back in HD, and Wii U was one of the launch platforms.

title: Ballpoint Universe - Infinite
history: Ink on paper is the look of the shooter Ballpoint Universe - Infinite (2013), a ballpoint-styled arcade game that received a Wii U release.

title: Puddle
history: Tilting a bead of liquid through machinery is the physics puzzle Puddle (2012), which later reached the Wii U eShop.

title: Scribblenauts Unmasked: A DC Comics Adventure
history: 5th Cell set its word-summoning puzzles inside the DC universe for Scribblenauts Unmasked: A DC Comics Adventure (2013), on Wii U and 3DS.

meta.name: Scribblenauts Unmasked: A DC Comics Adventure

title: Plantera
history: Gentle plant-raising fills the small gardening sim Plantera (2016), released on 3DS and Wii U.

title: Space Hulk
history: Games Workshop's squad board game became Space Hulk (2013), with Terminators clearing a derelict ship, and a Wii U edition was released.

title: Gravity Badgers
history: Wales Interactive's Gravity Badgers (2013) launches badgers through caves by flipping gravity, a physics puzzle on the Wii U eShop.

title: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD
history: A higher-resolution sail across the same sea, with a quicker boat and the same cartoon look.
lineup: The Swift Sail and a sharper Toon Link sea are the reissue on this page. The 2002 GameCube original has its own page.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD

title: Mutant Mudds Deluxe
history: Renegade Kid expanded its 3DS platformer as Mutant Mudds Deluxe (2013), adding levels for a Wii U release of that deluxe set.

title: Mario Kart 8
history: Anti-gravity tracks and a living-room roster on Wii U, before the Switch Deluxe edition.
lineup: This page is the Wii U original. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is its own Switch entry.

title: Kung Fu Panda: Showdown of Legendary Legends
history: DreamWorks characters brawl on floating stages in the platform fighter Kung Fu Panda: Showdown of Legendary Legends (2015), released on Wii U and 3DS.

meta.name: Kung Fu Panda: Showdown of Legendary Legends

title: Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze
history: Cold-themed levels and a Dixie partner in the Country game Retro made after Returns.
lineup: This page names both the 2014 Wii U original and the later Switch port of the same game.

title: Dungeons & Dragons: Chronicles of Mystara
history: Capcom bundled its arcade beat-em-ups Tower of Doom and Shadow over Mystara as Dungeons & Dragons: Chronicles of Mystara (2013), and that collection reached Wii U.

title: Quest of Dungeons
history: A compact roguelike crawl, Quest of Dungeons (2014) generates small dungeons and shipped on Wii U and 3DS.

title: Shiftlings
history: Two aliens share one body in the co-op game Shiftlings (2015), sold on the Wii U eShop.

title: Girls Like Robots
history: Adult Swim Games published the seating-chart puzzle Girls Like Robots (2012), later brought to Wii U.

title: Tekken Tag Tournament 2
history: Namco's tag-team fighter Tekken Tag Tournament 2 (2012) pairs a huge roster, and the Wii U version added modes the arcade release lacked.

title: Mario Kart DS
history: Mission mode and online play on a handheld, with courses that use both screens for a map.
lineup: It is the DS Mario Kart, between Super Circuit and Mario Kart 7.

title: New Super Mario Bros.
history: A return to side-scrolling Mario on two screens, with a wall jump and a huge mushroom.
lineup: It restarted 2D Mario on DS and led to the Wii, Wii U, and later Deluxe games.

title: Jones On Fire
history: A firefighter outruns the blaze in the short runner Jones On Fire (2015), an indie sold on the Wii U eShop.

title: The Book of Unwritten Tales 2
history: KING Art's comedy point-and-click sequel The Book of Unwritten Tales 2 (2015) followed the PC adventure with a Wii U port.

title: Dracula's Legacy
history: Jetdogs Studios' hidden-object adventure Dracula's Legacy (2015) uses a vampire theme, and a Wii U eShop port followed the PC release.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass
history: Touch-screen sailing and a temple you revisit on a timer, in a sequel to Wind Waker's sea.
lineup: It is the DS Zelda that follows Link after The Wind Waker.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass

title: Angry Video Game Nerd Adventures
history: The web-series host becomes a deliberately harsh retro platformer in Angry Video Game Nerd Adventures (2013), released on Wii U and 3DS.

title: Super Mario 3D World
history: Clear courses, a cat suit, and a pace closer to 2D Mario than to the sandbox 3D games.
lineup: This page covers the 2013 Wii U game and the later Switch edition, which adds Bowser's Fury as an extra story rather than a replacement.

title: Woah Dave!
history: Choice Provisions' one-screen arcade scuffle Woah Dave! (2014) is a small multiplayer throwback on Wii U and 3DS.

title: Master Reboot
history: Wales Interactive set the first-person horror game Master Reboot (2013) inside a machine that stores memories, and released it on Wii U.

title: forma.8
history: A small probe crosses an alien surface with no dialogue in forma.8 (2017), an exploration game brought to Wii U.

title: Ninja Pizza Girl
history: Delivery runs and schoolyard cruelty share the momentum platformer Ninja Pizza Girl (2015), an Australian indie on Wii U.

title: Bridge Constructor Playground
history: Stress-testing homemade spans with vehicles is the sandbox Bridge Constructor Playground (2012), a physics playground from the bridge-building series on Wii U.

title: Armikrog
history: The Neverhood team returned with clay animation in the Kickstarted point-and-click Armikrog (2015), later sold on Wii U.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks
history: A train replaces the boat, and Zelda is a spirit partner rather than a distant goal.
lineup: It is the second DS Zelda in the Wind Waker's art style, and a different adventure from Phantom Hourglass.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks

title: Letter Quest: Remastered
history: Bacon Bandit Games mixes spelling with monster battles in Letter Quest: Remastered (2016), a word RPG whose remaster reached Wii U.

title: Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker
history: Diaphragm puzzles: rotate a small diorama and walk Toad to the star without jumping.
lineup: It grew out of Super Mario 3D World levels. This page names the Wii U original and the Switch port.

title: 1001 Spikes
history: Nicalis published the cruel temple platformer 1001 Spikes (2014), a spike-filled arcade challenge on Wii U and 3DS.

title: The Deer God
history: Pixel-art reincarnation as a deer is the premise of The Deer God (2015), a side-scroller released on Wii U among other platforms.

title: Injustice: Gods Among Us
history: NetherRealm's DC Comics fighter Injustice: Gods Among Us (2013) reached Wii U with the same one-on-one battles as the other consoles.

title: Severed
