history: Drinkbox Studios built the first-person slash adventure Severed (2016) for touch controls, and released it on Wii U and 3DS.

title: Tengami
history: Nyamyam styled the puzzle adventure Tengami (2014) as a pop-up paper book, a Wii U eShop release.

title: Tetrobot and Co.
history: Swing Swing Submarine's block-pushing puzzle Tetrobot and Co. (2013) was ported to Wii U after its other digital releases.

title: A World of Keflings
history: NinjaBee's toy-like god game A World of Keflings (2010) has you helping tiny villagers by hand, and a Wii U version followed the Xbox original.

title: Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams - Director's Cut
history: Black Forest Games revived the 1980s series with Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams - Director's Cut, a hard fantasy platformer whose expanded cut reached Wii U in 2014.

meta.name: Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams - Director's Cut

title: Extreme Exorcism
history: Your previous life replays as a ghost in the party game Extreme Exorcism (2015), a local multiplayer idea sold on Wii U.

title: Electronic Super Joy: Groove City
history: A new city of music-driven stages continues the tough platforming in Electronic Super Joy: Groove City (2014), including a Wii U version.

title: Super Smash Bros.
history: Nintendo characters knock each other off floating arenas in a four-player fighting game.
lineup: It is the first Smash Bros., the Nintendo 64 original of a series that grew on every home console after.

title: Pirate Pop Plus
history: 13AM Games dressed a bubble-popping arcade game like a tiny handheld in Pirate Pop Plus (2016), on 3DS and Wii U.

title: Zombie Defense
history: Placing units against incoming waves is the defense game Zombie Defense (2010), later sold on the Wii U eShop.

title: Cubemen 2
history: 3 Sprockets' blocky strategy game Cubemen 2 (2013) lets cube squads attack each other's bases, and Nnooo brought cross-platform matches to Wii U.

title: Super Toy Cars
history: Miniature cars race household-sized tracks in Super Toy Cars (2014), an indie racer on the Wii U eShop.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess HD
history: The 2006 adventure rebuilt for a higher resolution, with amiibo extras that the original did not have.
lineup: The wolf-Link adventure, rebuilt with amiibo caves and a sharper Hyrule, is the reissue on this page. The Wii and GameCube original is a different page.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess HD

title: WARRIORS OROCHI 3 Ultimate
history: Koei Tecmo folded Dynasty Warriors and Samurai Warriors into the giant crossover WARRIORS OROCHI 3 Ultimate (2013), and the Wii U edition was part of that Ultimate set.

title: Mahjong Deluxe 3
history: Solitaire tile-matching on the Wii U eShop is Mahjong Deluxe 3 (2016), a late casual release for that shop.

title: Lone Survivor
history: Jasper Byrne's 2D survival horror Lone Survivor (2012) is the original PC release, later expanded by a director's cut.

title: New Super Mario Bros. U
history: A side-scrolling Mario that uses the GamePad for boost blocks when a second player wants them.
lineup: Boost blocks on the GamePad are the Wii U idea on this page. The Switch package that adds New Super Luigi U has its own page.

title: Level 22: Gary’s Misadventure - 2016 Edition
history: Sneaking an office worker past patrolling managers is the top-down stealth puzzle Level 22: Gary’s Misadventure - 2016 Edition.

title: LEGO DIMENSIONS
history: TT Games' toys-to-life kit LEGO DIMENSIONS (2015) drops many Warner licenses into one brick world, and Wii U had a starter set.

title: The Walking Dead: Survival Instinct
history: Activision's first-person spinoff The Walking Dead: Survival Instinct (2013) is separate from Telltale's episodic series and was widely panned, including a Wii U release.

title: Just Dance 2016
history: Ubisoft introduced the Just Dance Unlimited streaming library with Just Dance 2016 in 2015, while a Wii U disc still held an on-disc tracklist.

title: Super Mario Maker
history: A tool for building and sharing 2D Mario stages in the styles of several earlier games.
lineup: The first course editor that let players upload 2D Mario stages in classic styles is this page. Super Mario Maker 2 on Switch is a sequel, not this tool.

title: Shiny The Firefly
history: Padaone Games ported the mobile garden game Shiny The Firefly to Wii U, where a firefly's glow both leads the way and draws danger.

title: Sonic Generations
history: Classic and modern Sonics share Sonic Generations (2011) for the series anniversary, and the 3DS version uses its own stages rather than the console levels.

title: VVVVVV
history: Terry Cavanagh's VVVVVV (2010) flips gravity instead of jumping, a PC platformer later ported to 3DS and Switch.

title: SteamWorld Dig 2
history: Image and Form sent a new robot into a larger mine in SteamWorld Dig 2 (2017), a dig-and-upgrade sequel on 3DS and Switch.

title: Punch Club
history: Lazy Bear Games' pixel-art boxing manager Punch Club (2016) is about training and fight nights, and it reached 3DS.

title: FIFA 15
history: EA Sports' FIFA 15 (2014) is that season's football sim, and the 3DS edition is a simplified handheld, not the Ignite-engine console game.

title: Mega Man Legacy Collection / ロックマン クラシックス コレクション
history: Capcom gathered the first six Mega Man games, plus extra challenges, in Mega Man Legacy Collection / ロックマン クラシックス コレクション (2015), and a 3DS version followed the console release.

meta.name: Mega Man Legacy Collection / ロックマン クラシックス コレクション

title: NightSky
history: Nifflas rolls a silhouetted orb through quiet stages in NightSky (2011), a puzzle later brought to 3DS.

title: Retro City Rampage DX
history: Brian Provinciano's 8-bit open-city crime parody Retro City Rampage DX (2012) expanded on 3DS as the DX edition of his PC original.

title: Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater
history: Hideo Kojima's jungle-survival stealth game Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater (2004) began on PlayStation 2, and a 3DS version later carried that same mission.

title: DRAGON QUEST XI: Echoes of an Elusive Age
history: Square Enix's mainline RPG DRAGON QUEST XI: Echoes of an Elusive Age (2017) launched in Japan on 3DS beside PlayStation 4.

meta.name: DRAGON QUEST XI: Echoes of an Elusive Age

title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Trilogy
history: Capcom's Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Trilogy packages the first three courtroom games, the cases that began on the Game Boy Advance.

title: Ghostbusters: The Video Game
history: Dan Aykroyd and Harold Ramis helped write Ghostbusters: The Video Game (2009), often treated as a third film, while the Wii version is a separate on-rails take.

title: LEGO Pirates of the Caribbean: The Video Game
history: TT Games retold four films in brick form as LEGO Pirates of the Caribbean: The Video Game (2011), shipping on Wii, DS, and 3DS.

meta.name: LEGO Pirates of the Caribbean: The Video Game

title: Gauntlet
history: The four-hero dungeon crawl that Midway made famous in arcades lends its name to Gauntlet (2009), a DS-era release rather than the 1985 cabinet.

title: Marvel: Ultimate Alliance 2
history: The comics' registration conflict becomes a team brawler in Marvel: Ultimate Alliance 2 (2009), with separate Wii and DS versions of that Marvel game.

title: Ys I & II Chronicles
history: Falcom's remake package Ys I & II Chronicles bundles the first two Ys action RPGs, and that Chronicles edition is associated with PSP rather than a DS launch.

title: Zuma's Revenge!
history: PopCap's sequel Zuma's Revenge! (2009) continues the frog-and-marble matching of Zuma, firing colored balls into rolling chains.

title: Pokemon Pearl
history: The paired Sinnoh version, with a different legendary and a different wild roster.
lineup: It is the other 2006 DS edition, not the Switch remake.

title: Pokemon Black
history: A region that questions whether trainers should catch creatures at all, with seasons on the calendar.
lineup: Black is one half of the 2010 pair. Black 2 is a sequel, not a third version.

title: TRON: Evolution - The Video Game
history: Propaganda Games tied TRON: Evolution - The Video Game (2010) to TRON: Legacy, and the DS release is a separate handheld from the console action game.

title: Cut the Rope
history: ZeptoLab's Cut the Rope (2010) swings candy to a small monster by slicing ropes, and DS and 3DS ports followed the phone original.

title: Pokemon Platinum
history: The third Sinnoh version, with a distortion world and a fuller story.
lineup: It is the refined DS edition of the fourth generation.

title: Tom Clancy's EndWar
history: Voice commands made Ubisoft's near-future strategy game Tom Clancy's EndWar (2008) famous on consoles, while the DS version is a separate handheld campaign.

title: Pokemon White 2
history: The paired sequel to White, sharing Black 2's two-years-later Unova.
lineup: It is the other 2012 DS sequel.

title: Myst
history: Cyan's pre-rendered island puzzle Myst (1993) was a point-and-click landmark on home computers, and a DS port arrived years after the Macintosh original.

title: Puzzle Kingdoms
history: Infinite Interactive's strategy-puzzle hybrid Puzzle Kingdoms (2009) is a DS cousin of Puzzle Quest, mixing match puzzles with a kingdom map.

title: Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days
history: Square Enix told a mission-based chapter of the series on DS as Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days (2009), later folded into HD collections.

title: Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars
history: Rockstar Leeds' top-down DS original Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars (2009) is a Liberty City crime story praised far above a typical handheld spinoff.

title: Carcassonne
history: The tile-laying board game came to DS as Carcassonne (2010), scoring cities, roads, and fields the way the tabletop original does.

title: Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors
history: Escape-room puzzles on a sinking ship, with story branches that need more than one ending.
lineup: It is the DS original of the Zero Escape series.

meta.name: 999: Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors

title: The Lord of the Rings: Conquest
history: Pandemic set the battle game The Lord of the Rings: Conquest (2009) in the film trilogy's wars, and the DS edition is a smaller companion to the console release.

meta.name: The Lord of the Rings: Conquest

title: N+
history: Metanet's punishing jumper reached DS as N+ (2008), an expanded edition of N with a large stack of user levels.

title: Dragon's Lair HD
history: Don Bluth's laserdisc arcade cartoon returned as Dragon's Lair HD (2009), the quick-time fantasy played as animated scenes rather than free movement.

title: Super Mario 64 DS
history: Four characters replay the castle, with touch controls and extra stars the Nintendo 64 game did not have.
lineup: It is the DS reworking. The 1996 Nintendo 64 game remains its own page.

title: Professor Layton and the Curious Village
history: A gentleman puzzle hunt wrapped in a village mystery.
lineup: It is the first Layton game in the DS line, published by Nintendo in the West.

meta.name: Professor Layton and the Curious Village

title: 7 Wonders II
history: MumboJumbo's tile-matcher 7 Wonders II (2007) is the sequel in that casual line of ancient-wonder puzzles.

title: Puzzler World
history: Crosswords, word searches, and logic grids from the Puzzler brand fill the DS compilation Puzzler World (2009).

title: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective
history: A dead man possesses objects to rewind the four minutes before a death.
lineup: It is Shu Takumi's DS puzzle adventure, from the Ace Attorney director, and its own story.

title: WWE SmackDown vs. RAW 2010
history: THQ and Yuke's shipped the annual wrestling sim WWE SmackDown vs. RAW 2010 in 2009, DS edition included.

title: FIFA 08
history: EA Sports' football season FIFA 08 arrived in 2007, with a DS edition beside the console game.

title: Iron Man
history: Sega's action tie-in to the first Marvel film is Iron Man (2008), and a DS version was part of that licensed set.

title: KINGDOM HEARTS Re:coded
history: Square Enix remade its mobile Kingdom Hearts story for DS as KINGDOM HEARTS Re:coded (2010), a journal-data chapter later compiled in HD.

title: Mario and Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story
history: AlphaDream split the DS role-playing game Mario and Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story (2009) between the brothers and a giant Bowser they travel inside.

meta.name: Mario and Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story

title: Lego Rock Band
history: Harmonix and Traveller's Tales aimed Lego Rock Band (2009) at younger players, and the DS edition is a simpler rhythm game than the console instruments.

title: Zoo Tycoon
history: Blue Fang and Microsoft's zoo-building sim Zoo Tycoon (2001) is a PC management game, distinct from the later DS spinoff that reused the name.

title: Dark Void Zero
history: Capcom released the 8-bit side-scroller Dark Void Zero (2010) on DSiWare as a retro prequel tied to the bigger Dark Void shooter.

title: 7 Wonders of the Ancient World
history: MumboJumbo themed the tile-matcher 7 Wonders of the Ancient World (2007) on ancient monuments, and a DS version joined the casual PC original.

title: Animal Crossing: Wild World
history: A pocket town you can visit online, smaller than the GameCube village and always in your bag.
lineup: It is the DS Animal Crossing, between the GameCube original and City Folk.

title: WWE Smackdown vs. RAW 2009
history: THQ's wrestling season WWE Smackdown vs. RAW 2009 arrived in 2008, with a DS edition of that annual.

title: Spider-Man: Friend or Foe
history: Activision's lighter team brawler Spider-Man: Friend or Foe (2007) is a kid-aimed Spider-Man, and a DS version shipped with it.

title: Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney
history: Capcom introduced a new defense attorney on DS in Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney (2007), the fourth main courtroom game after the Phoenix Wright trilogy.

title: The Incredible Hulk (2008)
history: The Marvel film named in the title received the action tie-in The Incredible Hulk (2008), and a DS version shipped with the other editions.

title: Madden NFL 09
history: EA's Madden NFL 09 put Brett Favre on the cover in a Packers jersey for the 2008 season, then issued a Jets cover after he changed teams. The Nintendo DS cart is that year's handheld edition, not a later Madden.

title: Disney Bolt
history: The animated film about a TV dog got the platform tie-in Disney Bolt (2008), and a DS version shipped in that movie season.

title: The World Ends with You
history: Two-screen battles in Shibuya, fashion pins for powers, and a week-long deadline.
lineup: It is the DS original. Later ports and a sequel exist; this page is the 2007 handheld game.

meta.name: The World Ends With You DS

title: Secret Files 2: Puritas Cordis
history: Animation Arts followed Tunguska with the point-and-click sequel Secret Files 2: Puritas Cordis (2009), including a DS port of that mystery.

title: Puzzle Quest 2
history: Infinite Interactive's match-puzzle RPG Puzzle Quest 2 (2010) continues the Puzzle Quest idea, and a DS version was part of the release.

title: Thrillville: Off the Rails
history: Frontier's theme-park sequel Thrillville: Off the Rails (2007) mixes roller-coaster building with minigames, including a DS version.

title: Professor Layton and the Diabolical Box
history: Level-5's second DS puzzle adventure Professor Layton and the Diabolical Box (2009) followed the curious village with another suitcase of riddles, known in Europe as Pandora's Box.

meta.name: Professor Layton and the Diabolical Box

title: 4 Elements
history: Matching elemental tokens to clear boards is the casual puzzle 4 Elements (2010), and editions were sold on DS and 3DS.

title: Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow
history: Soma returns, and magic seals ask you to draw on the touch screen to finish a boss.
lineup: It is the DS sequel to Aria of Sorrow.

title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1
history: EA turned the seventh film into the cover shooter Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1 (2010), a sharp break from the earlier Potter adventures, with a DS version.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1

title: Ace Attorney Investigations - Miles Edgeworth
history: Capcom moved the courtroom series onto investigation scenes with Ace Attorney Investigations - Miles Edgeworth (2009), a DS game starring the prosecutor instead of the defense.

title: Sudoku
history: The pencil-and-paper number grid comes to DS as Sudoku (2008), one of many handheld editions of a logic puzzle that long predates Nintendo.

title: Madden NFL 08
history: EA's Madden NFL 08 (2007) still shipped on GameCube as well as DS, among the last Madden seasons on Nintendo's disc console.

title: Mario & Luigi: Partners in Time
history: Adult brothers team with their baby selves across two screens.
lineup: It is the DS follow-up to Superstar Saga.

title: Sonic Colors
history: Alien Wisps that change moves define Sonic Team's Sonic Colors (2010), and the DS version is its own stage set rather than a shrunk Wii port.

title: Professor Layton and the Unwound Future
history: Level-5 closed its original DS puzzle trilogy with Professor Layton and the Unwound Future (2010), known in Europe as Professor Layton and the Lost Future.

meta.name: Professor Layton and the Unwound Future

title: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky
history: Chunsoft's expanded third version of the Explorers story is Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky (2009), adding episodes on top of Time and Darkness for DS.

meta.name: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky

title: WALL-E: The Video Game
history: THQ's tie-in to the Pixar film is WALL-E: The Video Game (2008), and the DS edition was part of that licensed set.

title: Puzzle Quest: Galactrix
history: Infinite Interactive moved the Puzzle Quest formula onto a hex grid for the sci-fi spinoff Puzzle Quest: Galactrix (2009), including a DS release.

title: Pokémon Ranger
history: Capturing with stylus loops, rather than battles, is the DS spinoff Pokémon Ranger (2006), the first game in that handheld line.

title: Disney•Pixar Cars 2: The Video Game
history: The spy sequel's racing tie-in Disney•Pixar Cars 2: The Video Game (2011) shipped with DS and 3DS versions alongside the consoles.

title: Sonic & SEGA Racing
history: Sega characters fill the DS kart game Sonic & SEGA Racing (2010), a handheld cousin of Sumo Digital's All-Stars Racing.

title: Shrek the Third
history: The third DreamWorks film received the tie-in Shrek the Third (2007), and a DS version was part of that licensed set.

title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 2
history: EA's cover-shooter tie-in to the eighth film is Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 2 (2011), with a DS version beside the consoles.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 2

title: Spider-Man: Edge of Time
history: The modern hero shares Spider-Man: Edge of Time (2011) with Spider-Man 2099, and the DS and 3DS releases are separate from the HD console game.

title: Disney Alice in Wonderland
history: Tim Burton's film received the tie-in Disney Alice in Wonderland (2010), and a DS version launched in that movie's season.

title: FIFA Street 3
history: EA dropped simulation rules for trick-heavy street football in FIFA Street 3 (2008), and a DS version carried that arcade spinoff.

title: World of Zoo
history: THQ's animal-care sim World of Zoo (2009) plays closer to toy creatures than to the older Zoo Tycoon management model, with a DS release.

title: Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia
history: Koji Igarashi's DS action-RPG Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia (2008) was the last of the handheld search-action Castlevanias before the series changed direction.

title: Superman Returns: The Videogame
history: EA's open-city tie-in to the film is Superman Returns: The Videogame (2006), and a separate DS game shipped with that license.

title: Band Hero
history: Activision's pop-leaning Guitar Hero spinoff Band Hero (2009) has a DS edition that is a simpler rhythm game than the console band set.

title: Labyrinth
history: Ravensburger's shifting-maze board game came to DS as Labyrinth (2008), sliding tiles to open a path.

title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
history: CD Projekt Red's open-world RPG The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (2015) won a pile of year-end awards, and a demanding Switch port followed in a later year.

title: Portal
history: Valve's 2007 puzzle game Portal uses a gun that links two holes in space, and the Companion Collection later brought it to Switch.

title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
history: Bethesda's open-world fantasy The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011) became one of the most re-released RPGs of its decade, including a 2017 Switch port.

title: BioShock Infinite
history: Irrational Games set BioShock Infinite (2013) in the floating city of Columbia, a sky-line shooter later included in the Switch collection.

title: Limbo
history: Playdead's silhouette puzzle-platformer Limbo (2010) was a breakout indie, and a Switch port followed the original releases.

title: DOOM (2016)
history: id Software rebooted the series as a fast, aggressive shooter in DOOM (2016), and Panic Button later brought that campaign to Switch.

title: Cyberpunk 2077
history: CD Projekt Red's Night City RPG Cyberpunk 2077 (2020) launched in a famously broken state and was rebuilt over years of patches.

title: Warframe
history: Digital Extremes' free-to-play squad shooter Warframe (2013) has run as a live game for years, and a Switch version joined it.

title: Rocket League
history: Psyonix turned cars playing soccer into Rocket League (2015), a surprise hit sequel to Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars, later on Switch.

title: Batman: Arkham Knight
history: Rocksteady closed its Arkham series with Batman: Arkham Knight (2015), built around the Batmobile on PC and that generation's HD consoles.

title: Apex Legends
history: Respawn's free squad shooter Apex Legends (2019) spun a battle royale out of the Titanfall universe.

title: Hollow Knight
history: Team Cherry's hand-drawn bug kingdom Hollow Knight (2017) became a landmark indie, and the Switch version was part of its wide release.

title: The Walking Dead: Season 1
history: Telltale's choice-driven adaptation of the comic, The Walking Dead: Season 1 (2012), revived the studio's reputation and later reached Switch.

title: Little Nightmares
history: Tarsier Studios' Little Nightmares (2017) shrinks the player inside a giant, hostile ship, and a Switch port followed.

title: BioShock 2
history: 2K Marin put the player in a Big Daddy's suit for BioShock 2 (2010), a return to Rapture after the original.

title: Stardew Valley
history: ConcernedApe built the farming life sim Stardew Valley (2016) largely alone, and the Switch version became one of its biggest platforms.

title: Hotline Miami
history: Dennaton's top-down violence puzzle Hotline Miami (2012) is scored like a club track, and a Switch port came later.

title: BioShock Remastered
history: Irrational's 2007 Rapture shooter was polished up as BioShock Remastered (2016), and that remaster later sat inside the Switch collection.

title: Outlast
history: Red Barrels' Outlast (2013) is a horror game about filming an asylum with a camcorder and no weapons, later ported to Switch.

title: Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice
history: Ninja Theory developed Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice (2017) with mental-health advisors, and a Switch port followed the PC and console release.

title: Hitman: Absolution
history: IO Interactive made Hitman: Absolution (2012) a more linear Agent 47 story, the follow-up to Blood Money before the World of Assassination reboot.

title: L.A. Noire
history: Team Bondi's detective game L.A. Noire (2011), published by Rockstar, is famous for facial-capture interrogations, and it was later ported to Switch.

title: Metro: Last Light Redux
history: 4A Games' post-nuclear sequel was cleaned up as Metro: Last Light Redux (2014), part of the Redux pair later brought to Switch.

title: Metro 2033 Redux
history: 4A Games rebuilt its Moscow-metro shooter on a newer engine as Metro 2033 Redux (2014), and that Redux edition later reached Switch.

title: Hades
history: Supergiant's roguelike Hades (2020) left early access to huge acclaim, built around repeated escape attempts, and the finished game launched on Switch at the same time.

title: BioShock 2 Remastered
history: The same remaster wave that updated the first Rapture game produced BioShock 2 Remastered (2016), a cleaner release of 2K Marin's sequel.

title: NieR:Automata
history: PlatinumGames and director Yoko Taro made NieR:Automata (2017) the series' breakout action RPG, later ported to Switch.

title: Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout
history: Mediatonic's obstacle-course brawl Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout (2020) became a costume knockout show and later went free-to-play, including on Switch.

title: Resident Evil 7: Biohazard
history: Capcom switched the series to a first-person haunted house with Resident Evil 7: Biohazard (2017), a softer reboot after years of action-heavy sequels.

title: Bastion
history: Supergiant's debut Bastion (2011) is an action RPG whose narrator comments on what the player just did, later ported to Switch.

title: Paladins
history: Hi-Rez Studios' free hero shooter Paladins (2016) joined the wave of class-based team games, with a Switch version following.

title: ARK: Survival Evolved
history: Studio Wildcard's dinosaur survival sandbox ARK: Survival Evolved (2015) is enormous on PC, and the Switch port was a notably compromised version of that world.

title: Cities: Skylines
history: Colossal Order's city builder Cities: Skylines (2015) picked up players after SimCity's troubled relaunch, and a Switch port followed.

title: Undertale
history: Toby Fox's RPG Undertale (2015) lets players spare monsters instead of fighting them, a surprise hit later brought to Switch.

title: Unturned
history: Teen developer Nelson Sexton released the free zombie survival game Unturned (2014), which spread widely on PC.

title: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons
history: Josef Fares' adventure Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons (2013) puts one brother on each thumbstick, and a Switch port followed the original consoles.

meta.name: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons

title: Titan Attacks!
history: Puppy Games' score-attack blaster Titan Attacks! (2012) pays homage to Space Invaders, and Curve later published it on 3DS.

title: Castlevania: Lords of Shadow - Mirror of Fate
history: MercurySteam's side-view adventure Castlevania: Lords of Shadow - Mirror of Fate (2013) debuted on 3DS inside the Lords of Shadow continuity, with HD ports afterward.

meta.name: Castlevania: Lords of Shadow - Mirror of Fate

title: Need for Speed: The Run
history: EA's cross-country race against the clock is Need for Speed: The Run (2011), and the Wii and 3DS editions are separate from the HD drive.

title: Zero Escape: Zero Time Dilemma
history: Kotaro Uchikoshi closed the Zero Escape trilogy with Zero Escape: Zero Time Dilemma (2016), a 3DS, Vita, and PC adventure of locked-room choices.

title: URBAN TRIAL FREESTYLE
history: Obstacle courses and crashes define the bike-trials game URBAN TRIAL FREESTYLE (2013), which received a 3DS version.

title: Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon
history: Inti Creates made the 8-bit-style action game Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon (2018) with Koji Igarashi producing, and a 3DS version was released.

title: Streets of Rage 2
history: Sega's Streets of Rage 2 (1992) is the Genesis brawler usually ranked as the high point of that trilogy, later reissued on Virtual Console for Wii and 3DS.

title: Pokémon X, Y
history: Game Freak took the main series fully into 3D with Pokémon X, Y (2013), introducing Mega Evolution on 3DS.

title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds
history: It revisits the shape of A Link to the Past, then lets Link become a painting and move along walls.
lineup: It is a Nintendo 3DS Zelda. That system's digital catalog is closed, and this page does not invent a current listing.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds

title: Garfield Kart
history: Microids put the comic-strip cat in a budget kart racer, Garfield Kart (2013), on 3DS.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 3D
history: Grezzo remade the Nintendo 64 adventure for 3DS as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 3D (2011), updated graphics and gyro aiming included.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 3D

title: Pokémon Sun, Moon
history: Game Freak replaced gyms with island trials in the Alola games Pokémon Sun, Moon (2016), a 3DS pair built around Z-Moves.

title: Pokémon Alpha Sapphire, Omega Ruby
history: Game Freak remade the Hoenn pair as Pokémon Alpha Sapphire, Omega Ruby (2014), bringing Mega Evolution back to those 3DS journeys.

title: Super Mario 3D Land
history: Stereoscopic depth and a Tanooki suit define Nintendo's 3DS platformer Super Mario 3D Land (2011), an early showcase for the handheld.

title: Wheel of Fortune
history: The television word-puzzle show came to DS as Wheel of Fortune (2010), spinning a wheel and filling in letters.

title: Kirby Super Star Ultra
history: An expanded remake of the SNES Kirby Super Star, with extra games on the cart.
lineup: Ultra adds Helper to Hero and other extra games on top of the SNES Kirby Super Star anthology. The SNES original has its own entry.

title: WarioWare: Touched!
history: Intelligent Systems built WarioWare: Touched! (2004) around the DS touch screen and microphone, the first WarioWare made for that handheld.

title: You Don't Know Jack HD
history: Jackbox revived its sarcastic trivia show for touch screens as You Don't Know Jack HD (2011), a different product from the older console Jack games and not a DS original.

title: Jagged Alliance
history: Sir-Tech's turn-based mercenary tactics game Jagged Alliance (1994) began on PC, long before any handheld version reused the name.

title: Hotel Dusk: Room 215
history: Cing's mystery Hotel Dusk: Room 215 (2007) is played with the DS held sideways like a book, a point-and-click set in a rundown hotel.

title: SEGA Superstars Tennis
history: Sumo Digital filled SEGA Superstars Tennis (2008) with Sega characters whose minigames nod at their own series, including a DS version.

title: Mario Party DS
history: Hudson brought the series' board and minigames to the dual screen in Mario Party DS (2007), with many events built around the stylus.

title: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin
history: Konami's DS search-action game Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin (2006) lets two heroes swap in and out during the castle crawl.

title: Brain Challenge
history: Gameloft's set of short mental exercises Brain Challenge (2008) is a DS brain-training package from the boom that followed Nintendo's own series.

title: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon
history: Intelligent Systems remade the first Fire Emblem for DS as Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon (2009), the Marth story western players had mostly missed.

title: Nintendogs: Labrador & Friends
history: One of the three DS launch packs, Nintendogs: Labrador & Friends (2005) uses the touch screen and microphone to care for virtual puppies.

title: Sonic Rush
history: Dimps brought a boost dash and tall dual-screen stages to DS in Sonic Rush (2005), a Sonic built for that handheld.

title: Iron Man 2
history: The second Marvel film received Sega's action tie-in Iron Man 2 (2010), again with a DS game alongside the consoles.

title: Dragon's Lair II: Time Warp
history: Don Bluth's laserdisc sequel Dragon's Lair II: Time Warp (1991) continues the animated quick-time adventures that began with Dragon's Lair.

title: Juiced 2: Hot Import Nights
history: THQ's street-racing sequel Juiced 2: Hot Import Nights (2007) includes a DS edition made for that release.

title: Puzzle Chronicles
history: Another match-puzzle RPG from the Puzzle Quest family, Puzzle Chronicles (2010) shipped with a DS version.

title: Rhythm Heaven
history: Short rhythm scenes that use a tap, with a flick that the DS hardware made the joke.
lineup: It is the DS Rhythm Heaven, between the GBA game that stayed in Japan and the later Wii and 3DS entries.

title: Metroid Prime Hunters
history: A bounty-hunter shooter on two screens, with local wireless fights.
lineup: It is the DS Prime spin-off, not a numbered console sequel.

title: Lock's Quest
history: 5th Cell's DS strategy game Lock's Quest (2008) has you build walls by day and defend them when the siege starts at night.

title: Disney•Pixar Cars Mater-National Championship
history: Pixar's tow truck headlines the racing tie-in Disney•Pixar Cars Mater-National Championship (2007), and a DS version was part of that Cars spinoff.

title: Professor Layton and the Last Specter
history: Level-5's fourth DS puzzle adventure Professor Layton and the Last Specter (2011) is a prequel, called Spectre's Call in Europe.

meta.name: Professor Layton and the Last Specter

title: Frogger Returns
history: Konami sent the arcade hopper back across traffic in the DS revival Frogger Returns (2009).

title: Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift
history: Square Enix followed Final Fantasy Tactics Advance with the DS strategy RPG Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift (2008), another Ivalice job system.

meta.name: Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift

title: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies
history: A class-changing party and street-pass guests in a huge handheld Dragon Quest.
lineup: It is the DS mainline Dragon Quest, built for local play as much as a solo story.

meta.name: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies

title: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Time
history: Chunsoft's DS roguelike Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Time (2008) is one half of the Explorers pair, alongside Explorers of Darkness.

meta.name: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Time

title: Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia
history: The second stylus-capture spinoff, Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia (2008), continues the DS line that began with Pokemon Ranger.

title: BATTLESHIP
history: The naval film's licensed game BATTLESHIP (2012) shipped with a DS version in that same tie-in wave.

title: Bejeweled Twist
history: PopCap replaced gem swapping with rotating clusters in Bejeweled Twist (2008), a match-three spinoff of Bejeweled.

title: SimCity 3000
history: Maxis deepened zoning and added landmarks in the PC city builder SimCity 3000 (1999), a different game from the later DS SimCity.

title: Mahjong
history: A DS solitaire take on the tile-matching table game, Mahjong (2009) clears pairs from a stacked layout.

title: Space Ace
history: Don Bluth's laserdisc follow-up to Dragon's Lair is Space Ace, an animated quick-time game later reissued on DS.

title: The Settlers 2: Veni, Vidi, Vici
history: Blue Byte's Roman village builder The Settlers 2: Veni, Vidi, Vici (1996) is a PC strategy game, remembered far from any DS shelf.

title: Yoshi's Island DS
history: Artoon followed the Super Nintendo classic with Yoshi's Island DS (2006), a DS platformer that puts baby Mario on Yoshi's back again.

title: Rocks and Rockets
history: TikGames' DSiWare arcade game Rocks and Rockets (2011) shoots rockets at meteor waves before they hit a city.

title: The Sims 2: Pets
history: EA's pet expansion The Sims 2: Pets (2006) added animals to the PC life sim, while the DS release is a separate handheld about looking after creatures.

title: Rayman Raving Rabbids 2
history: Ubisoft turned the Rabbids into a party-minigame sequel, Rayman Raving Rabbids 2 (2007), and a DS version was part of that set.

title: F1 2011
history: Codemasters' official Formula 1 season is F1 2011, and the 3DS release is a cut-down handheld companion to the console sim.

title: KAMI
history: Flooding each sheet with a single color is the paper-fold puzzle KAMI, and a 3DS eShop version of that indie was released.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask 3D
history: Grezzo's 3DS remake The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask 3D (2015) followed that studio's Ocarina of Time 3D, rebuilding the Nintendo 64 adventure with revised controls.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask 3D

title: Animal Crossing: New Leaf
history: The player becomes mayor in Animal Crossing: New Leaf (2012), the 3DS mainline Animal Crossing that towns lived in for years.

title: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles
history: Capcom's The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles collects two historical courtroom games that began on 3DS in Japan in 2015, later bundled for a worldwide release.

title: Fire Emblem Awakening
history: Intelligent Systems' 3DS tactics game Fire Emblem Awakening (2012) is widely credited with saving the series, thanks to casual mode and unit pairing.

title: Alter World
history: Hopping between alternate versions of a stage is the idea of Alter World, a platformer first sold on the New Nintendo 3DS eShop.

title: Pokémon Ultra Sun, Ultra Moon
history: Game Freak expanded the Alola pair as Pokémon Ultra Sun, Ultra Moon (2017), a 3DS follow-up with a larger story than Sun and Moon.

title: Mario Kart 7
history: Hang gliders and underwater driving arrived in Nintendo's Mario Kart 7 (2011), the kart racer built for 3DS.

title: Puyo Puyo Tetris
history: Sonic Team crossed Puyo blobs with falling tetrominoes in Puyo Puyo Tetris (2014), a versus puzzle that reached 3DS.

title: Bloo Kid 2
history: Short hop-and-run stages make up the indie platformer Bloo Kid 2 (2014), a numbered sequel on the 3DS eShop.

title: New Super Mario Bros. 2
history: Coin rush is the obsession of Nintendo's New Super Mario Bros. 2 (2012), a 3DS side-scroller built around grabbing huge totals.

title: Gunman Clive
history: Horberg Productions' sketch-styled western Gunman Clive (2012) is a small 3DS eShop platformer that punched above its price.

title: Batman: Arkham Origins Blackgate
history: Armature Studio's side-view Metroidvania Batman: Arkham Origins Blackgate (2013) is a Blackgate prison side story on 3DS and Vita, between the console Arkham games.

title: Metroid: Samus Returns
history: MercurySteam remade Metroid II for 3DS as Metroid: Samus Returns (2017), adding a melee counter to Samus's hunt.

title: Slay the Spire
history: MegaCrit's deck-building climb Slay the Spire (2019) turned a roguelike card game into a huge hit, and Switch was one of its platforms.

title: Drawful 2
history: Jackbox's party game Drawful 2 (2016) has players draw terrible prompts so friends can guess the caption.

title: Vampire Survivors
history: poncle's Vampire Survivors (2022) swarms the screen while attacks fire on their own, a breakout auto-battler that came to Switch.

title: Dragon's Dogma: Dark Arisen
history: Capcom's expanded re-release Dragon's Dogma: Dark Arisen (2013) adds the Bitterblack Isle dungeon to Dragon's Dogma, and a Switch port followed.

title: Resident Evil: Village
history: Capcom's Resident Evil: Village (2021) continues the first-person story from Resident Evil 7, a village horror sequel in the main line.

title: ABZU
history: Giant Squid, founded by Journey art director Matt Nava, made the wordless ocean dive ABZU (2016), later ported to Switch.

title: Oxenfree
history: Night School Studio's teen supernatural mystery Oxenfree (2016) is told through walking conversations, and a Switch port followed.

title: Tales from the Borderlands: A Telltale Game Series
history: Telltale's episodic comedy Tales from the Borderlands: A Telltale Game Series (2015) adapts the Borderlands universe as a choice-driven story, later collected on Switch.

meta.name: Tales from the Borderlands: A Telltale Game Series

title: Broken Age
history: Double Fine's Kickstarted adventure Broken Age (2014) shipped in two acts after a long gap, and a Switch version came later.

title: Dying Light
history: Techland's parkour zombie game Dying Light (2015) makes daylight scavenging safer than the night, and a Switch port followed.

title: Sonic Mania
history: Christian Whitehead, Headcannon, and PagodaWest returned to classic Sonic physics in Sonic Mania (2017), and Switch was one of its platforms.

title: The Talos Principle
history: Croteam's first-person puzzle game The Talos Principle (2014) asks philosophical questions between laser and block puzzles, later on Switch.

title: Gris
history: Nomada Studio's wordless platformer Gris (2018) uses watercolor stages and almost no combat, and it came to Switch.

title: Vampyr
history: Dontnod's action RPG Vampyr (2018) follows a doctor turned vampire in 1918 London, and a Switch port came later.

title: Outer Wilds
history: Mobius Digital's Outer Wilds (2019) is a space mystery on a 22-minute loop, widely praised, and later ported to Switch.

title: The Flame in the Flood
history: The Molasses Flood's river-raft survival game The Flame in the Flood (2016) is a roguelike trip downstream, later released on Switch.

title: Deponia
history: Daedalic's comedy point-and-click Deponia (2012) started a German adventure series, and a Switch port collected that trip later.

title: Rogue Legacy
history: Cellar Door Games' Rogue Legacy (2013) sends a new heir into the castle each time you die, a roguelike platformer later on Switch.

title: Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy
history: Vicarious Visions rebuilt the first three Crash games as Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy (2017), and that remaster collection reached Switch.

title: Dust: An Elysian Tail
history: Dean Dodrill largely made the action RPG Dust: An Elysian Tail (2012) alone for Xbox Live Arcade, and a Switch port followed years later.

title: Sniper Elite 4
history: Rebellion set the WWII marksman game Sniper Elite 4 (2017) in Italy, famous for its bullet-camera shots, and a Switch version followed.

title: Life is Strange 2
history: Dontnod's episodic sequel Life is Strange 2 (2018) tells a new road-trip story rather than continuing the first game's lead, and it reached Switch.

title: Machinarium
history: Amanita Design's robot point-and-click Machinarium (2009) has almost no written dialogue, and a Switch port followed the PC original.

title: Valiant Hearts: The Great War
history: Ubisoft Montpellier's puzzle adventure Valiant Hearts: The Great War (2014) follows ordinary people through World War I, later ported to Switch.

title: Yakuza Kiwami
history: Sega's Yakuza Kiwami (2016) is a ground-up remake of the first Yakuza, the Kamurocho crime story that started on PlayStation 2.

title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Call of Pripyat
history: GSC Game World's third Zone shooter S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Call of Pripyat (2009) followed Shadow of Chernobyl as a PC sequel set around Pripyat.

title: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy
history: Eidos-Montreal's single-player action game Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy (2021) is a separate project from Telltale's earlier Guardians series.

title: The LEGO NINJAGO Movie Video Game
history: TT Games' brick tie-in to the Ninjago film is The LEGO NINJAGO Movie Video Game, released in the same year as that movie across several consoles.

meta.name: The LEGO NINJAGO Movie Video Game

title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky
history: GSC Game World's prequel S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky (2008) is the second S.T.A.L.K.E.R. release, set before Shadow of Chernobyl on PC.

title: Outlast 2
history: Red Barrels followed its camcorder horror with Outlast 2 (2017), a rural sequel that kept the defenseless first-person filming.

title: Overcooked! 2
history: Ghost Town Games' kitchen panic sequel Overcooked! 2 (2018) throws new hazards at cooperating chefs, and Switch was a major platform.

title: Ghostrunner
history: One More Level's first-person cyber-ninja Ghostrunner (2020) is built around dying in one hit and restarting the run, including a Switch version.

title: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy
history: Raven Software's Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy (2003) is the third Jedi Knight shooter, letting players build a lightsaber moveset, and Aspyr later ported it to Switch.

meta.name: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy

title: Gone Home
history: Fullbright's exploration game Gone Home (2013) tells a family story by walking through an empty house, and a Switch port followed.

title: Final Fantasy VII (1997)
history: Square's PlayStation RPG Final Fantasy VII (1997) took the series into 3D, and that original version later reached Switch.

title: Katana ZERO
history: Askiisoft's neo-noir action game Katana ZERO (2019) rewinds deaths in short cinematic rooms, and it launched with a Switch version.

title: Shadowrun: Dragonfall - Director's Cut
history: Harebrained Schemes expanded a Shadowrun Returns campaign into Shadowrun: Dragonfall - Director's Cut in 2014, a standalone cyberpunk tactics RPG with a fuller version of that story.

title: INSIDE
history: Playdead followed Limbo with INSIDE in 2016, another wordless side-view puzzle story about a boy slipping through a grim facility. Critics treated it as one of that year's standout games.

title: SEGA Mega Drive and Genesis Classics
history: Sega began shipping SEGA Mega Drive and Genesis Classics on PC in 2010, a growing compilation of Mega Drive and Genesis games that later consolidated onto consoles.

meta.name: SEGA Mega Drive and Genesis Classics

title: Brawlhalla
history: Blue Mammoth Games put the free platform fighter Brawlhalla into early access in 2014. It plays in the Smash mold and later came under Ubisoft.

title: Firewatch
history: Campo Santo's first game, Firewatch, arrived in 2016 as a first-person story set at a Wyoming fire lookout, told largely through radio talks with a supervisor.

title: Assassin's Creed Odyssey
history: Ubisoft Quebec set Assassin's Creed Odyssey in ancient Greece in 2018, with a dialogue-heavy RPG structure and a choice between siblings Alexios and Kassandra.

title: No Man's Sky
history: Hello Games launched the procedural space explorer No Man's Sky in 2016 to a harsh reception, then spent years adding bases, story, and multiplayer.

title: Alien: Isolation
history: Creative Assembly's 2014 Alien: Isolation strands Amanda Ripley on a space station with one xenomorph, fifteen years after the 1979 film.

title: Disco Elysium
history: ZA/UM's 2019 Disco Elysium is a detective RPG in the city of Revachol with no ordinary combat, and it swept a long list of year-end awards.

title: Cuphead
history: Studio MDHR spent years on Cuphead before the 2017 release, a boss-rush run-and-gun drawn and scored like a 1930s rubber-hose cartoon.

title: Darksiders
history: Vigil Games, under THQ, opened its horseman series with Darksiders in 2010, putting War through a combat adventure often compared with Zelda.

title: DOOM Eternal
history: id Software followed its 2016 reboot with DOOM Eternal in 2020, a faster demon shooter that makes the player manage ammo, armor, and health from the enemies themselves.

title: Among Us
history: InnerSloth released the social-deduction game Among Us in 2018, about finding an impostor aboard a ship. Its huge popularity spike came a couple of years later.

title: Transistor
history: Supergiant Games followed Bastion with Transistor in 2014, an isometric action RPG whose fights can be paused and planned.

title: Resident Evil 5
history: Capcom's 2009 Resident Evil 5 teams Chris Redfield with Sheva Alomar and pushes the series further into co-op shooting.

title: XCOM 2
history: Firaxis reversed the 2012 reboot's outcome in XCOM 2, a 2016 turn-based tactics game where the aliens have already occupied Earth.

title: Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition
history: Moon Studios' platformer gained a new area and difficulty options in Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition, the 2016 expansion of the 2015 original.

meta.name: Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition

title: Red Dead Redemption
history: Rockstar San Diego's open-world Western Red Dead Redemption arrived in 2010 with John Marston as its lead, and later ports carried it to newer hardware.

title: Sid Meier’s Civilization VI
history: Firaxis added city districts to the long strategy series in Sid Meier’s Civilization VI, the 2016 entry where urban sprawl matters as much as the capital tile.

title: Trine 2: Complete Story
history: Frozenbyte bundled its puzzle platformer and the Goblin Menace expansion as Trine 2: Complete Story in 2013, still starring a thief, a knight, and a wizard.

title: This War of Mine
history: 11 bit studios shifted war games onto civilians with This War of Mine in 2014, a scavenging sim inspired by accounts of the siege of Sarajevo.

title: Call of Juarez: Gunslinger
history: Techland's 2013 Call of Juarez: Gunslinger is a first-person Western narrated by a bounty hunter whose tall tales rewrite the level as he talks.

title: Dead Cells
history: Motion Twin brought the roguelike metroidvania Dead Cells to a 1.0 release in 2018 after a long early access, with runs that keep combat upgrades rare between deaths.

title: Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus
history: MachineGames continued its alternate-history shooter in 2017 with Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus, following B.J. Blazkowicz through a Nazi-occupied America.

title: Divinity: Original Sin 2
history: Larian's co-op computer RPG Divinity: Original Sin 2 landed in 2017 and became the studio's calling card before Baldur's Gate 3.

title: A Plague Tale: Innocence
history: Asobo Studio set A Plague Tale: Innocence in plague-era France in 2019, following two siblings through swarms of rats.

title: Subnautica
history: Unknown Worlds set the survival game Subnautica under an alien ocean. A full release followed years of early access in 2018.

title: South Park: The Stick of Truth
history: Obsidian made the role-playing game South Park: The Stick of Truth with the show's creators. Ubisoft published it in 2014 after THQ collapsed.

meta.name: South Park: The Stick of Truth

title: Fallout Shelter
history: Bethesda's free vault manager Fallout Shelter started on mobile in 2015, letting players build rooms, assign dwellers, and ride out disasters.

title: Darkest Dungeon
history: Red Hook Studios shipped Darkest Dungeon in 2016, a dungeon crawl in which stress can shatter a party as surely as wounds do.

title: FEZ
history: Phil Fish and Polytron released the perspective-rotating puzzle platformer FEZ in 2012, years after it first drew attention at indie shows.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
history: BioWare's 2003 Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic is the Xbox and PC role-playing game set thousands of years before the films, not the later MMO.

meta.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic

title: Castle Crashers
history: The Behemoth's four-player beat-em-up Castle Crashers became a signature Xbox Live Arcade hit after its 2008 debut.

title: Batman: Arkham City
history: Rocksteady opened up a sealed slice of Gotham in Batman: Arkham City, the 2011 sequel to Arkham Asylum.

title: SUPERHOT
history: Time moves only when the player does in SUPERHOT, the 2016 shooter built around that single rule.

title: What Remains of Edith Finch
history: Giant Sparrow's 2017 What Remains of Edith Finch walks through one cursed family's stories, and it later won the BAFTA for best game.

title: Torchlight II
history: Runic Games followed its dungeon crawler with Torchlight II in 2012, an action RPG known for co-op and a mod-friendly PC release.

title: Corpse Party
history: Corpse Party is the Japanese horror adventure about students trapped after a friendship charm fails. It began as a 1996 PC-98 game and spread through later remakes.

title: Goosebumps: The Game
history: WayForward's Goosebumps: The Game is a 2015 tie-in to the Goosebumps film, drawing monsters from R.L. Stine's children's horror books.

title: Adventure Time: Finn and Jake Investigations
history: The cartoon leads become a detective pair in Adventure Time: Finn and Jake Investigations, a 2015 adventure set in Pendleton Ward's world.

meta.name: Adventure Time: Finn and Jake Investigations

title: Bravely Default
history: Square Enix brought Bravely Default west in 2014. The 3DS RPG, made with Silicon Studio, hangs its battles on a job system plus Brave and Default commands.

title: Tetris Ultimate
history: Ubisoft's multiplatform Tetris Ultimate arrived in 2014 and drew poor notices for a clumsy take on the classic falling-block puzzle.

title: Pro Evolution Soccer 2011
history: Konami's soccer annual Pro Evolution Soccer 2011, released in 2010, continued the long rivalry with EA's FIFA.

title: Luigi's Mansion: Dark Moon
history: Next Level Games returned to the vacuum-cleaner ghost hunt with Luigi's Mansion: Dark Moon in 2013, known as Luigi's Mansion 2 in some regions.

title: Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward
history: Chunsoft followed 999 with Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward in 2012, another escape-room visual novel directed by Kotaro Uchikoshi.

title: Gunstar Heroes
history: Treasure's Sega Genesis run-and-gun Gunstar Heroes arrived in 1993, famous for combining weapons, and later reappeared in Sega's 3D Classics line.

title: Fire Emblem Fates: Birthright
history: Intelligent Systems split Fire Emblem Fates into separate campaigns in 2016. Fire Emblem Fates: Birthright is the Hoshido route, usually treated as the easier path.

title: Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia
history: Intelligent Systems remade the 1992 Famicom game Gaiden as Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia in 2017, keeping the split between two armies.

meta.name: Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia

title: Dragon Quest VIII: Journey of the Cursed King
history: Level-5's PlayStation 2 RPG Dragon Quest VIII: Journey of the Cursed King arrived in 2004 with Akira Toriyama's designs, and a 3DS port followed years later.

meta.name: Dragon Quest VIII: Journey of the Cursed King

title: TRANSFORMERS: Rise of the Dark Spark
history: The 2014 action game TRANSFORMERS: Rise of the Dark Spark links the live-action toys with the War for Cybertron games through the Dark Spark.

meta.name: TRANSFORMERS: Rise of the Dark Spark

title: Angry Birds Star Wars
history: Rovio reskinned its slingshot puzzle as Angry Birds Star Wars in 2012, swapping the birds and pigs for characters and vehicles from the films.

title: Kung Fu Rabbit
history: French studio cTools shipped the mobile platformer Kung Fu Rabbit in 2012, starring a rabbit who teaches kung fu. Console editions followed with Neko Entertainment.

title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Dual Destinies
history: Capcom's fifth main Ace Attorney game, Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Dual Destinies, arrived on the 3DS in 2013 in full 3D and introduced Athena Cykes.

meta.name: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Dual Destinies

title: Shovel Knight: Specter of Torment
history: Yacht Club Games made Shovel Knight: Specter of Torment in 2017 as a prequel campaign about Specter Knight, also folded into the Treasure Trove package.

title: Shakedown: Hawaii
history: Vblank Entertainment, the studio behind Retro City Rampage, released the open-world crime game Shakedown: Hawaii in 2019.

title: Fire Emblem Fates: Conquest
history: The harder half of the 2016 split, Fire Emblem Fates: Conquest, follows the Nohr family and limits the grinding the sister campaign allows.

title: Kid Icarus: Uprising
history: Project Sora and Masahiro Sakurai revived the series on the 3DS with Kid Icarus: Uprising in 2012, mixing on-rails air battles with ground fights.

title: The Sims 3 Pets
history: The pet-focused Sims release The Sims 3 Pets arrived in 2011. On PC it was an expansion; consoles and handhelds got a standalone game instead.

title: Galaga
history: Namco's 1981 arcade shooter Galaga followed Galaxian and made the tractor beam its signature, yanking the player's ship up to be captured.

title: WWE All Stars
history: THQ's 2011 WWE All Stars drops simulation rules for an arcade wrestler of oversized legends and then-current stars.

title: DIG DUG
history: Namco's 1982 arcade game DIG DUG has the player tunnel under the ground, inflate enemies until they pop, and drop rocks on them.

title: Azure Striker Gunvolt
history: Inti Creates, staffed by Mega Man veterans, released Azure Striker Gunvolt in 2014, a side-scroller about tagging foes and unleashing a flash field.

title: Angry Birds Trilogy
history: Activision's 2012 Angry Birds Trilogy packs the original slingshot game, Seasons, and Rio onto home consoles.

title: Quell Memento
history: Fallen Tree Games' third droplet puzzle, Quell Memento, keeps the series' calm logic mazes and frames them as sorting through scattered memories.

title: Skylanders Giants
history: Activision's second toys-to-life Skylanders game, Skylanders Giants, arrived in 2012 and added oversized Giant figures beside the returning cast.

title: Shin Megami Tensei IV
history: Atlus set Shin Megami Tensei IV in a kingdom sealed over a ruined Tokyo. The 2013 3DS RPG became many players' first mainline SMT game.

title: Ecco the Dolphin (1992)
history: Novotrade's Sega Genesis adventure Ecco the Dolphin (1992) follows a dolphin cut off from his pod, and it is remembered for a steep, strange difficulty.

title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Spirit of Justice
history: Capcom's sixth main Ace Attorney game, Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Spirit of Justice, took Phoenix Wright to the kingdom of Khura'in in 2016.

meta.name: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Spirit of Justice

title: Gunslugs
history: Orangepixel's tiny run-and-gun Gunslugs started on mobile in 2013, sending a squad against the Black Duck Army.

title: 6180 the moon
history: Turtle Cream's puzzle platformer 6180 the moon wraps the screen from bottom to top, so a fall drops you back in from above. The number is how many seconds the first prototype took.

title: Elliot Quest
history: Ansimuz built Elliot Quest in 2014 as an action RPG openly modeled on Zelda II, with side-view combat and an island of dungeons.

title: Quell Reflect
history: Fallen Tree Games placed Quell Reflect between the original Quell and later Memento, another calm puzzle about steering a droplet through logic mazes.

title: Fire Emblem Warriors
history: Omega Force, Team Ninja, and Intelligent Systems crossed Fire Emblem with the Warriors brawler format in Fire Emblem Warriors in 2017, on Switch and New 3DS.

title: 80'S OVERDRIVE
history: Insane Code's retro racer 80'S OVERDRIVE, released in 2017, chases the OutRun mood of sunset highways and a synth-styled soundtrack.

title: Skylanders SWAP Force
history: The third toys-to-life entry, Skylanders SWAP Force, arrived in 2013 with figures that split into swappable top and bottom halves.

title: The Legend of Dark Witch
history: Japanese indie studio INSIDE SYSTEM released The Legend of Dark Witch in 2014, a Mega Man-style action platformer about a witch who takes powers from bosses.

title: Mario & Luigi: Dream Team
history: AlphaDream's 3DS RPG Mario & Luigi: Dream Team, released in 2013, turns Luigi's dreams into both the overworld gimmick and the battles.

title: Fire Emblem Fates: Revelation
history: The third 2016 route, Fire Emblem Fates: Revelation, joins the Hoshido and Nohr armies and was sold apart from the two main campaigns.

title: The Keep
history: Czech studio Cinemax made The Keep in 2014 as a first-person dungeon crawler for the 3DS, with real-time combat and rune magic inside a wizard's tower.

title: Adventure Time: The Secret of the Nameless Kingdom
history: WayForward's 2014 Adventure Time: The Secret of the Nameless Kingdom turns Finn and Jake's cartoon into a top-down dungeon-crawling adventure.

meta.name: Adventure Time: The Secret of the Nameless Kingdom

title: Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney
history: Level-5 and Capcom crossed their puzzle and courtroom series in Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney, first released in Japan in 2012.

meta.name: Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney

title: Kirby: Triple Deluxe
history: HAL Laboratory's 2014 3DS platformer Kirby: Triple Deluxe uses the handheld's depth and gives Kirby a Hypernova inhale that swallows huge objects.

title: Pixel Hunter
history: Lemondo's voxel side-scroller Pixel Hunter first appeared on PC in 2014, sending a hunter through themed stages to take back stolen weapons.

title: Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS
history: Bandai Namco and Sora Ltd. shipped Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS in 2014 as the portable half of that generation's Smash, alongside a separate Wii U game.

title: Skylanders Spyro's Adventure
history: Toys for Bob started the toys-to-life boom with Skylanders Spyro's Adventure in 2011, storing each character's progress in a figure placed on a portal.

title: Kirby: Planet Robobot
history: HAL Laboratory gave Kirby a pilotable mech in Kirby: Planet Robobot, the 2016 3DS game often ranked with the strongest mainline Kirby releases.

title: Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth
history: Atlus crossed Persona 3 and Persona 4 with Etrian Odyssey-style mapping in Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth, a 2014 3DS dungeon RPG.

meta.name: Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth

title: The Legend of Zelda: Tri Force Heroes
history: Nintendo built The Legend of Zelda: Tri Force Heroes in 2015 for three players on the 3DS, stacking Links to reach switches and fight.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Tri Force Heroes

title: Blaster Master Zero
history: Inti Creates reimagined the NES classic in Blaster Master Zero in 2017, keeping the swap between a tank and on-foot cavern exploration.

title: Spyro Reignited Trilogy
history: Toys for Bob remade the first three PlayStation games as Spyro Reignited Trilogy in 2018, rebuilding Spyro, Ripto's Rage, and Year of the Dragon.

title: Risk of Rain 2
history: Hopoo Games moved its roguelike from a side view into 3D with Risk of Rain 2, which left early access in 2020.

title: Blasphemous
history: The Game Kitchen's 2019 Blasphemous is a severe side-view action game steeped in Spanish Catholic imagery and pixel art.

title: Kholat
history: IMGN.PRO's 2015 first-person horror game Kholat draws on the Dyatlov Pass incident, with the player lost in the snowy Ural mountains.

title: Surgeon Simulator
history: Bossa Studios' physics comedy Surgeon Simulator arrived in 2013, with each finger of a clumsy surgeon controlled on its own.

title: Sniper Elite 3
history: Rebellion moved its X-ray sharpshooter to the North African campaign in Sniper Elite 3, released in 2014.

title: Genshin Impact
history: miHoYo launched the free-to-play open-world action RPG Genshin Impact in 2020, built around elemental character swaps and a gacha roster.

title: Serious Sam: The First Encounter
history: Croteam's 2001 arena shooter Serious Sam: The First Encounter throws huge waves of enemies at the player and forms the first half of the original Serious Sam.

title: Furi
history: The Game Bakers' 2016 boss rush Furi alternates sword fights with shooting, one duel after another and almost no ordinary levels between them.

title: Doom 3
history: id Software rebuilt the series as a slower Mars horror shooter in Doom 3, the 2004 game famous for its darkness and flashlight.

title: Titan Quest
history: Iron Lore's 2006 action RPG Titan Quest walks a mythic ancient world from Greece through Egypt and onward, with loot-driven combat.

title: Serious Sam HD:  The First Encounter
history: Croteam's 2009 remaster Serious Sam HD:  The First Encounter updates the look of the 2001 wave shooter without changing its crowd-combat design.

meta.name: Serious Sam HD:  The First Encounter

title: Super Mario Odyssey
history: Kingdoms are sandboxes full of optional moons, and a hat named Cappy does the possessing.
lineup: It is a Nintendo Switch 3D Mario, not a port of Sunshine, Galaxy, or 64.

title: The Banner Saga
history: Stoic's Viking caravan RPG The Banner Saga arrived in 2014, pairing turn-based fights with a travel story drawn in a storybook style.

title: Crypt of the NecroDancer
history: Brace Yourself Games locked movement to the soundtrack in Crypt of the NecroDancer, the 2015 roguelike where missing the beat means missing the step.

title: Darksiders III
history: Gunfire Games put the horseman Fury in the lead for Darksiders III in 2018, a narrower action game than the earlier open-world entries.

title: The Vanishing of Ethan Carter
history: Former People Can Fly developers at The Astronauts released the first-person mystery The Vanishing of Ethan Carter in 2014, later reissued as Redux.

title: Plague Inc: Evolved
history: Ndemic Creations expanded its mobile plague sim for PC and consoles as Plague Inc: Evolved in 2015, adding modes around the original infection puzzle.

title: Hogwarts Legacy
history: Avalanche Software's open-world action RPG Hogwarts Legacy, published by Portkey Games in 2023, is set in the 1890s of the Harry Potter world.

title: Unravel
history: Coldwood Interactive's yarn-figure platformer Unravel, published by EA in 2016, follows the little character Yarny through physics puzzles.

title: SpeedRunners
history: DoubleDutch Games released the competitive runner SpeedRunners in 2016, a side-view race built on grapples and shoving rivals off the screen.

title: Moonlighter
history: Digital Sun's 2018 Moonlighter splits each day between dungeon runs and minding a shop that sells whatever you carried out.

title: Gothic
history: Piranha Bytes' PC role-playing game Gothic arrived in 2001, set in a prison colony trapped under a magic barrier, and later gathered a cult following.

title: Risk of Rain
history: Hopoo Games' 2013 side-view roguelike Risk of Rain makes every minute harsher, and it is the game later remade in 3D as a sequel.

title: Remnant: From the Ashes
history: Gunfire Games combined shooter combat with procedurally arranged worlds in Remnant: From the Ashes, released in 2019.

title: RiME
history: Tequila Works' 2017 puzzle adventure RiME follows a boy across a Mediterranean island and tells the story with very little dialogue.

title: South Park: The Fractured But Whole
history: Ubisoft's 2017 sequel South Park: The Fractured But Whole moves the kids from a fantasy stick fight to a homemade superhero game.

meta.name: South Park: The Fractured But Whole

title: This is the Police
history: Weappy's 2016 management game This is the Police follows a corrupt chief, Jack Boyd, through his last 180 days in the job.

title: Factorio
history: Wube Software's factory builder Factorio is about automating a hostile planet. Version 1.0 arrived in 2020 after a long early access.

title: Golf With Your Friends
history: The mini-golf party game Golf With Your Friends entered early access in 2016 and later reached a wider console release with Team17 publishing.

title: My Friend Pedro
history: DeadToast Entertainment's slow-motion shooter My Friend Pedro, published by Devolver Digital in 2019, takes orders from a talking banana.

title: Hyper Light Drifter
history: Heart Machine's wordless top-down action game Hyper Light Drifter, funded by a closely watched Kickstarter, was released in 2016.

title: Dungeon of the Endless
history: Amplitude Studios mixed a dungeon crawl with tower defense in Dungeon of the Endless, a 2014 game set on a stranded crystal-powered ship.

title: Duck Hunt
history: Light-gun shooting at ducks and clay pigeons, with a dog that comments on misses.
lineup: It shipped with a huge number of NES bundles and stands for that light-gun era in this catalog.

title: Balloon Fight
history: Flapping balloons keep you aloft while you pop rivals and dodge lightning.
lineup: It is a small NES arcade-style game, often grouped with the console's early black-box lineup.

title: Contra
history: A run-and-gun with two soldiers, spreading guns, and a famous cheat code culture around it.
lineup: The NES version is the one that defined Contra for a generation of home players.

title: Dragon Warrior
history: A single hero walks a small kingdom, grinds levels, and talks to townspeople in a turn-based quest.
lineup: North America met Dragon Quest under the Dragon Warrior name on NES.

title: StarTropics
history: Mike Jones searches island dungeons with a yo-yo weapon and a letter that famously needed water.
lineup: It is a late NES Nintendo adventure, cousin to Zelda but with its own island story.

title: Blaster Master
history: A tank explores caverns, then the driver hops out for tight overhead caves.
lineup: It is one of the NES action games people still name when they talk about Sunsoft's 8-bit run.

title: Ghosts 'n Goblins
history: Arthur loses his armor in two hits on a graveyard march that expects you to finish twice.
lineup: The NES port is the notoriously strict home version of Capcom's arcade game.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
history: Four turtles share a life bar across an overhead map and side-view fights.
lineup: It is the first NES TMNT game, distinct from the arcade-style sequel that followed.

title: Faxanadu
history: A side-view action RPG in a dying world tree, with stalls of gear and a password save.
lineup: It is a cult NES adventure and one of the deeper action RPGs on the console.

title: Bionic Commando
history: A swinging arm replaces the jump button in a mission-based action game.
lineup: The NES version is its own campaign, not a straight arcade port, and a Capcom staple of the era.

title: Super Mario All-Stars
history: A 16-bit compilation of the NES Mario side-scrollers, redrawn and sold as one cartridge.
lineup: It is how many SNES owners met the earlier Mario games, and it stays a compilation entry here, not a replacement for the NES pages.

title: Pilotwings
history: Flight-school lessons in a hang glider, plane, and jet pack, graded by instructors.
lineup: It is a launch-window SNES showcase, with a later Nintendo 64 sequel of its own.

title: Secret of Mana
history: Real-time weapon charging and drop-in co-op distinguish this Square action RPG.
lineup: It is the SNES Mana game that reached the widest audience, between earlier and later series entries.

title: Kirby Super Star
history: A collection of short Kirby games on one cartridge, including helper characters who copy abilities with you.
lineup: It is the SNES Kirby anthology, later revisited on DS as Super Star Ultra.

title: Kirby's Dream Course
history: Kirby is a golf ball, and copying an enemy on the green changes the shot.
lineup: It is the odd SNES Kirby, a sports spin rather than a platformer.

title: Street Fighter II
history: One-on-one fights with a roster of special moves, in the home version that lived in a lot of SNES collections.
lineup: This page is the SNES era of Street Fighter II, not a PlayStation or arcade-only release.

title: Mario Party 2
history: Costume boards and a larger minigame list refine the first party game.
lineup: It is the second Nintendo 64 Mario Party, still built for the same shared-controller setup.

title: F-Zero X
history: A huge machine roster and a very high frame rate, with tracks that loop through silence more than scenery.
lineup: It is the Nintendo 64 F-Zero, between the SNES original and the GameCube GX.

title: Wave Race 64
history: Jet-ski racing where the water itself is the obstacle, with buoys that judge your line.
lineup: It is a Nintendo 64 launch-window racer, a showcase more than a character game.

title: 1080 Snowboarding
history: Trick lines and timed courses on snow, with a later GameCube cousin in 1080 Avalanche.
lineup: It is Nintendo's Nintendo 64 snowboard game.

title: GoldenEye 007
history: Mission objectives and split-screen firefights made a movie license into a console shooter.
lineup: It is Rare's Nintendo 64 GoldenEye, the one living rooms played, not a later reimagining.

title: Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards
history: Copy abilities combine in pairs, which is the puzzle as much as the platforms.
lineup: It is the Nintendo 64 Kirby, between the SNES games and the later handheld entries.

title: Mario Tennis
history: Arcade tennis with Mario characters and a simple charge shot.
lineup: Camelot's Nintendo 64 game opened a sports line that continued on later Nintendo systems.

title: Diddy Kong Racing
history: Kart, hovercraft, and plane races on one island hub, with a boss at the end of each world.
lineup: Rare's Nintendo 64 racer, a rival to Mario Kart 64 in the same generation.

title: Yoshi's Story
history: A picture-book Yoshi game about eating fruit to clear short, scored pages.
lineup: It is the Nintendo 64 Yoshi, softer and shorter than the SNES Yoshi's Island.

title: Mario Golf
history: Approach shots and a small RPG-like mode sit under a Mario golf career.
lineup: Camelot's Nintendo 64 golf game, paired in spirit with their tennis entry.

title: Sin and Punishment
history: An on-rails shooter with a stick-controlled aim, released in Japan and later noticed worldwide.
lineup: Treasure's Nintendo 64 game. A Wii sequel followed years later.

title: Pokemon Puzzle League
history: Panel-matching puzzles skinned with the Pokemon anime cast.
lineup: It is Nintendo's Nintendo 64 puzzle game in the Tetris Attack tradition, not a mainline Pokemon quest.

title: Kirby's Dream Land 2
history: Animal friends combine with copy abilities for puzzles the first Dream Land did not have.
lineup: It is the second Game Boy Kirby, between Dream Land and the color sequel.

title: Pokemon Blue
history: The paired version of Red, with a different roster of wild encounters and a different starter story beat.
lineup: It is the other half of the 1996 Game Boy pair, not a sequel.

title: Pokemon Yellow
history: Pikachu follows on screen and the story leans on the anime's first season.
lineup: It is the special Game Boy edition after Red and Blue, still the same generation of monsters.

title: Tetris
history: Falling blocks on the handheld that came packed with an enormous number of Game Boys.
lineup: This page is the Game Boy Tetris, the version that made the puzzle a portable habit, not a later theme-park edition.

title: Pokemon Silver
history: The paired version of Gold, with legendary and version-exclusive differences.
lineup: It is the other 1999 Game Boy Color edition, not a sequel and not the DS remake.

title: Wario Land 3
history: Wario cannot die in the usual way. Getting crushed or burned is how new paths open.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Color Wario Land, a puzzle-platformer more than a score attack.

title: Mario Tennis
history: A role-playing story mode builds a tennis rookie between matches.
lineup: Camelot's Game Boy Color game is the story-heavy sibling of the Nintendo 64 Mario Tennis.

title: Metal Gear Solid
history: A stealth mission in the Metal Gear line, built for the handheld rather than ported scene for scene from the console game.
lineup: It is Konami's Game Boy Color entry, known in Japan as Ghost Babel.

title: Shantae
history: A half-genie dances through towns and transformations on a late color cartridge.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Color original of a series that continued long after the handheld ended.

title: Dragon Warrior III
history: A class-changing party and a world that opens into a second map, in the color remake of an NES epic.
lineup: This page is the Game Boy Color edition players used as the portable Dragon Quest III.

title: Pokemon Sapphire
history: The paired version of Ruby, with a different legendary and version-exclusive teams.
lineup: It is the other 2002 Game Boy Advance edition, not the 3DS remake.

title: Pokemon Emerald
history: The third Hoenn version, with a battle frontier and a story that uses both legendaries.
lineup: It is the refined Game Boy Advance edition of the third generation.

title: Pokemon LeafGreen
history: The paired remake of Blue, built to link with FireRed.
lineup: It is the other 2004 Kanto remake on Game Boy Advance.

title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past & Four Swords
history: A portable Link to the Past shares a cartridge with a multiplayer Four Swords quest.
lineup: It is the Game Boy Advance release, a reissue plus a new mode, not a replacement for the SNES page.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past & Four Swords

title: Pikmin
history: A tiny explorer directs plant-animal helpers to carry cargo before the day's sunlight ends.
lineup: Captain Olimar's first crash-landed rescue, with a hard sunset on each day, is the game on this page. Nintendo later collected the first two Pikmin games in an official Switch release. This page does not claim that collection's current listing.

title: Pikmin 2
history: Debt collection replaces the strict day limit, and caves drop you into longer dungeons.
lineup: It is the GameCube sequel. The later Switch collection pairs it with the first game.

title: F-Zero GX
history: Extremely fast tracks and a story mode of cruel license tests.
lineup: It is the GameCube F-Zero, developed with Sega's Amusement Vision, and the last mainline game for a long time.

title: Pokemon Colosseum
history: A snagged team of shadow Pokemon in a 3D desert story, not a traditional gym quest.
lineup: It is a GameCube spin-off that uses the handheld creatures in a console campaign.

title: Pokemon XD: Gale of Darkness
history: A follow-up campaign about purifying shadow Pokemon, with a deeper roster than Colosseum.
lineup: It is the second GameCube Pokemon story RPG from Genius Sonority.

title: Super Mario Strikers
history: Arcade soccer with items and tackles that would not pass a referee.
lineup: It is the GameCube original of the Strikers line. Later charged-up sequels are separate games.

title: Kirby Air Ride
history: A simple accelerator and a city mode where stats permanently change how you ride.
lineup: It is the GameCube Kirby racer, unusual in the series for how little it explains itself.

title: Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance
history: Ike's mercenary company in a 3D tactics story with a laguz and beorc cast.
lineup: It is the GameCube Fire Emblem. Radiant Dawn on Wii continues the same war.

title: Tales of Symphonia
history: A real-time party RPG about a chosen one and a world split into two realms.
lineup: The GameCube release is the original home version of this Tales story.

title: Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem
history: A horror story told across centuries, with sanity effects that break the screen as well as the character.
lineup: It is a Nintendo-published GameCube exclusive and a one-off, not a series entry with a sequel in this catalog.

title: Chibi-Robo!
history: A tiny robot cleans a house, earns happy points, and learns the family's problems at appliance scale.
lineup: It is the GameCube original of a small Nintendo-published series.

title: Viewtiful Joe
history: A side-scrolling brawler that slows time when the hero strikes a pose.
lineup: It debuted on GameCube before other versions, which is why this catalog files it here.

title: SoulCalibur II
history: Weapon fighters and a guest character, Link, in the GameCube edition of the 2002 fighter.
lineup: This page is the GameCube version, kept because that edition's guest fighter is a Nintendo character. It is not a Nintendo-made game.

title: Super Mario Galaxy
history: Small planets with their own gravity, and a hub observatory between orchestral set pieces.
lineup: The Comet Observatory and planetoids with their own gravity are the Mario adventure on this page. Super Mario Galaxy 2 is a different game. A limited Switch compilation included the first Galaxy for a time.

title: Wii Sports Resort
history: Swordplay, archery, and cycling on an island, built for the MotionPlus add-on.
lineup: It is the Wii follow-up to Wii Sports, not the Switch sports game.

title: Wii Fit
history: Balance-board exercises and a body-test score, sold as a fitness routine rather than a win-the-game campaign.
lineup: The Balance Board trainer, with yoga, strength tests, and a body-test score, starts on this page. Later Fit follow-ups are separate products.

title: Metroid Prime 3: Corruption
