history: Samus travels several planets while a corruption meter rewards and punishes hypermode.
lineup: It is the Wii close of the original Prime trilogy.

title: Kirby's Epic Yarn
history: A yarn world where Kirby cannot die in the usual way, and the goal is beads and patches.
lineup: It is the Wii Kirby by Good-Feel. A later 3DS port exists; this page is the Wii original.

title: Animal Crossing: City Folk
history: A Wii town with a city you visit by bus, and voice chat that the series later dropped.
lineup: It is the Wii Animal Crossing, between the GameCube original and the 3DS New Leaf.

title: Super Paper Mario
history: A side-scroller that flips into 3D, closer to an action game than the turn-based Paper Mario stories.
lineup: It is the Wii Paper Mario, a departure from the GameCube Thousand-Year Door.

title: Punch-Out!!
history: A return to Little Mac's tells and glass jaws, with motion controls that can be turned down.
lineup: It is the Wii Punch-Out!!, a revival of the NES career rather than a new sport.

title: Monster Hunter Tri
history: Underwater fights and a village hub in the Monster Hunter that brought the series to a wide Nintendo audience.
lineup: It is the Wii entry. Later portable Monster Hunter games are separate.

title: Fire Emblem: Radiant Dawn
history: Three armies and a huge cast continue the Path of Radiance war on Wii.
lineup: It is the direct sequel to the GameCube Fire Emblem, and one of the largest games in the series.

title: Sin & Punishment: Star Successor
history: A sequel to the Nintendo 64 rail shooter, with a partner character and the same stick-aim idea.
lineup: It is Treasure's Wii follow-up, not a remake of the 2000 game.

title: The Last Story
history: A mercenary band in a dying-magic city, with cover-based command battles.
lineup: Mistwalker's late Wii RPG, published by Nintendo in the West, alongside that era's Xenoblade and Pandora's Tower.

title: Pikmin 3
history: Three captains split squads across a garden to bring fruit home before juice runs out.
lineup: Three captains ration fruit juice across a garden on this page. The later Deluxe release, with extra difficulties, has its own Switch page.

title: Splatoon
history: Teams shoot ink to claim ground, and the match ends when the paint does.
lineup: It is the Wii U original of a series whose sequels, Splatoon 2 and Splatoon 3, are Switch games.

title: Super Smash Bros. for Wii U
history: The home-console half of the pair that also shipped on 3DS, with larger stages.
lineup: It is the Wii U Smash. The 3DS version is a separate page, and Ultimate on Switch is a later game.

meta.name: Super Smash Bros. for Wii U

title: Xenoblade Chronicles X
history: A frontier planet, a customizable avatar, and a transforming doll mech.
lineup: It is the Wii U spin on Xenoblade, separate from the numbered Shulk story. A later Definitive Edition is its own page.

title: Yoshi's Woolly World
history: Yarn Yoshis unravel secrets in craft-textured stages.
lineup: It is the Wii U Good-Feel game. A 3DS version with Poochy followed; this page is the home-console original.

title: Nintendo Land
history: A theme-park of attractions that show off the GamePad, from a ghost house to a Luigi mansion minigame.
lineup: It is the Wii U launch compilation, a pack-in for many deluxe sets.

title: Star Fox Zero
history: A cockpit drawn on the GamePad and a TV view that does not always agree with it.
lineup: It is the Wii U Star Fox, a retelling rather than Star Fox 64, and a late game for the console.

title: Paper Mario: Color Splash
history: Paint restores a paper island, and battles are card-based rather than the old partner system.
lineup: It is the Wii U Paper Mario, between Sticker Star and the Switch Origami King.

title: The Wonderful 101
history: A crowd of heroes forms a giant fist, sword, or gun when you draw the shape.
lineup: It is the Wii U PlatinumGames game published with Nintendo. A later remastered edition exists; this page is the Wii U original.

title: Hyrule Warriors
history: Musou crowds and Zelda characters on big battlefields, a crossover rather than a mainline quest.
lineup: Omega Force and Team Ninja's first Zelda battlefield crossover is this page. Definitive Edition on Switch is a separate, expanded page.

title: Nintendogs
history: A puppy you train with the touch screen and the microphone, on a real-time clock.
lineup: It is the DS pet simulation that was a launch-era phenomenon. Later + Cats on 3DS is a sequel.

title: Pokemon Diamond
history: A Sinnoh journey with a physical-special split that changed how moves work.
lineup: Diamond is one half of the 2006 pair. Platinum is the third version. Brilliant Diamond on Switch is a remake with its own page.

title: Pokemon SoulSilver
history: The paired remake of Silver, built to match HeartGold's walking companion and two regions.
lineup: It is the other 2009 DS remake.

title: Pokemon White
history: The paired Unova version, with a different legendary and a city that changes after the story.
lineup: It is the other 2010 DS edition.

title: Pokemon Black 2
history: A direct sequel set two years later, which the series had not done for a paired edition before.
lineup: It is the DS follow-up to Black, not a remake.

title: Mario & Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story
history: Mario and Luigi explore Bowser's body while Bowser fights on the top screen.
lineup: It is the DS Mario & Luigi. A 3DS remake later revisited it.

title: Kirby: Canvas Curse
history: You draw paths for a ball of Kirby instead of moving him directly.
lineup: It is the DS Kirby built entirely around the touch screen.

title: Chrono Trigger
history: The SNES time-travel RPG on DS, with added scenes and a dual-screen map.
lineup: The dual-screen reissue adds the Lost Sanctum and an Arena the Super Nintendo cartridge did not have. The SNES original remains a separate entry.

title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney
history: Courtroom objections and crime-scene searches, in the first Ace Attorney released widely on DS.
lineup: It is Capcom's DS adventure that opened the series for many players outside Japan.

title: Elite Beat Agents
history: Touch-screen rhythm scenes about agents who fix lives by hitting marks on a song.
lineup: It is the Western sibling of Ouendan, a DS rhythm game published by Nintendo.

title: Advance Wars: Dual Strike
history: Two COs share a battle across both screens.
lineup: It is the DS Advance Wars, the follow-up to the Game Boy Advance pair.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
history: A changed Hyrule adds a sky, a depths, and a way to combine objects as you travel.
lineup: It is the Switch sequel to Breath of the Wild, not a mode inside that game. RAWG has filed it under more than one slug; this page is the 2023 game.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe
history: The Switch edition adds a revised battle mode, more characters, and later extra cups.
lineup: It is not the same entry as the Wii U Mario Kart 8, which has its own page.

title: Animal Crossing: New Horizons
history: You settle an island, invite neighbors, and decorate on the real-world calendar.
lineup: It is the Switch Animal Crossing, not the GameCube, DS, Wii, or 3DS towns.

title: Metroid Dread
history: A side-view Metroid about slipping past threats you cannot beat yet, then coming back armed.
lineup: It is a Switch original and the numbered follow-up to Fusion, developed with MercurySteam.

title: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six
history: Red Storm's 1998 tactical shooter Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six made players plan a breach, then carry it out, and a Nintendo 64 version followed.

title: Mortal Kombat Trilogy
history: Midway packed the first three Mortal Kombat games into Mortal Kombat Trilogy in 1996. The Nintendo 64 cart held a larger roster than the PlayStation disc.

title: Re-Volt
history: Acclaim's 1999 remote-control racer Re-Volt runs toy cars through houses and streets, and the PC version includes a track editor.

title: Conker's Bad Fur Day
history: Rare scrapped a family-friendly Conker game and shipped the foul-mouthed platformer Conker's Bad Fur Day instead, in 2001.

title: Fighting Force
history: Core Design tried to carry belt-scrolling brawlers into 3D with Fighting Force, a 1997 beat-em-up on the new disc consoles and Nintendo 64.

title: Pokémon Stadium 2
history: The Nintendo 64 battle game Pokémon Stadium 2 transfers Gold and Silver teams into 3D fights. Japan received it in 2000.

title: Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards
history: HAL Laboratory's Nintendo 64 platformer Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards, released in 2000, is the Kirby game where copied powers can be combined.

title: Yoshi's Story (1997)
history: Nintendo followed Yoshi's Island with Yoshi's Story (1997), a side-scroller of pre-rendered scenery whose goal is collecting fruit.

title: Mario Party 3
history: Hudson's Mario Party 3, released in 2000, added story duels and was the last Mario Party board game on the Nintendo 64.

title: Mario Tennis (2000)
history: Camelot's Nintendo 64 game Mario Tennis (2000) mixes tournament tennis with character growth, and a separate Game Boy Color game shares the name.

title: 007: The World is not Enough
history: Eurocom's Nintendo 64 first-person shooter 007: The World is not Enough, released in 2000, is a different game from the PlayStation tie-in to the same Bond film.

title: FIFA '98: Road to World Cup
history: EA themed its soccer annual around World Cup qualifying in FIFA '98: Road to World Cup, which shipped in 1997.

title: Army Men: Sarge's Heroes
history: 3DO took the plastic army into a third-person shooter with Army Men: Sarge's Heroes in 1999, shrinking Sarge down into the human world.

title: Destruction Derby
history: Reflections' 1995 combat racer Destruction Derby is about wrecking the other cars, and it became an early PlayStation staple.

title: Nightmare Creatures
history: Kalisto's 1997 action game Nightmare Creatures is set in a monster-haunted London and plays as a weapon-based brawler.

title: Mortal Kombat Mythologies: Sub-Zero
history: Midway stepped outside the tournaments with Mortal Kombat Mythologies: Sub-Zero in 1997, a side-scrolling prequel starring Sub-Zero.

title: Robotron: 2084
history: Eugene Jarvis and Larry DeMar's 1982 Williams arcade game Robotron: 2084 is the twin-stick shooter about saving the last humans from robots.

title: F-Zero X
history: Nintendo EAD's 1998 futuristic racer F-Zero X puts a huge field of machines on the Nintendo 64 and is remembered for its speed and track design.

title: Mario Golf (1999)
history: Camelot's Nintendo 64 game Mario Golf (1999) pairs stroke play with a role-playing mode, beside a separate Game Boy Color version.

title: Vigilante 8: 2nd Offense
history: Luxoflux followed its vehicular combat game with Vigilante 8: 2nd Offense in 1999, still an alternate-1970s car war.

title: South Park (1998)
history: Acclaim's first-person shooter South Park (1998), based on the Comedy Central show, was widely panned when it launched.

title: Extreme-G 2
history: Acclaim's futuristic motorcycle sequel Extreme-G 2 arrived in 1998, continuing the anti-gravity bike races of the first game.

title: Rampage World Tour
history: Midway revived George, Lizzie, and Ralph for Rampage World Tour in 1997, a city-smashing sequel to the arcade monster game.

title: Bomberman 64 (1997)
history: Hudson moved the series into polygonal stages with Bomberman 64 (1997), adding a single-player rescue story beside the blasting.

title: 1080° Snowboarding (N64)
history: Nintendo EAD's weighty snowboard sim 1080° Snowboarding (N64) arrived in 1998 and stayed a favorite of the console's sports line.

title: Gex 3: Deep Cover Gecko (1999)
history: Crystal Dynamics closed its gecko trilogy with Gex 3: Deep Cover Gecko (1999), another platformer built on the character's TV-channel jokes.

title: Jet Force Gemini
history: Rare's 1999 third-person shooter Jet Force Gemini stars a brother, a sister, and their dog against an insect army on the Nintendo 64.

title: Harvest Moon 64 (1999)
history: Natsume's Nintendo 64 farm sim Harvest Moon 64 (1999) is about crops, livestock, and town life, a localization from the Bokujou Monogatari line.

title: International Superstar Soccer 64
history: Konami's International Superstar Soccer 64, released in 1997, was widely called the best soccer game on the Nintendo 64.

title: Beetle Adventure Racing
history: Paradigm's 1999 arcade racer Beetle Adventure Racing uses Volkswagen's New Beetle and hides shortcuts in the scenery. Australia got it as HSV Adventure Racing.

title: Space Station Silicon Valley
history: DMA Design's 1998 Space Station Silicon Valley lets the player possess robot animals while exploring a stranded station.

title: Hey You, Pikachu!
history: Nintendo's Hey You, Pikachu! uses the Nintendo 64 Voice Recognition Unit so a player can talk to Pikachu. The Japanese release was in 1998.

title: NBA Live 2000
history: EA's annual basketball sim NBA Live 2000 shipped in 1999, covering the season that followed the lockout.

title: Winback: Covert Operations
history: Omega Force and Koei's 1999 third-person shooter Winback: Covert Operations is built around leaning out of cover, years before that style was common.

title: V-Rally (1997)
history: Infogrames' rally racer V-Rally (1997) helped establish the off-road series on PlayStation, with later ports and sequels under the same name.

title: WWF No Mercy
history: AKI and THQ's 2000 wrestling game WWF No Mercy is still cited as a high point of the genre, especially its create-a-wrestler.

title: Star Wars Episode I: Battle for Naboo
history: Factor 5 followed Rogue Squadron with the Nintendo 64 flight shooter Star Wars Episode I: Battle for Naboo in 2000, this time from the Naboo side of the film.

meta.name: Star Wars Episode I: Battle for Naboo

title: Chameleon Twist
history: Japan System Supply's 1997 platformer Chameleon Twist gives its hero a long tongue for swinging, swallowing, and reaching distant poles.

title: The Powerpuff Girls: Chemical X-traction
history: The Cartoon Network series became a 2001 fighter in The Powerpuff Girls: Chemical X-traction, with Chemical X as the power the title names.

title: Custom Robo
history: Custom Robo is a toy-robot battler about outfitting a small fighter. The series began on the Nintendo 64 in Japan in 1999, and a GameCube game carried the short title west in 2004.

title: Dr. Mario 64
history: Nintendo brought the pill-matching puzzle to four players in Dr. Mario 64 in 2001, and the story mode puts Wario in the mix.

title: ClayFighter 63⅓
history: Interplay's claymation fighter ClayFighter 63⅓ arrived on the Nintendo 64 in 1997, a numbered sequel in the ClayFighter series.

title: Mega Man 64 (2001)
history: Capcom's Mega Man 64 (2001) is the Nintendo 64 port of Mega Man Legends, the 3D adventure spinoff rather than a side-scrolling classic.

title: Body Harvest
history: DMA Design's 1998 shooter Body Harvest, published by Gremlin, fights giant insects across several time periods in open areas.

title: Superman: The New Adventures
history: Titus's 1999 Superman: The New Adventures, better known as Superman 64, is the Nintendo 64 game that became a fixture on worst-of lists.

title: Cruis'n World
history: Midway followed Cruis'n USA with the globe-trotting arcade racer Cruis'n World in 1998.

title: Bio F.R.E.A.K.S.
history: Midway's 1998 weapons fighter Bio F.R.E.A.K.S. lets combatants tear off limbs and bolt on replacements mid-battle.

title: South Park: Chef's Luv Shack
history: Acclaim turned the Comedy Central show into a quiz-and-minigame party disc with South Park: Chef's Luv Shack in 1999, hosted by Chef.

title: Snowboard Kids 2
history: Atlus's cartoon snowboard racer Snowboard Kids 2 arrived in 1999 as a sequel with new riders and courses.

title: Power Rangers Lightspeed Rescue
history: The television season became a 2000 action game in Power Rangers Lightspeed Rescue, one of many licensed Power Rangers titles of that era.

title: NFL Blitz (1998)
history: Midway's arcade football game NFL Blitz (1998) is known for late hits and exaggerated violence, not a league simulation.

title: Ridge Racer 64
history: Nintendo Software Technology's 2000 Ridge Racer 64 is the Nintendo 64 chapter of Namco's series, built from Ridge Racer and Revolution courses.

title: Road Rash 64
history: THQ's 1999 motorcycle brawler Road Rash 64 was made for the Nintendo 64 apart from Electronic Arts' earlier Road Rash games.

title: Mission: Impossible (1998)
history: Ocean's stealth-action tie-in Mission: Impossible (1998) is based on the 1996 film and is best known in its Nintendo 64 version.

title: WCW Mayhem
history: Electronic Arts' 1999 WCW Mayhem is a professional wrestling game using the WCW license and its television roster.

title: Turok: Rage Wars
history: Acclaim's 1999 Turok: Rage Wars drops most of the exploration and focuses on multiplayer arena fights in the Turok setting.

title: NBA Live 99
history: EA shipped the basketball annual NBA Live 99 in 1998, the edition tied to the lockout-shortened NBA season.

title: Namco Museum (1995)
history: PlayStation owners got Namco's arcade cabinet set in Namco Museum (1995), including Pac-Man, Galaga, Dig Dug, and other coin-op hits.

title: Madden NFL 2001
history: EA's football annual Madden NFL 2001 reached stores in 2000, part of the long Madden NFL series.

title: War Gods
history: Midway's 1996 3D weapon fighter War Gods used digitized characters, a follow-up in spirit to Mortal Kombat from the same publisher.

title: Duke Nukem 64
history: Duke Nukem 64 is the cartridge port of Duke Nukem 3D, with violence trimmed for Nintendo and extra stages the PC release did not ship. The cartridge arrived in 1997.

title: International Track & Field 2000
history: Konami's button-mashing Olympic sequel International Track & Field 2000 is themed to the Sydney Games and follows the 1996 International Track & Field.

title: San Francisco Rush 2049
history: Atari pushed the arcade city racer into the future with San Francisco Rush 2049 in 2000, adding airborne and underground tracks.

title: Rocket: Robot on Wheels
history: Sucker Punch's first game, the 1999 platformer Rocket: Robot on Wheels, showed off a physics-heavy Nintendo 64 engine before the studio moved on to Sly Cooper.

title: Puzzle Bobble 2
history: Taito's bubble-matching sequel Puzzle Bobble 2, also widely sold as Bust-a-Move II, continues the aiming-and-matching puzzle of the arcade original.

title: WWF War Zone
history: Acclaim's 1998 wrestling game WWF War Zone is remembered for a create-a-wrestler mode and full-motion entrances.

title: Hot Wheels Turbo Racing
history: Stormfront Studios' 1999 Hot Wheels Turbo Racing is a Mattel-licensed arcade racer built around Hot Wheels cars.

title: Nagano Winter Olympics '98
history: Konami's official licensed sports game Nagano Winter Olympics '98 shipped in 1997, with skiing, skating, and other winter events.

title: Wipeout 64
history: Psygnosis brought anti-gravity racing to the Nintendo 64 with Wipeout 64 in 1998, an exclusive chapter of the Wipeout series.

title: Iggy's Reckin' Balls
history: Iguana's 1998 party racer Iggy's Reckin' Balls rolls characters inside spiked balls through Nintendo 64 obstacle courses.

title: WWF WrestleMania 2000
history: AKI and THQ's wrestling game WWF WrestleMania 2000 shipped in 1999 and set up the more celebrated No Mercy the following year.

title: Madden NFL 2002
history: EA's football annual Madden NFL 2002, released in 2001, was among the last Madden seasons published for the Nintendo 64.

title: WCW Nitro
history: Inland Productions and THQ's 1998 WCW Nitro is a wrestling game tied to the WCW Monday night television show.

title: San Francisco Rush: Extreme Racing
history: Atari Games started the shortcut-filled city racer with San Francisco Rush: Extreme Racing in 1997.

title: International Superstar Soccer 2000
history: Konami continued its soccer series with International Superstar Soccer 2000, which reached the Nintendo 64 in 1999.

title: Ms. Pac-Man Maze Madness
history: Namco's 2000 Ms. Pac-Man Maze Madness turns the dot-muncher into a 3D maze adventure instead of a straight arcade port.

title: Cruis'n Exotica
history: Midway's third Cruis'n arcade racer, Cruis'n Exotica, arrived in 2000 with fantasy courses beyond the earlier real-world tours.

title: Puyo Puyo SUN
history: Compile's 1997 puzzle game Puyo Puyo SUN keeps the colored-blob chain clears and adds a sun meter that powers them up.

title: Madden NFL 2000
history: EA released the football annual Madden NFL 2000 in 1999, another season in the Madden NFL line.

title: Mace: The Dark Age
history: Atari's 1997 weapons fighter Mace: The Dark Age pits fantasy combatants against each other in 3D arenas, in arcades and on the Nintendo 64.

title: Chameleon Twist 2
history: Japan System Supply continued the tongue-swinging Nintendo 64 platformer with Chameleon Twist 2 in 1998.

title: NASCAR 2000
history: EA's stock-car annual NASCAR 2000 reached players in 1999, one entry in the long EA Sports NASCAR line.

title: Monaco Grand Prix
history: Ubisoft's 1999 street-circuit racer Monaco Grand Prix focuses on the famous race around the principality and was also sold under a Racing Simulation name.

title: Knockout Kings 2000
history: EA's licensed boxing game Knockout Kings 2000 shipped in 1999, part of the Knockout Kings series of real fighters.

title: Wheel of Fortune (Old)
history: Wheel of Fortune (Old) is an early home version of the television quiz show, dated 1988, in which players spin a wheel and call letters.

title: Top Gear Rally
history: Boss Game Studios and Kemco's Nintendo 64 rally racer Top Gear Rally arrived in 1997, noted for changing weather on its courses.

title: Puzzle Bobble 3
history: Taito's third bubble-matcher, Puzzle Bobble 3, continues the series also sold under the Bust-a-Move name.

title: Wetrix
history: Zed Two's puzzle game Wetrix makes you raise and lower terrain so falling water does not spill off the map. It became a known Nintendo 64 puzzle release.

title: Shadowgate 64: Trials of the Four Towers
history: Kemco's 1999 Shadowgate 64: Trials of the Four Towers retells the 1987 castle adventure in 3D.

meta.name: Shadowgate 64: Trials of the Four Towers

title: NASCAR 99
history: EA's stock-car annual NASCAR 99 shipped in 1998, an earlier season in the same NASCAR line as the later numbered editions.

title: ECW Hardcore Revolution
history: Acclaim's 2000 wrestling game ECW Hardcore Revolution uses the Extreme Championship Wrestling license and its hardcore-match reputation.

title: Blues Brothers 2000
history: The platformer Blues Brothers 2000 follows Jake and Elwood and is tied to the film of the same name.

title: F-1 World Grand Prix
history: Video System's 1998 Nintendo 64 simulation F-1 World Grand Prix runs a Formula 1 season across real-world circuits.

title: BattleTanx: Global Assault
history: 3DO followed its tank combat game with BattleTanx: Global Assault in 1999, another Nintendo 64 shooter of rival tanks.

title: Buck Bumble
history: Argonaut's 1998 shooter Buck Bumble puts the player in control of an armed bee on the Nintendo 64.

title: Automobili Lamborghini
history: Titus's 1997 Nintendo 64 racer Automobili Lamborghini is built around the Italian sports cars and was called Super Speed Race in Japan.

title: NBA Hangtime
history: Midway's 1997 arcade basketball game NBA Hangtime succeeds NBA Jam, keeping the exaggerated dunks and adding a create-a-player.

title: Polaris SnoCross
history: Vicarious Visions' 2000 snowmobile racer Polaris SnoCross carries the Polaris brand onto the Nintendo 64.

title: Hybrid Heaven
history: Konami's 1999 Nintendo 64 game Hybrid Heaven mixes role-playing stats with close-quarters fighting in a science-fiction setting.

title: Aero Fighters Assault
history: Paradigm and Video System took the shooter series into 3D with Aero Fighters Assault, a 1997 Nintendo 64 entry.

title: Scooby-Doo! Classic Creep Capers
history: THQ's 2001 Scooby-Doo! Classic Creep Capers is a 3D adventure based on the Hanna-Barbera cartoon and its mystery-solving crew.

title: Pokémon Pinball
history: Jupiter and HAL Laboratory's 1999 Game Boy Color game Pokémon Pinball puts Pokemon on pinball tables and lets you catch them from the playfield.

title: 102 Dalmatians: Puppies to the Rescue
history: The Disney film sequel got a 2000 platformer in 102 Dalmatians: Puppies to the Rescue, with puppies as the playable leads.

title: Xena: Warrior Princess
history: The syndicated television series received a 1999 PlayStation action game titled Xena: Warrior Princess. Titus later shipped a separate Game Boy Color version.

title: Croc 2
history: Fox Interactive's 1999 platformer Croc 2 continues the crocodile adventure that began with Croc: Legend of the Gobbos.

title: Army Men
history: 3DO opened its plastic-soldier line with Army Men in 1998, the green-versus-tan war that spawned a long run of sequels.

title: Super Mario Bros. Deluxe
history: Nintendo's 1999 Game Boy Color cart Super Mario Bros. Deluxe includes the original Super Mario Bros., Lost Levels material, and extra challenge modes.

title: X-Men: Mutant Academy
history: Activision's 2000 one-on-one fighter X-Men: Mutant Academy puts Marvel's mutant teams into versus matches.

title: Metal Gear: Ghost Babel
history: Konami's 2000 Game Boy Color game Metal Gear: Ghost Babel was retitled Metal Gear Solid outside Japan, but it tells a separate story from the PlayStation game.

title: Blade (2000)
history: The Wesley Snipes vampire film received a handheld action tie-in in Blade (2000).

title: Moorhuhn 2
history: The German casual hit about shooting pheasants gained a 2000 sequel in Moorhuhn 2, also known under the Crazy Chicken name.

title: LEGO Island 2: The Brickster's Revenge
history: LEGO Island 2: The Brickster's Revenge, released in 2001, continues the LEGO Island adventure after the Brickster's escape.

title: Hugo: The Evil Mirror
history: The Danish TV-show troll returned in Hugo: The Evil Mirror, a 2002 platformer in the long Hugo series.

title: Mat Hoffman's Pro BMX
history: Activision's 2001 trick-biking game Mat Hoffman's Pro BMX carries the name of the real BMX rider, from the same boom as the Tony Hawk games.

title: Mr. Driller
history: Namco's 2000 puzzle game Mr. Driller sends the player drilling down through colored blocks while an air meter keeps running out.

title: Test Drive 6
history: Accolade continued its street-racing series with Test Drive 6 in 1999, another set of licensed cars and point-to-point courses.

title: Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX
history: Acclaim's Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX, released in 2000, is the first game built around the X Games rider and other pro BMX tricks. The Game Boy Color cart is a smaller side-view edition, not the 3D PlayStation and Dreamcast game, and Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX 2 is the sequel.

title: Buzz Lightyear of Star Command
history: Disney's television spinoff, not the Toy Story films alone, is the source for Buzz Lightyear of Star Command, a 2000 platformer.

title: The Grinch
history: Ron Howard's film of the Dr. Seuss story got a 2000 platform tie-in simply titled The Grinch.

title: Walt Disney World Quest: Magical Racing Tour
history: Eidos published the 2000 kart racer Walt Disney World Quest: Magical Racing Tour, set in the Florida theme park.

meta.name: Walt Disney World Quest: Magical Racing Tour

title: Chicken Run
history: Aardman's stop-motion film about chickens plotting an escape received a 2000 tie-in titled Chicken Run.

title: Puzzle Bobble 4
history: Taito's fourth bubble-matcher, Puzzle Bobble 4, also sold as Bust-a-Move 4, continued the series on consoles in 1998.

title: Wacky Races (1991)
history: Hi-Tec Software's computer platformer Wacky Races (1991) is based on the Hanna-Barbera cartoon and appeared on machines such as the Amiga and Commodore 64.

title: Hype: The Time Quest
history: Ubisoft's 1999 action RPG Hype: The Time Quest follows a knight thrown through time.

title: Rampart (1990)
history: Atari Games' arcade classic Rampart (1990) alternates building a castle wall with cannon defense, and it later spread to many home ports.

title: Milon's Secret Castle (1988)
history: Hudson Soft's maze-like action game debuted on the Famicom Disk System in 1986 and reached the NES as Milon's Secret Castle (1988).

title: Tomb Raider: Curse of the Sword
history: Core Design made the 2001 Game Boy Color adventure Tomb Raider: Curse of the Sword, published by Activision as a sequel to the earlier handheld Tomb Raider.

meta.name: Tomb Raider: Curse of the Sword

title: Lufia: The Legend Returns (2001)
history: The Lufia series reached the Game Boy Color in Lufia: The Legend Returns (2001), a handheld role-playing continuation of that line.

title: Stuart Little 2
history: The second Stuart Little film received a 2002 tie-in game titled Stuart Little 2.

title: Survival Kids
history: Konami's 1999 Game Boy Color game Survival Kids, also called Stranded Kids, is about children living off a hostile island.

title: Megami Tensei Gaiden: Last Bible
history: Megami Tensei Gaiden: Last Bible is the Game Boy spinoff that opened the Last Bible line, a monster-collecting RPG under the Megami Tensei name.

title: Harvest Moon 3 GBC (2000)
history: Harvest Moon 3 GBC (2000) is the third color-handheld entry in the farming series, after Harvest Moon GB and Harvest Moon 2 GBC, about raising crops, animals, and town relationships.

title: Redline Racer
history: Criterion Games' first release, the 1998 superbike racer Redline Racer, is an early step for the studio later known for Burnout.

title: Warriors of Might and Magic
history: 3DO's 2000 Warriors of Might and Magic is an action role-playing spinoff, separate from the turn-based Heroes strategy games.

title: LEGO Stunt Rally
history: The brick-built racer LEGO Stunt Rally arrived in 2000, with tracks assembled from LEGO pieces.

title: Woody Woodpecker Racing
history: Universal's cartoon bird headlines the 2000 kart racer Woody Woodpecker Racing, alongside other licensed characters.

title: Deja Vu: A Nightmare Comes True
history: ICOM Simulations' 1985 MacVenture Deja Vu: A Nightmare Comes True is a point-and-click noir mystery about an amnesiac in Chicago.

meta.name: Deja Vu: A Nightmare Comes True

title: Spider-Man (2001)
history: Marvel's wall-crawler headlines Spider-Man (2001), one of the action games from the wave of Spider-Man titles just before the 2002 film.

title: Deer Hunter
history: The budget hunting sim Deer Hunter became a surprise PC hit in 1997 and later spun off a long line of follow-ups and ports.

title: Spider-Man 2: The Sinister Six
history: Torus Games' 2001 handheld Spider-Man 2: The Sinister Six pits the hero against that villain team, and it is not the later movie game.

title: Wings of Fury (1987)
history: Broderbund's side-scrolling World War II game Wings of Fury (1987) launches the player from a carrier to strafe ships and ground targets.

title: Alleyway
history: Nintendo's 1989 Game Boy launch-window game Alleyway is a brick-breaker starring Mario, in the tradition of Breakout.

title: Earthworm Jim: Menace 2 the Galaxy
history: Crave and IMS Productions' 1999 handheld platformer Earthworm Jim: Menace 2 the Galaxy is a later, smaller entry in the Earthworm Jim series.

title: Toobin'
history: Atari Games' 1988 arcade game Toobin' sends riders down a river on inner tubes, dodging hazards and tossing cans at obstacles.

title: Pokemon Trading Card Game 2
history: The Japanese Game Boy Color sequel Pokemon Trading Card Game 2 arrived in 2001 and did not get an official English release at the time.

title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (GBC)
history: Griptonite's 2001 Game Boy Color RPG Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (GBC) adapts the first story and is separate from the console action games.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (GBC)

title: New York Race
history: Kalisto's 2001 futuristic racer New York Race began as a Fifth Element game and shipped without that film's license.

title: Titus the Fox (GB, GBC)
history: Titus the Fox (GB, GBC) is the handheld port of the platformer about a fox heading for Marrakech. The computer original is from 1992, and the Game Boy edition followed in 1993.

title: Star Wars: Yoda Stories
history: LucasArts' 1997 desktop game Star Wars: Yoda Stories builds a short randomized adventure around Yoda each time it is played.

title: Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children
history: Atlus aimed Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children at a younger audience in 2000, a Game Boy Color spinoff that pairs children with demon partners.

title: LEGO Alpha Team
history: The PC puzzle adventure LEGO Alpha Team arrived in 2000, with agents taking apart the Brickster's contraptions.

title: Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children: Black Book
history: Atlus sold Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children: Black Book in 2000 as one of two paired Game Boy Color cartridges, alongside a Red Book with its own path.

meta.name: Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children: Black Book

title: Shamus (1982)
history: William Mataga's maze shooter Shamus (1982), published by Synapse, was an Atari 8-bit favorite about a detective in a robot-filled labyrinth.

title: Batman: Chaos in Gotham
history: DC's hero headlines the 2001 handheld action game Batman: Chaos in Gotham, drawn from the animated-series era of Batman licenses.

title: Suzuki Alstare Extreme Racing
history: The motorcycle team license shows up in Suzuki Alstare Extreme Racing, a 1999 bike racer.

title: Shanghai
history: Activision published Brodie Lockard's Shanghai in 1986, the mahjong-solitaire game about clearing matching tiles from a stacked layout.

title: Dropzone (1984)
history: Archer MacLean's single-screen shooter Dropzone (1984) follows the Defender tradition and became a favorite on 8-bit Atari computers.

title: The Black Onyx
history: Henk Rogers' 1984 computer RPG The Black Onyx is often credited as the commercial role-playing game that opened Japan's home-computer market to the genre.

title: Disney's Atlantis: The Lost Empire
history: Disney's animated film received a 2001 action tie-in in Disney's Atlantis: The Lost Empire.

title: Balloon Kid (1990)
history: Nintendo's Game Boy follow-up to Balloon Fight, Balloon Kid (1990), stars Alice as she stays aloft with the balloons she carries.

title: Nicktoons Racing
history: Several Nickelodeon cartoons share the tracks in Nicktoons Racing, a 1999 kart racer.

title: Magical Drop
history: Data East's 1995 puzzle game Magical Drop has the player catch falling drops and throw them back to clear columns of color.

title: Quest for Camelot
history: Warner Bros.' animated film received a 1998 action tie-in titled Quest for Camelot.

title: Shadowgate Classic
history: ICOM's 1987 MacVenture Shadowgate Classic is the point-and-click castle adventure that later traveled to many home computers and handhelds.

title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (GBC)
history: Griptonite followed its first handheld RPG with Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (GBC) in 2002, again separate from the console action game.

meta.name: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (GBC)

title: Star Ocean: Blue Sphere
history: tri-Ace and Enix released Star Ocean: Blue Sphere only in Japan, in 2001, as a Game Boy Color follow-up set after Star Ocean: The Second Story.

title: The Dukes of Hazzard
history: The Dukes of Hazzard is a video game based on the CBS series about cousins Bo and Luke Duke and their car, the General Lee.

title: Lego Alpha Team (2001)
history: Lego Alpha Team (2001) is the handheld puzzle game starring those agents, and it plays differently from the PC adventure released the year before.

title: Pokémon Gold Version
history: Game Freak's Pokémon Gold Version opened the Johto generation on the Game Boy Color, in Japan in 1999 and in the West in 2000.

title: Xtreme Sports (2000)
history: WayForward packed several extreme-sports events into the Game Boy Color game Xtreme Sports (2000).

title: Pocket Bomberman
history: Hudson's 1997 Pocket Bomberman turns Bomberman into a side-scrolling platformer instead of a maze battle.

title: Oddworld Adventures 2
history: The 2001 handheld follow-up Oddworld Adventures 2 draws on Abe's Exoddus for the Game Boy Color.

title: X-Men: Mutant Wars
history: Marvel's mutants appear in the 2000 side-scrolling action game X-Men: Mutant Wars, a different title from the one-on-one Mutant Academy fighter.

title: X-Men: Wolverine's Rage
history: Wolverine carries the 2001 handheld action game X-Men: Wolverine's Rage, another Marvel license aimed at the Game Boy Color.

title: SpongeBob SquarePants: Legend of the Lost Spatula
history: One of the earliest games from the Nickelodeon cartoon, SpongeBob SquarePants: Legend of the Lost Spatula is a 2001 Game Boy Color platformer.

meta.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: Legend of the Lost Spatula

title: Hamtaro Ham-Hams Unite!
history: The hamster cartoon reached the Game Boy Color in Hamtaro Ham-Hams Unite!, which came west in 2001.

title: Pong: The Next Level
history: Hasbro updated the 1972 paddle game with power-ups in Pong: The Next Level, released in 1999.

title: Game & Watch Gallery 2
history: Nintendo's second Game & Watch collection, Game & Watch Gallery 2, pairs the old LCD modes with redrawn versions starring Mario characters. The color edition arrived in 1998.

title: Legend Of Zelda: Link's Awakening DX
history: The 1998 color update Legend Of Zelda: Link's Awakening DX rebuilds the 1993 Game Boy adventure with color, a photo feature, and an extra Color Dungeon.

meta.name: Legend Of Zelda: Link's Awakening DX

title: Microsoft Pinball Arcade
history: Microsoft's 1998 collection Microsoft Pinball Arcade recreates a set of real pinball tables for play at home.

title: Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children: Red Book
history: The companion cartridge Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children: Red Book shipped in 2000 beside Black Book, the other half of Atlus's paired Devil Children release.

meta.name: Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children: Red Book

title: Conker's Pocket Tales
history: Rare's 1999 Game Boy Color adventure Conker's Pocket Tales stars a gentle Conker, made before the adult humor of Bad Fur Day.

title: Ronaldo V-Football
history: Infogrames' 2000 soccer game Ronaldo V-Football is endorsed by the Brazilian striker Ronaldo, and it is also known as Ronaldo V-Soccer in the United States.

title: Ultimate Fighting Championship
history: The mixed-martial-arts promotion lent its name to Ultimate Fighting Championship, an early licensed fighting game from 2000.

title: Resident Evil Code: Veronica
history: Capcom's 2000 Dreamcast game Resident Evil Code: Veronica follows Claire Redfield and is a mainline entry, even though it sits outside the numbered titles.

title: Army Men RTS
history: The plastic soldiers moved into real-time strategy with Army Men RTS in 2002, commanding Sarge's troops across oversized household battlefields.

title: Disney•Pixar Cars
history: THQ's 2006 racing game Disney•Pixar Cars is the tie-in to the first Pixar film, not to the later Cars sequel.

title: Worms 3D
history: Team17 took the artillery series fully into 3D with Worms 3D in 2003, leaving the familiar side-on battlefield.

title: True Crime: Streets of LA
history: Luxoflux's 2003 open-world game True Crime: Streets of LA stars cop Nick Kang in Los Angeles, with a meter that tracks whether he stays clean.

title: Second Sight
history: Free Radical Design, the TimeSplitters studio, released the psychic action game Second Sight in 2004.

title: True Crime: New York City
history: Luxoflux moved the open-world cop series to Manhattan with True Crime: New York City in 2005, starring Marcus Reed.

title: Tony Hawk's American Wasteland
history: Neversoft set Tony Hawk's American Wasteland in Los Angeles in 2005 and linked its skate areas into one continuous city.

title: Sonic 3D Blast (1996)
history: Traveller's Tales put Sonic in an isometric view for Sonic 3D Blast (1996), a Genesis game that also shipped on the Saturn.

title: Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes
history: Silicon Knights remade the 1998 stealth game as Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes on the GameCube in 2004, with new cutscenes directed by Ryuhei Kitamura.

meta.name: Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes

title: Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex
history: Traveller's Tales' 2001 platformer Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex is the fourth main Crash game and introduces the brute Crunch.

meta.name: Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex

title: Sonic Riders
history: Sonic Team replaced footraces with hoverboard Extreme Gear in Sonic Riders, the 2006 racing game.

title: Shadow the Hedgehog
history: Sega gave the black hedgehog guns and a branching hero-or-villain story in Shadow the Hedgehog, released in 2005.

title: Def Jam: Fight for NY
history: AKI and EA's 2004 hip-hop fighter Def Jam: Fight for NY is the sequel to Def Jam Vendetta, with a roster full of rappers.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures
history: Nintendo's 2004 GameCube game The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures is a multiplayer Zelda that links Game Boy Advance systems for four players.

meta.name: The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures

title: Call of Duty: Finest Hour
history: Spark Unlimited brought the World War II shooter to consoles for the first time with Call of Duty: Finest Hour in 2004.

title: Mortal Kombat: Deception
history: Midway followed Deadly Alliance with Mortal Kombat: Deception in 2004, adding Chess Kombat and a puzzle mode beside the fights.

title: TimeSplitters 2
history: Free Radical's 2002 shooter TimeSplitters 2 is remembered for time-hopping missions, a map maker, and strong multiplayer.

title: X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse
history: Raven Software's squad action RPG X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse, published by Activision in 2005, is the sequel to X-Men Legends.

meta.name: X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse

title: Skies of Arcadia
history: Overworks' 2000 Dreamcast RPG Skies of Arcadia follows air pirates among floating islands, and a later GameCube edition was titled Legends.

title: Tales of Symphonia (2003)
history: Namco's GameCube action RPG Tales of Symphonia (2003) follows Lloyd Irving and uses the series' real-time battles. It was a console exclusive at launch.

title: TimeSplitters: Future Perfect
history: Free Radical closed the trilogy with TimeSplitters: Future Perfect in 2005, adding a four-player campaign and console online play.

title: Resident Evil - Code: Veronica X
history: The expanded edition Resident Evil - Code: Veronica X adds scenes to Code Veronica. It spread widely on PlayStation 2 in 2001 and later reached the GameCube.

title: Sonic Spinball (1993)
history: Sega turned Sonic into a set of flipper tables with Sonic Spinball (1993), a Genesis pinball game built around his speed.

title: Call of Duty 2: Big Red One
history: Treyarch's 2005 console shooter Call of Duty 2: Big Red One follows the U.S. 1st Infantry Division and was not a PC expansion.

meta.name: Call of Duty 2: Big Red One

title: The Hulk
history: Radical Entertainment's 2003 film tie-in The Hulk switches between rampaging as the creature and playing as Banner.

title: Crash Tag Team Racing
history: Radical Entertainment's 2005 Crash Tag Team Racing mixes karts with on-foot platforming, and cars can fuse in the middle of a race.

title: SSX 3
history: EA Canada's 2003 snowboard game SSX 3 puts the series on one connected mountain instead of a menu of separate courses.

title: Mario Party 4
history: Hudson's Mario Party 4, released in 2002, was the first Mario Party on the GameCube and kept the boards-and-minigames format.

title: Star Fox Adventures
history: Rare's 2002 GameCube game Star Fox Adventures began as the separate project Dinosaur Planet before it was recast around Fox McCloud.

title: Viewtiful Joe (2003)
history: Clover Studio and Hideki Kamiya's side-scroller Viewtiful Joe (2003) gives its hero film-style VFX powers on the GameCube.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Melee
history: Konami's 2005 arena brawler Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Melee is a fighting spinoff of the cartoons, not a story platformer.

meta.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Melee

title: Spyro: Enter the Dragonfly
history: After Insomniac left the series, Spyro: Enter the Dragonfly arrived in 2002 under Universal and launched to a notoriously rough reception.

title: Medal of Honor: Rising Sun
history: EA moved Medal of Honor from Europe to the Pacific theater with Medal of Honor: Rising Sun in 2003.

title: Hobbit, The (2003)
history: Sierra's action game based on Tolkien's novel shipped as Hobbit, The (2003), a tie-in era adaptation rather than a later film game.

title: Mario Party 5
history: Hudson stayed on the GameCube for Mario Party 5 in 2003, another board-and-minigame party with a new set of boards.

title: Barnyard
history: Nickelodeon's animated film about a farm of animals received a 2006 tie-in game titled Barnyard.

title: Mario Power Tennis
history: Camelot added charged special shots to the Mario tennis formula in Mario Power Tennis, a 2004 GameCube game.

title: Ice Age 2: The Meltdown
history: The Blue Sky film sequel received a 2006 platform tie-in titled Ice Age 2: The Meltdown.

title: Medal of Honor: European Assault
history: EA returned Medal of Honor to the European theater with Medal of Honor: European Assault in 2005, after the Pacific-set Rising Sun.

title: Dragon Ball Z: Budokai
history: Dimps opened its long line of 3D anime fighters with Dragon Ball Z: Budokai in 2002.

title: Driver San Francisco
history: Ubisoft Reflections built Driver San Francisco in 2011 around Shift, a power that jumps the player from car to car across an open city.

title: Alone in the Dark (2008)
history: Eden Games rebooted the survival-horror series with Alone in the Dark (2008), moving the story to Central Park and splitting the game into episodes.

title: Sonic the Hedgehog 4 - Episode I
history: Dimps and Sonic Team returned to side-view Sonic in 2010 with Sonic the Hedgehog 4 - Episode I, sold as an episodic follow-up to the Genesis games.

title: Metal Slug X
history: SNK's 1999 Metal Slug X revises Metal Slug 2, rebalancing the run-and-gun and easing the slowdown that hurt the earlier board.

title: METAL SLUG
history: Nazca's 1996 Neo Geo run-and-gun METAL SLUG launched the series, with chunky vehicles and a small squad against General Morden's army.

title: SEGA Bass Fishing
history: The 2008 Wii release SEGA Bass Fishing brings Sega's arcade fishing game, originally Get Bass, to motion controls.

title: Call of Duty 3
history: Treyarch's 2006 World War II shooter Call of Duty 3 was built for consoles and did not receive a PC version at launch.

title: La-Mulana
history: Nigoro's ruin explorer La-Mulana homages MSX action adventures. It began as 2005 freeware, and a remake reached more players around 2012.

title: BIT.TRIP BEAT
history: Gaijin Games opened the BIT.TRIP series on WiiWare in 2009 with BIT.TRIP BEAT, a rhythm game in which CommanderVideo bounces a dot to the beat.

title: Destroy All Humans!
history: Pandemic's 2005 Destroy All Humans! casts the alien Crypto as a 1950s invader harvesting human brains.

title: FIFA 10
history: EA Sports shipped the annual soccer game FIFA 10 in 2009, another season in the long-running FIFA series on consoles and PC.

title: Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 2 - The Siege of Spinner Cay
history: Telltale's second episode, Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 2 - The Siege of Spinner Cay, strands Guybrush on the merfolk island of Spinner Cay while the Pox of LeChuck from the 2009 season keeps spreading. It is one WiiWare chapter of that five-part revival, not a LucasArts Monkey Island.

meta.name: Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 2 - The Siege of Spinner Cay

title: Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 3 - Lair of the Leviathan
history: Third of five episodes in Telltale's 2009 season, Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 3 - Lair of the Leviathan keeps Guybrush Threepwood as the pirate lead.

meta.name: Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 3 - Lair of the Leviathan

title: Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 5 - Rise of the Pirate God
history: Telltale closed its five-episode 2009 Monkey Island season with Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 5 - Rise of the Pirate God.

meta.name: Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 5 - Rise of the Pirate God

title: Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 4 - The Trial and Execution of Guybrush Threepwood
history: Fourth in Telltale's 2009 run, Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 4 - The Trial and Execution of Guybrush Threepwood puts the series hero's name on the episode itself.

meta.name: Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 4 - The Trial and Execution of Guybrush Threepwood

title: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
history: Moon Studios followed its hand-painted platformer with Ori and the Will of the Wisps in 2020, again published with Microsoft.

meta.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

title: Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number
history: Dennaton's top-down sequel Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number arrived in 2015, larger and more divisive than the 2012 original.

title: Resident Evil 6
history: Capcom pushed the series toward action in Resident Evil 6 in 2012, splitting the story across campaigns for Leon, Chris, Jake, and Ada.

title: Grim Fandango Remastered
history: Double Fine's 2015 Grim Fandango Remastered updates Tim Schafer's 1998 LucasArts adventure about a travel agent in the Land of the Dead.

title: The Outer Worlds
history: Obsidian's satirical first-person RPG The Outer Worlds, published by Private Division in 2019, is set in the corporately owned Halcyon colony.

title: Broforce
history: Free Lives' run-and-gun Broforce, published by Devolver Digital in 2015, parodies action movies by making each bro a send-up of a film hero.

title: The Walking Dead: Season 2
history: Telltale continued its comic-based adventure with The Walking Dead: Season 2 in 2013, this time with Clementine as the lead.

title: Borderlands 3
history: Gearbox continued the looter-shooter series with Borderlands 3 in 2019, introducing a new group of vault hunters.

title: Syberia 2
history: Benoit Sokal's 2004 adventure Syberia 2 continues Kate Walker's journey with Hans Voralberg, the sequel to the 2002 game.

title: Celeste
history: Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry's 2018 platformer Celeste sends Madeline up a mountain and was praised for its assist options as much as its precision.

title: To the Moon
history: Kan Gao and Freebird Games released To the Moon in 2011, an RPG Maker story about granting a dying man's wish by editing his memories.

title: Frostpunk
history: 11 bit studios' 2018 city builder Frostpunk is about keeping the last settlement alive around a generator in an endless winter.

title: SMITE
history: Hi-Rez's free-to-play battleground SMITE pits gods from world myth against each other in a third-person lane fight, and it left beta for a full release in 2015.

title: Borderlands Game of the Year Enhanced
history: Gearbox's 2009 looter shooter returned as Borderlands Game of the Year Enhanced in 2019, with updated visuals and a handful of gameplay additions.

meta.name: Borderlands Game of the Year Enhanced

title: Batman: Arkham Asylum
history: Rocksteady started the Arkham series with Batman: Arkham Asylum in 2009, a stealth-action game set inside the asylum and written with Paul Dini.

title: Dead by Daylight
history: Behaviour Interactive's 2016 asymmetric horror game Dead by Daylight pits four survivors against one killer.

title: Overcooked
history: Ghost Town Games' co-op kitchen game Overcooked, published by Team17 in 2016, is about cooking under a timer as the kitchen falls apart.

title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl
history: GSC Game World opened its series with S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl in 2007, a first-person survival shooter in the Zone around the Chernobyl plant.

title: Human: Fall Flat
history: No Brakes Games' 2016 physics puzzle Human: Fall Flat stars a wobbly human figure and later became a popular co-op party game.

title: The Long Dark
history: Hinterland's Canadian wilderness survival game The Long Dark entered early access in 2014, with its story mode arriving later.

title: Stray
history: BlueTwelve Studio's 2022 Stray, published by Annapurna Interactive, follows a cat through a sealed city inhabited by robots.

title: Mortal Kombat 11
history: NetherRealm's 2019 fighter Mortal Kombat 11 emphasizes custom move sets and a roster that mixes series regulars with guest characters.

title: Dark Souls: Remastered
history: FromSoftware's 2011 action RPG returned as Dark Souls: Remastered in 2018, including the Artorias of the Abyss content.

title: It Takes Two
history: Hazelight and Josef Fares made the co-op-only platformer It Takes Two in 2021, and it won Game of the Year at The Game Awards.

title: Darksiders II Deathinitive Edition
history: The 2015 enhanced rerelease Darksiders II Deathinitive Edition updates the 2012 sequel, which shifts the horseman lead from War to Death.

title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords
history: Obsidian's 2004 sequel Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords followed BioWare's RPG and is famous for a rushed launch later patched by fans.

meta.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords

title: Beholder
history: Warm Lamp Games' 2016 Beholder makes you a landlord in a totalitarian state, ordered to spy on the tenants of your building.

title: Prison Architect
history: Introversion's prison-management sim Prison Architect reached a full 1.0 release in 2015 after a long public alpha.

title: Resident Evil 2
history: Capcom's 2019 Resident Evil 2 is the over-the-shoulder remake of the 1998 survival-horror game, again following Leon and Claire.

title: Jotun: Valhalla Edition
history: Thunder Lotus Games' hand-painted boss battles against Norse giants were packaged as Jotun: Valhalla Edition, the complete form of the 2015 game.

title: Trine Enchanted Edition
history: Trine Enchanted Edition refreshes Frozenbyte's 2009 puzzle platformer, in which a thief, a wizard, and a knight combine their skills.

title: Enter the Gungeon
history: Dodge Roll's bullet-hell roguelike Enter the Gungeon, published by Devolver Digital in 2016, is set in a dungeon full of guns.

title: Resident Evil Revelations 2
history: Capcom released Resident Evil Revelations 2 in episodes in 2015, pairing Claire Redfield with Barry Burton.

title: Resident Evil 3
history: Capcom's 2020 Resident Evil 3 reimagines the 1999 Nemesis story with Jill Valentine, as a shorter companion to the second game's remake.

title: Fortnite Battle Royale
history: Epic Games launched the free 100-player mode Fortnite Battle Royale in 2017, and it quickly overshadowed the original Save the World campaign.

title: Mark of the Ninja
history: Klei's 2012 side-view stealth game Mark of the Ninja shows sound and light so the player can plan each takedown.

title: Bomberman Quest
history:
Hudson Soft took White Bomberman off the single-screen bomb grid and sent him walking across a world map in Bomberman Quest, a 1998 Game Boy Color journey. Monsters occupy pockets of land, and the bombs he finds do not share one blast. A fight is decided by which effect he brought, whether the charge homes, punches, or sits in place until the fuse ends.

Encounters stay small enough to read on the handheld screen. The creature closes distance while the timer runs, and a poorly chosen bomb wastes the only shot that would have reached it. New bombs turn up along the roads, so later fields assume a kit the opening hills never offered.

Towns break the hiking, and a sealed path often waits until the matching bomb is clipped to his pack. Hudson Soft keeps the round face and the bright danger, while the job is to finish the route rather than to outlast a rival bomber.

Maze cartridges live on soft blocks, shrinking arenas, and a last survivor. Progress on this quest is the ground already crossed, the creatures already beaten, and the strange bombs hanging from his belt.

title: Warlocked
history:
Queen Azarel's humans and Chief Zog's beasts divide Warlocked into two campaigns of real-time war on the Game Boy Color. Bits Studios built the battles, Nintendo published the cartridge in North America in 2000, and units are summoned only by spending resources pulled off the map. A full menu of troop names means nothing when the stockpile is empty.

Fog covers the enemy until a scout walks close enough to see them. Workers haul the resource home, the commander anchors the camp, and fresh bodies appear beside the buildings after the cost is paid. Spend too early and the next wave cannot be called; hesitate and the other faction is already at the wall.

Humans bring archers and knights, beasts bring heavier brutes, and each army has wizards who can afflict the soldiers across the field. Orders shift from holding a point to razing the far camp, and no turn marker ever freezes the field.

Strategy this direct was scarce beside the platformers on that handheld's shelf. The live argument is the resource number against the headcount already deployed. Lose the gathering and the summon list is only a set of names with no one left to answer them.

title: Bionic Commando: Elite Forces
history:
These soldiers cannot jump, so the claw is the only way up in Bionic Commando: Elite Forces. Nintendo Software Technology built the Game Boy Color adventure, and Nintendo published it in 1999. A male commando and a female commando each walk a slightly different route, with starting guns the other does not carry.

Latch the arm overhead, swing, and let go to cross a shaft. Some rooms open a sniper view for a distant shot, a beat the pure swinging games never asked for. Commander Joe has been taken by the Avar forces, and the mission is to bring him back.

The female commando begins with a lighter weapon and a quieter approach, while the male commando opens with heavier fire and a more direct push. Both still fall if the claw misses, because nothing in the move list replaces that grab. Nintendo Software Technology shapes a long run of vertical rooms around that single limitation.

The NES Bionic Commando tells a different war with a different mission list. Here the paired leads, the sniper moments, and the rescue of Joe are the campaign Nintendo actually shipped on the Color handheld.

title: Legend of the River King 2
history:
Yuki's Heaven Jewel has been stolen, and fishing it back is the errand inside Legend of the River King 2. Natsume and Victor Interactive brought the Game Boy Color sequel out in 1999. Two brothers can lead, rods improve when the current tackle cannot hold a strike, and a catch book records every species that actually reaches shore.

The Mountain God and the Sea God took the jewel's halves and turned themselves into giant fish, the River King and the Sea King. Smaller catches feed the trip, pay for better gear, and earn the right to fish the next bank. People along the road trade favors for bugs, flowers, and odd jobs, but the line in the water is still the tool the plot requires.

A timed pier contest would weigh one fish and send the angler home. This journey keeps walking, selling, and rebaiting until those divine fish are landed for Yuki. Victor Interactive's structure and Natsume's release leave the jewel, not a ticket total, as the reason to cast.

Lead with the younger brother and one god-fish comes first; lead with the older and the Sea King and River King duties trade places. Either route still lives in the book, the upgraded rod, and the help Yuki asked for. The day is done when the jewel is whole.

title: Dragon Warrior Monsters 2
history:
Cobi's Journey and Tara's Adventure are the two United States releases of Dragon Warrior Monsters 2, both built by Tose for Enix. Breeding is the daily work: pair two monsters and the child keeps a mix of their skills. In 2001 the adventure moved from island to island, and the boat between shores is how new families enter the matching pool.

A handsome monster with an empty move list still loses, so a pairing is judged by what the offspring can actually do. The two cartridges are not one plot with the cover art swapped; each lead meets the chain of islands from another side. Tose spends the hours on feeding, scouting, and combining rather than on a single dungeon march.

Enix kept the American boxes in the Dragon Warrior line while the raising did the talking. Skip an island and you may miss a family the team has never produced. The next battle is the audit of whatever traits you chose to pass down.

The earlier breeding quest in this series woke inside a monster kingdom and stayed there. These stories leave that kingdom for open water and two separate leads. The goal is still a child stronger than either parent, only now the horizon is a shoreline.

title: Mickey's Racing Adventure
history:
Rare parked a garage between Mickey and the checkered flag in Mickey's Racing Adventure. Nintendo and Disney share the 1999 Game Boy Color release with Rare, and the kart improves because a hub of minigames pays out parts. An engine or a set of tires from those errands changes the launch, so a bare chassis is not the car you want on the grid.

One side challenge may be a short chase, another a timing test, always inside a Disney setting and always with hardware as the prize. Bolt the part on, then line up against the rest of the cast. Minnie, Donald, Daisy, Goofy, and the others take their own cars, which keeps every rival inside that stable.

Ignore the hub and the kart stays slow, because Rare tied speed to the errand before the event. The circuit repeats as a side challenge, a new piece of the car, then a race. The scenery changes, and the reason to enter it is whichever part is still missing.

Mario's kart games seat a different cast for a different purpose. This adventure earns its pace in minigames, then spends it on Disney drivers and Rare's own feel for a handheld race.

title: Ninja Gaiden Shadow
history:
What began as a Shadow of the Ninja design reached the Game Boy in 1991 as Ninja Gaiden Shadow, released by Tecmo with Natsume sharing the development. Ryu takes the sword onto side-view stages crowded with soldiers. The swing is short, the screen is narrow, and a long windup does not fit.

Standing close enough to connect is the real spacing problem, and a thrown blade covers the fighter who refuses to approach. Natsume's side-on stance still shows in his posture even though the name on the box, and the man holding the steel, belong to the Gaiden line. A thin health bar makes a sloppy room expensive.

The Shadow of the Ninja direction supplied the original plan, and Tecmo's choice was to ship Ryu under the Ninja Gaiden name. The cartridge you hold is that finished chapter: corridors, a blade, and groups of enemies who drop once the edge lands. Little happens between those rooms except the next group.

NES chapters in the same series stop for cinema scenes between acts. This one stays inside the side-view fighting, with Ryu already drawn and the corridor already full.

title: Solar Striker
history:
Nintendo R&D1 and Minakuchi Engineering aimed a small ship up the glass and named the vertical shooter Solar Striker. Nintendo published it in 1990, and shooters carrying that publishing credit were rare on the Game Boy. Icons scooped up during the climb rewrite the shot leaving the nose.

A plain pellet can open into a spread or tighten into a heavier beam, and dropping the power returns the weak stream at the worst moment. Bosses already occupy the top edge when that happens. The view never turns sideways: threats fall from above while the craft stays low.

Minakuchi Engineering keeps the formations legible on the tiny display. Nintendo R&D1's hand in the project, together with Nintendo's name on the box, makes this an official first-party shooter on a machine that seldom received one. Hold the powered gun through the pattern and meet whatever caps the climb.

There is no town and no horizontal trek between waves. The cartridge is the ascent, the changing nose gun, and the large silhouettes waiting at the end of each stretch of sky.

title: Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru
history:
Prince of Sablé leaves on a rescue and spends much of Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru in the body of a frog. Nintendo and Intelligent Systems released the Game Boy cartridge in Japan in 1992. English-speaking players took to calling it For the Frog the Bell Tolls. The team that made it later made Link's Awakening.

The frog shape is a way through the land, not only a curse to cure. It reaches gaps and landings the prince cannot manage on two legs, so the transformation opens the map. People in the towns still address him as royalty on an errand, even while he travels low to the ground. Fights stay close and brief beside that exploration.

Nintendo published the script in Japanese and never issued an English edition. The cartridge remains an official Nintendo release, sold in Japan through ordinary channels. Readers abroad coined the bell-and-frog nickname from the meaning of the title, and that nickname does not push the product off to the side.

Intelligent Systems and Nintendo folded the prince, the changed body, and a compact set of towns into one quest. Link's Awakening, from that same team afterward, shares the taste for a small world with an unusual condition at its center. The earlier game is the one where the useful body is the frog.

meta.name: Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru

title: Game & Watch Gallery
history:
Manhole, Fire, Octopus, and Oil Panic share Game & Watch Gallery, the collection Nintendo published in 1997. Each chore can be played with the old LCD stick figures or in a redrawn mode that hands the same clock to Mario series characters. The idea of the cartridge is that double life, not a brand-new sport.

Classic mode keeps the sparse shapes and the original split-second demands: cover the holes, catch the people leaping from the flames, slip past tentacles while lifting treasure, catch dripping oil before it ruins the floor. The redrawn mode puts Mario and the cast around him into those jobs, and some of the falling bodies even move at different speeds. Miss the beat and the penalty arrives either way.

This set lives on the original Game Boy and stops after those four. Later collections numbered 2 and 3 add other LCD toys and longer menus. Their extra titles are separate cartridges, not secret pages in this one.

Scores can be stored, yet the play is still the old reflex test in both costumes. Nintendo's publishing is what pairs the LCD look with the Mario look on a single Game Boy release. Oil, tentacles, open holes, and a burning building remain the four emergencies on offer.

title: Mega Man V (1994)
history:
Stardroids, alien robots rather than the familiar robot masters, are the bosses to clear in Mega Man V (1994). Capcom published the Game Boy cartridge and Minakuchi Engineering developed it, the last classic-style Mega Man on that handheld. Terra leads the invasion, and the Mega Arm throws a returning fist in place of the ordinary buster charge.

Defeat a Stardroid and its weapon joins the menu, preserving the habit of hunting the tool that hurts the next foe. Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto hold stretches of the planet, chosen from a select screen. A later upgrade lets the flying fist grab and pummel, which matters when a normal shot skids off alien armor.

Sunstar, a doomsday machine, waits after those planet bosses, and Doctor Wily cannot keep control of it. Tango the robotic cat comes along as a new helper while the Stardroids occupy the cities. Minakuchi Engineering drew original routes for this roster instead of replaying NES robot-master stages.

The classic Game Boy formula closes on an extraterrestrial lineup and a throwing arm. Later handheld Mega Man stories leave this select-a-boss structure for other kinds of play. Here you still pick a target, cross the stage, and leave with the weapon.

title: Operation C
history:
Konami sent a Contra commando onto the Game Boy in 1991 and named the American cartridge Operation C. Europe sold that same game as Probotector, continuing the regional habit of presenting the lead as a robot. Side-view runs alternate with overhead rooms where the gun can point in several directions, and the spread shot is the pickup that clears a crowd.

A sideways corridor is the familiar dash, jump, and stream of fire. An overhead floor turns the soldier into a figure seen from above, threading lanes of bullets across open ground. Aliens and the widening gun keep the feel inside the Contra series, while the stage order belongs to this handheld cartridge alone.

Players in Japan meet it under the Contra title. All three names are official Konami releases of one compact campaign. The European robot presentation changes the body on the box more than it changes the act of shooting through a mixed set of views.

The NES Contra is a longer, separate mission list. Nothing here reprints that run onto a small screen. You take the commando through both camera angles, chase the spread shot, and finish the route Konami laid out for the handheld.

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III: Radical Rescue
history:
Michelangelo is the only brother still loose when Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III: Radical Rescue begins, and Konami built the 1993 Game Boy game around freeing the rest. Leonardo, Raphael, and Donatello become playable as he reaches them, each with a way through the fortress the others lack. The map pushes backward as often as forward, because a newly freed turtle opens a passage already walked past.

Spinning nunchaku let Michelangelo hang over gaps and spikes. Leonardo drills cracked floors with his swords, Raphael withdraws into his shell to fit tight tunnels, and Donatello climbs walls toward exits that were out of reach. Swapping among them is how a locked corridor becomes a route.

Shredder's Foot hold Splinter and April as well as the brothers. Soldiers fill the space between keys and cells, and the fighting itself stays direct so the puzzle can be which body crosses the next obstacle. Konami expects the select screen of rescued turtles to matter more than a longer combo.

This is not the NES tournament fighter, where the brothers duel one another, and it is not Turtles in Time. The Game Boy chapter is a rescue with backtracking and a fortress that opens only in a certain order. Four abilities, not four identical fighters, are what make the rooms solvable.

meta.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III: Radical Rescue

title: Mole Mania (1996)
history:
Muddy Mole shoves dirt and sets bombs because his family is trapped underground in Mole Mania (1996). Pax Softnica constructed the puzzles, Shigeru Miyamoto produced them, and Nintendo published the Game Boy cartridge. A room is a small diagram: drop a dirt block into a pit, crack a wall with a bomb, or dig down to the layer beneath.

A block that falls into a hole becomes floor and stays there. Detonate in the wrong cell and you erase the very step he needed. Farmer Jinbe is the one who took the family, so every clever shove aims at reaching them.

Surface trails and buried chambers stack on top of each other, and a dig swaps Muddy Mole between those layers. Miyamoto's production keeps the verbs tiny: push, place, explode, drop. Pax Softnica chains those verbs into rooms that punish a hurried shove with a worse layout than the one you started with.

He is not sprinting a cartoon field for points. The family is the destination, and the dirt is both the barrier and the material that builds a path. Nintendo's cartridge measures progress by how much closer that reunion has become.

title: Avenging Spirit (1991)
history:
You play a murdered man's ghost in Avenging Spirit (1991), and the only durable skin is a body that still belongs to someone else. Jaleco made the arcade original, and the Game Boy version is by C.P. Brain. Gangsters killed him and kidnapped his girlfriend, so the spirit overlaps an enemy and inherits that enemy's jump and weapon.

Step out of the host and a spirit meter drains until another body is caught. A gunner, a high jumper, and a slow bruiser answer different hallways, and a slain host throws the ghost back into open air. Restorative pickups sit in the stages, which means you want to be wearing someone when you reach them.

City streets, rooftops, a factory, and the syndicate's base make up the route. Finding the right keys changes whether the girlfriend can be reached before the finish; miss them and the ending plays without her. The handheld version keeps the possession, softens some of the cabinet's harsher timing, and remains an official Jaleco release.

The body currently worn is the entire move set. No permanent upgrade retires that choice, because the next corridor may want a different host. Both the arcade premise and the Game Boy stages are built on the swap.

title: Sword of Mana
history:
Brownie Brown retold the first Mana quest as Sword of Mana, Square Enix released that Game Boy Advance version in 2003, and Nintendo published it outside Japan. Choosing the hero or the heroine changes the story scenes that follow. Ring spirits, worn as equipped magic, sit beside sword swings that happen in real time.

The root is Final Fantasy Adventure, called Seiken Densetsu in Japan, not the sixteen-bit Secret of Mana with its party on the Super Nintendo. Towns, partners, and the ring menu enlarge a journey the old Game Boy game only sketched. A spirit ring swaps the magic in hand, and the blade still has to reach the body in front of you.

Her playthrough is not his script with a different portrait. Who stands at the center of a conversation shifts, so a second trip tells another version of the same crisis. Brownie Brown stages the fights as action: step in, swing, and spend the ring instead of freezing the field for a command menu.

Square Enix handled the Japanese side of an official retelling, while Nintendo carried the release abroad. Secret of Mana remains the other branch of the series. This cartridge returns to the earlier pair of leads and lets you decide which of them you follow.

title: Parodius Da!
history:
Konami's comic answer to Gradius, born in 1990, reached the Game Boy as Parodius Da! A penguin and an octopus can pilot, and the power-ups are jokes that still rewrite the shot. Side-scrolling dodges and a weapon meter survive from the serious shooter, then every option gets dressed as a gag.

Bells push the arsenal forward the way a military game would, except the things flying in formation beside you may honk or flap. Enemy waves still punish a lazy line. The comedy lives in the sprites and the noises, not in a rule that deletes the bullets.

This official handheld edition, published by Konami, is the parody itself rather than a sober Gradius campaign in a costume. Stages scroll through punchlines built from the parent series' imagery. Dying strips the ridiculous weapons away, and that loss still hurts.

Anyone hunting a straight-faced space fighter will not find its tone here. The penguin, the octopus, and the absurd upgrades are both the cast and the kit. Konami asks for the familiar weave through fire, only everyone on screen seems to know the war is a joke.

title: Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire (2003)
history:
Jupiter laid out two boards, Ruby and Sapphire, for Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire (2003), and Nintendo published the cartridge. Hit a Pokémon on the playfield to weaken it, then catch it with the ball, and keep playing if you want that catch to evolve. A rumble motor buried in the shell shakes the Game Boy Advance on the hits that matter.

The two tables do not share a layout. Ramps, sinkholes, and the spots where a wild Pokémon appears are arranged differently, so mastering one board leaves the other unsolved. Evolution gives a reason to protect a catch instead of treating every bumper as a pure score.

An earlier Pokémon pinball game used other tables and another roster. This pair is the Ruby board beside the Sapphire board, with the shaking hardware in the plastic. Jupiter's rules still depend on flippers: aim, strike, and live with the bounce you actually got.

Nintendo's single official cartridge holds both tables. The collection grows because the catch happens on the playfield, not in a quiet menu. Miss the flipper and the evolution you were building rolls away down the drain.

title: Puyo Puyo
history:
Pairs of colored blobs fall, and Compile's Game Boy puzzle Puyo Puyo pops them only when four of one color connect. The 1991 cartridge is the handheld edition of that first puzzle, and a chain dumps garbage onto the opposing stack. Rotate the pair, nest it, and a linked group vanishes, which can tug the blobs above into another group.

An opponent drawn from Compile's fantasy cast answers with junk of their own. A long chain is how you bury them; a sloppy tower is how you bury yourself. There is no gun and no platforming, only the next pair and the rising ceiling.

The numbered follow-up Compile released later is a different cartridge. This edition stays with the original four-blob rule and with an enemy who will not pause while you tidy the well. Compile's official handheld duel is blob against blob, chain against chain.

A pretty pattern still fails if the fourth blob never touches its color. Garbage arrives as rubble you have to build around. The win is a cascade the other side cannot answer before their pile hits the lid.

title: Mario Tennis: Power Tour
history:
Camelot enrolled a student you create at a tennis academy and named the Game Boy Advance story Mario Tennis: Power Tour. Nintendo published it in 2005. Matches and training build that player, then a circuit of tournaments changes the bounce underfoot.

Clay holds and slows the ball, grass skids, and a hard court sends it back quickly. A weak serve becomes dangerous only after the academy has raised the stat behind it. A partner joins for doubles, so the trip is not a line of solo exhibitions against Mario's friends.

The Game Boy Color tennis game is another cartridge with its own story. This academy, this made-to-order athlete, and these traveling events belong to the Advance campaign Camelot wrote. Ignoring the surface is a good way to lose a point you thought you had read.

In Japan the same story carried a different official title, Mario Tennis Advance. Mario and the familiar roster still appear around the tour, yet the rallies that grow your student are the campaign. Court by court, the custom player is the person the story is actually about.

title: Mega Man Zero 2
history:
Elpizo breaks from the Resistance with a splinter faction in Mega Man Zero 2. Inti Creates developed the Game Boy Advance sequel and Capcom published it in 2003, sending Zero after that rebellion. Forms earned by the way he fights rewrite his moves, and cyber-elves can still be raised and then spent.

One form may stretch a saber string, another changes the dash or leans on an element, so a boss you barely survived becomes a different duel after the body shifts.
